title: Foundation: audit actual backend calls separately from replay fixture keys
body:
Refs #80

## What this is

Adds an optional `AuditedBackend` wrapper (`src/jev_cookbook/accounting.py`) that counts the `decide()` calls a notebook actually makes separately from the distinct replay-fixture keys those calls resolve to, and rewrites the recipe guard's README-budget check to use it. Nothing existing changes unless a notebook opts in: no backend, recipe, fixture or notebook is modified.

Why: a recipe that decides the same state more than once (repeats, retries, comparison arms) makes more calls than the replay file has entries. The old guard compared a README's stated call count to `len(responses.json)`, which is the distinct-key count, so it could pass while the notebook made a different number of real calls (recipe 36's earlier measurement: 290 calls against 72 distinct states).

- `decide_calls`: how many times `decide()` was invoked (a call that raises counts, with `returned: false`).
- `distinct_requests`: how many unique replay keys those calls had; this is the number a fixture file can match.
- The ledger carries only the replay key and a `returned` flag: no responses, contents, credentials or timing. A request that fails replay-key validation never reaches the backend and is not counted.
- This counts logical `decide()` calls, not HTTP attempts; it is separate from the live backend's `requests_made`.
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`: the README-budget check now requires, for an audited notebook, "makes exactly N calls" to equal `decide_calls` and the distinct keys to equal the keys in `responses.json` exactly; an unaudited recipe keeps the old `len(responses.json)` check, and a malformed audit fails rather than falling back to it.
- Docs: `docs/backends.md`, `docs/live.md`.

## Verification

The change is one commit (originally `9b9f73b`, cherry-picked onto `main` f00f56b2 with one docstring-only conflict resolved: the commit's rewritten bullet and `main`'s `noul_proposition_gold_coverage` bullet both kept). 8 files, +782/-50, no recipe folder touched.

- Bare `pytest` 4919 passed / 46 skipped / 50 deselected / 31 xfailed on 3.10 (no SDK) and on 3.14; `tests/test_live_sdk.py` 62 passed with the SDK mocked; ruff, hygiene (569 files), `render_catalog --check`, `notebook_ci.py fixtures`, `fixtures validate --all` clean.
- All 50 published notebooks and the template re-executed offline on 3.14: every one byte-identical to its committed file (no recipe uses `AuditedBackend` yet, so no printed count moves).

title: Foundation: image inputs and the Box primitive across backends, with local vision helpers
body:
Refs #80

## What this is

The shared-code foundation for the multimodal recipes (61 to 100, catalogued in #296): image inputs and the `Box` primitive across the decision backends, plus the local vision helpers. It adds no recipe, no notebook and no fixture of its own.

- `src/jev_cookbook/vision.py` (new, Pillow-based, imported only when used): image validation, content hashing, crops and coordinate transforms for tiled views, and evaluation helpers for boxes. Pillow is a new dependency.
- Backends, answers, questions, live recorder, style, fixture schema: a `Box` question and answer type, image assets attached to a state, replay keys that include an image's content hash, and live requests that send the experimental images header only when a state carries images. The replay key of a text-only request is unchanged (the `assets` entry is added to the hashed payload only when images are present), so every published recipe's fixtures keep replaying.
- `typesafe-sdk` stays an optional extra, now `>=0.7.5,<0.8`, and is not imported at module import time; the SDK is mocked in tests, so no test calls the API.
- Synthetic runs do not report invented API timing or cost (offline backends leave latency and cost unset).
- A hygiene fix: image content hashes are written with a delimiter so the secret scanner's rules stay unchanged (a regression test covers the format).
- Docs: `docs/vision.md` (new), plus image and `Box` sections in `docs/backends.md`, `docs/fixtures.md`, `docs/live.md`; image input fields are kept separate from gold labels.

Not in this change: request accounting for repeated calls (a follow-up, one commit), the catalog and tooling for ranks 61 to 100 (#296), and any recipe.

## Integration and verification

Cut from `main` b4e39ce; carries a signed merge of `main` 475d2195 (one conflict, `README.md`, taken from `main`; the overlapping catalog/tooling/docs files equal `main` byte for byte) and a formatting-only commit for the pinned ruff.

- Diff against `main`: 17 files, no catalog, tooling or README file.
- Bare `pytest` 4852 passed / 46 skipped / 50 deselected / 31 xfailed on 3.10 (no SDK installed) and on 3.14; ruff, hygiene (565 files), `notebook_ci.py fixtures` and `fixtures validate --all` clean; `catalog_audit` shows only the seven pre-existing inbound-link failures.
- All 50 published notebooks re-executed offline on 3.14 and match their committed outputs; `import jev_cookbook` loads neither `typesafe` nor Pillow.

title: Foundation: extend the catalog and tooling to 100 recipes for the multimodal track
body:
Refs #80

## What this is

Extends the catalog and the README from 60 to 100 recipes so the repository can describe the multimodal (vision, `Box` localization, multi-frame, long-context) track proposed for recipes 61 to 100. It adds the 40 new catalog entries and lets the shared tooling accept them. It adds no recipe, no notebook, no fixture and no image support code (those come in separate foundation and recipe pull requests).

- `catalog/recipes.json`: 100 entries (the original 60 are byte-for-byte unchanged in content; a test hashes them), four new source records S09 to S12 (reviewed 15 October 2026, after the Jev 1.14 release), 15 categories.
- `README.md`: regenerated by `tools/render_catalog.py` (never hand-edited). The table has 100 rows; 50 published rows link to notebooks and the rest say coming soon. New rows have no issue link because recipe ranks are not issue numbers: recipes 61 to 100 start with `issue: null` until a real issue is assigned.
- `tools/render_catalog.py`, `tools/check_recipe_scope.py`, `tools/new_recipe.py`, `tools/notebook_ci.py`: accept ranks up to 100. The scope check now reads assigned issue numbers from the trusted base catalog instead of assuming recipe N is issue N for N in 1 to 60, and stays fail-closed: unknown slug, unassigned issue, branch and closed-issue mismatch, a head-only assignment, only one of the two markers, or more than one closed issue are all rejected. The README-equals-render(base README, head catalog) rule and the path/mode allowlist are unchanged.
- Docs, `CONTRIBUTING.md` (issue-assignment wording only), the pull request template checklist, and the banner/getting-started guide are updated to match.

## Consequence worth reading before merge

A recipe pull request for a recipe 61 to 100 cannot pass `Scope (recipe pull requests)` until a real recipe issue has been created and its number recorded in the base catalog. That is intended: it keeps the closed-issue rule meaningful. It means issues need to be opened for 61 to 100 (by the owner) before any of those recipes can merge.

## Integration and verification

The branch was cut from `main` b4e39ce and carries a signed merge of `main` 9ef24c91 (one conflict, `README.md`, resolved by taking `main`'s and re-running the renderer; the badge now reads 50 of 100 published).

- Bare `pytest`: 4638 passed / 46 skipped / 50 deselected / 31 xfailed on 3.10 and on 3.14.
- ruff check and format, hygiene (561 files), `render_catalog.py --check`, `notebook_ci.py fixtures` (51 folders, 0 failed), `fixtures validate --all`: clean.
- `pytest -m catalog_audit` on 3.14: the same seven pre-existing inbound-link failures as `main` (recipes 42, 44, 46 to 50); nothing new.
- Scope: no recipe folder is touched.

title: Sweep: glossary-link coverage and risk in recipe 45
body:
Refs #163

## What this is

One corrective prose item from `SWEEP_163.md`: recipe 45 used two glossary lexicon terms in prose without
linking them. Both are now linked at their only prose occurrence each, in the recipe's own established form.

* `evaluation-note-md`: "The selective view's risk above is non-zero" →
  `[risk](../../docs/glossary.md#risk)`
* `next-md`: "Try raising the coverage floor" → `[coverage](../../docs/glossary.md#coverage)`

`docs/glossary.md` carries `## coverage` (line 193) and `## risk` (line 205), so both anchors resolve; a
bogus-anchor control over the same file returns nothing. The form matches the 20-odd other published
notebooks that link these two anchors, and recipe 45's own five existing glossary links.

## Scope

One file, 2+/2−: `recipes/45-memory-reconciliation/notebook.ipynb`. Scope diff over
`src tests tools docs .github CONTRIBUTING.md pyproject.toml` is **0 files**; can-fail control over the
identical path list (`a994608...origin/main`) returns **4 files**.

## Verification

* **Markdown only.** Cell ids, cell order, outputs, execution counts and per-cell metadata are byte-identical
  to the base; exactly two markdown cell sources moved. The numeric-token multiset over added and removed
  lines is equal (`{'04': 1, '0.90': 1, '0.75': 1}` each side), so no quantity moved.
* **Freshness, with a can-move proof.** A fresh offline execution reproduces the committed file byte for byte
  (`99a721de` both sides). Paired against the "byte-identical is also the signature of a notebook that never
  ran" hazard: planting `0.9375` → `0.9376` in a stored output moved the blob to `cb344ac5`,
  `check_notebook_fresh.py` failed at rc=1 naming `cells[19].outputs[0].text[1]`, and re-execution restored
  `99a721de` exactly.
* **Output does not change**, so this is not a both-interpreters output round — no cell id changed and no new

* **Tests on both interpreters**: `4387 passed, 6 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed` on 3.14.7 and on

  Both venvs verified to resolve `import jev_cookbook` into this worktree's `src/`. Those counts evidence that
  the round broke nothing; the positive evidence for the work is the grep at two refs.
* ruff check, ruff format --check (378 files), whole-tree hygiene (549 files): clean.
* Guard blob `40c1ffe3` at merge-base / `origin/main` / HEAD — three rows, **two distinct commits**, since
  `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` is `origin/main`. Neither divergence case applies.

## Deliberately not in this PR

* **Recipe 45's B-then-A mutual-supersession history print** — the other half of the same backlog bullet. It
  is additive (a new print block, a new claim surface), and recipe 45's additive item is what cost the

* **Recipe 44 is untouched.** Its four backlog items were verified against the tree before this round and all

title: Foundation: state Noul fixture requirements where issue authors and builders meet them
body:
Refs #283

Not all of #283's acceptance criteria are met by this branch alone -- see "Acceptance criteria" below. The PR body therefore says `Refs #283`, not `Closes #283`.

## What this adds

Recipe 48's review (feeding into #281) measured that a multi-proposition `Noul` issue can reach a builder with no requirement for a positive example of every proposition, no truth-combination coverage, and no row where a proposition's own tag changes the composed outcome -- because that requirement lived only in an orchestration brief, never in a file a repository reader can open. This closes that gap in the two places people actually read:

1. **`docs/recipe-template.md`**, at the existing `Noul` contract bullet -- the builder-facing document. States the three fixture-set requirements for a multi-proposition `Noul` recipe, with the reason each matters, in the document's own voice.
2. **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe.yml`**, the issue-author-facing form -- one added sentence in the existing "Fixtures and evaluation" field's description, prompting for the same three things when an issue proposes more than one `Noul` proposition together.
3. **`tests/test_recipe_guard.py`**, a new guard check, `noul_proposition_gold_coverage`: for every `Noul` proposition that zero-argument discovery reaches in a recipe's own code (discovered by calling the recipe's zero-argument question-building functions and keeping the `Noul`-valued entries of whatever dict each returns -- never by name or spelling), `labels.jsonl` must carry a gold-true row and a gold-false row for that proposition in every scored split. This is the mechanical half of #283's three requirements (the gold-coverage one); the truth-combination and outcome-determining requirements are not mechanically checked here -- see "Guard decision" below for why.

## Decisions

- **Scope of the guard.** #283 names three requirements; only the first ("at least one gold-true and one gold-false row per proposition per scored split") is stated as a candidate for a mechanical check in the issue itself. I implemented that one and investigated the other two (see "Guard decision"). I did not force the combination or outcome-determining properties into a guard that would have to key on something other than the real question definitions.
- **Discovery is by calling code, not by name.** `_noul_propositions` (tests/test_recipe_guard.py) calls every zero-required-argument function `helpers.py` defines (not one it imports) and keeps the `Noul`-valued entries of any dict it returns. This is the seventh time this repository has had to choose between an idiom-keyed check and a property-keyed one (#222, #227, #234, #270, #272, #276, #282 are the first six); I chose property-keyed. Measured: 51 such calls across 49 published recipes plus the template, 0 files opened, 0 output, 0 exceptions; the calls themselves take about 0.02s and the whole discovery sweep including module loads about 0.2s. Most calls are question builders, but not all: the docstring names the nine others that get called (e.g. recipe 36's `enumerate_game_space`). A recipe whose question builder takes an argument (recipe 39's `build_stage2_questions(which)`) is not reached and is skipped with a reason saying so.
- **Gold-value reading handles three shapes, not one.** Published multi-proposition `Noul` recipes record gold three different ways: a flat `{prop: bool}` mapping (26, 41, 42, 44, 48), one level of nesting (`{"features": {prop: bool}}`, recipe 35), and set-valued gold -- a list of the true proposition names (06, 37). `_noul_gold_value` reads all three. A fourth shape exists in the published set -- a bare `true`/`false` with no proposition key at all (recipes 02, 10, 15) -- but it occurs only when a recipe has exactly one `Noul` proposition, which this check does not apply to (see next point), so it is deliberately not read.
- **The check is scoped to two-or-more propositions, by skip, not by vacuous pass.** #283 is about the battery case. A recipe with 0 or 1 `Noul` proposition is `pytest.skip`-ed with a reason naming the count found, not silently passed.
- **No `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` entry was needed.** All ten published multi-proposition `Noul` recipes the check reaches (06, 25, 26, 31, 35, 37, 41, 42, 44, 48) already satisfy the gold-coverage property -- recipe 48 had already fixed the first of the three defects #283 measured on it (`breaks_reference` now has gold-true rows in `validation` and `test`) but not the third: no row in any split has both propositions true. This check implements only the per-proposition requirement, which 48 meets, so it needed no allowlist entry; truth-combination coverage is deferred (scored-split combination coverage: 48: 3/4, 44: 11/16, 06: 13/32, 35: 14/64). Ten recipes (06, 25, 26, 31, 35, 37, 41, 42, 44, 48) are covered; an eleventh, 39, builds two propositions but is not reached by zero-argument discovery.

## Guard decision (full ruling)

**Gold-true/gold-false coverage per proposition per scored split: implemented**, with mutation proof (see "How it was verified").

**Truth-combination coverage and outcome-determining rows: deferred, not implemented**, and here is the reasoning and the cost, so this can be sequenced separately rather than guessed at:

- *Truth-combination coverage* ("at least one row for every combination the use case admits") requires knowing which combinations a given recipe's use case actually admits -- that is a judgment about the recipe's own domain (does "both true" even make sense for these two propositions?), not a fact `labels.jsonl` or the question definitions can state by themselves. A mechanical check could verify "all 2^n combinations of n propositions are present among the gold rows", but that is a stricter and different claim than "every combination the use case admits" -- it would force every recipe into full factorial coverage even where a combination is nonsensical for the task, which is exactly the kind of one-shape-fits-all guard this repository's house rules (#273's ruling, and the threshold-objective-pin check's own history) warn against adopting without evidence that the shape fits every case.
- *Outcome-determining rows* ("at least one row where each proposition's own tag changes the composed outcome") requires running the recipe's own composition function -- the `decide`-style function that turns the propositions' tags into a final action -- over the committed fixtures with each proposition flipped, and comparing outcomes. That function is not named consistently across recipes (recipe 48's is `decide_consistency`; others differ), so finding it mechanically hits the same name-vs-property problem the gold-coverage check solved by calling code instead of grepping names -- but the composition function, unlike a question builder, needs the OTHER answers as arguments (confidences, thresholds, a confidence gate), which this check cannot safely guess or default. A guard here would need either a documented naming convention for the composition entry point (which does not exist today) or a second discovery mechanism as careful as `_noul_propositions`, built and proven against the published set the same way.

Both are real, buildable guards -- I am not saying they are impossible -- but they need a design decision (what counts as "admits" for truth combinations; how a composition function is discovered without guessing its name) that is bigger than this PR's scope and that I should not make unilaterally inside a foundation PR whose diff is meant to be read in one sitting. I am handing the orchestrator a concrete starting point instead of a vague "future work" note: the outcome-determining check's hardest sub-problem is discovering the composition function without keying on a name, and the natural next step is to look for a documented convention (e.g., every recipe's composition entry point takes a `LabelDecision`-shaped or `dict[str, float]`-shaped argument) across the published set before writing a check, the same way I measured the question-builder shapes before writing this one.

## Proposed amendment text for #53 and #56

(Not applied -- I was asked to propose text only; the orchestrator applies it so the tracker keeps one voice.)

Append to each issue:

> **Fixture requirement for this recipe's `Noul` proposition(s), if more than one is asked together:** the fixture set must carry, in the split used to select each threshold, a gold-true row and a gold-false row for every proposition; at least one row for every truth combination the use case admits (both true, both false, each true alone); and at least one row where each proposition's own tag is what changes the composed outcome. The second and third are not implied by the first -- a fixture set can be positive-complete and still never exercise the states or the load-bearing-ness a battery exists to test.

## Acceptance criteria (from #283)

- [ ] "#53 and #56 carry the requirement before a builder is dispatched." **Not met by this PR** -- I propose the exact text above; I was instructed not to edit those issues myself.
- [x] "The guidance lives in a document an issue author reads." **Met** -- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe.yml`'s "Fixtures and evaluation" field now prompts for it directly.
- [x] "A decision is recorded on whether a guard enforces it, with reasons either way." **Met** -- gold-coverage is implemented and proven; truth-combination and outcome-determining coverage are ruled out of this PR's scope with the specific cost each would carry, above.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable -- this is foundation work (`docs/`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `tests/` only; no recipe folder touched).

## How it was verified

All commands run from `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-283` at head `c808be7810efb8fd69719b839ebe170336e9799c`.

```
# Verified the brief's "exact boilerplate appears in zero files" claim, can-speak proof included
git grep -n "One independent question per label or concern" -- '*'   # RC=1, no match
git grep -n "each threshold is chosen from examples and evaluated" -- '*'   # RC=1, no match
git grep -n "chosen from examples and evaluated" -- '*'   # RC=0, matches CONTRIBUTING.md:65 (can-speak proof)

# Targeted guard check, both interpreters
source .venv/bin/activate      # Python 3.14.7
python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX
# -> 730 passed, 43 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed (10 passed + 40 skipped are the new check)

source .venv310/bin/activate   # Python 3.10.21
python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX
# -> 730 passed, 43 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed -- identical totals

# Mutation proof the new check can both fire and not fire (fail-open discipline)
# On a scratch copy of recipes/48-document-revision-consistency/fixtures: removed every
# labels.jsonl row with breaks_reference == true, asserted the mutated text != the original
# text (mutation took), then re-ran _noul_gold_gaps on the mutated copy:
#   ORIGINAL: gaps=[]
#   MUTATED:  gaps=['validation/breaks_reference: no gold-true row (saw only [False])',
#                   'test/breaks_reference: no gold-true row (saw only [False])']
# introduces_new_fact (the untouched proposition) produced no gap in either run -- the mutation
# reddened exactly the proposition it touched, not an unrelated assertion.

# Full bare-root pytest, CI's own invocation, both interpreters, under the heavy-job lock
# (3.14, acquired as foundation-283, released by the ownership-checked trap in the same command)
python -m pytest -rX > "$TMPDIR/pytest_bare.out" 2>&1; echo $?
# -> 0; tail: "4395 passed, 46 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed in 116.85s"; grep -c
# "FAILED\|ERROR" on the full output -> 0 matches (grep rc=1, read as the three-way case:
# 0=matched, 1=clean, 2=grep itself broken)

# (3.10, same lock discipline, reacquired after the first run released it)
python -m pytest -rX > "$TMPDIR/pytest_bare_310.out" 2>&1; echo $?
# -> 0; tail: "4395 passed, 46 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed in 150.55s"; 0 FAILED/ERROR

python tools/render_catalog.py --check   # exit 0, empty output -- README unaffected (no recipe touched)
ruff check .                              # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                     # 378 files already formatted
```

No notebook was executed locally (foundation-PR rule); no recipe file was touched; `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` was not touched; no API key was used or looked for.

title: Recipe 44: Plan constraint assessment

title: Recipe 50: Model comparison and calibration
body:
Closes #50

Refs #78

## What this adds

`recipes/50-model-comparison-and-calibration/`: a harness that sends the same vendor-compliance
statement to three decision backends through one typed interface
(`jev_cookbook.backends.Backend`) -- Jev, and two fabricated decision adapters, `atlas-compact`
and `northstar-7b` -- and calibrates each one separately, on its own validation answers.

- **All three primitives.** Request A (always sent, one request): a `Choice` category over four
  fixed options (`data_handling`, `security_controls`, `business_continuity`, `other` as the
  fallback) plus two independent `Noul` propositions (`verifiable`, `names_control`), asked
  together. Request B (dependent, sent only when request A's own `category` answer is not
  `other`): a `Score` rubric rating how specific the statement is, every level described in
  words. The notebook's "The composition boundary" cell shows the gate explicitly: it fetches
  request B for one demo statement and visibly skips it for another, per backend, rather than
  fetching and discarding.
- **Calibration per backend.** Two thresholds, chosen on `validation` only and frozen: the
  `Choice` confidence threshold (`select_confidence_threshold`, `min_coverage` objective) and
  the `Noul` gate width for the two-sided band `confidence = |2p-1| >= gate_width` (same
  function, applied to `noul_confidence`, pooling both propositions). Both are computed in one
  loop per backend, in the notebook's `calibrate` cell.
- **No comparison drawn.** No live run has been recorded for this recipe. Every cell is a
  pipeline check on synthetic fixtures; no cell ranks the three backends, states a winner, or
  reports a margin. The issue is explicit that the offline run "draws no comparative
  conclusion" and that real numbers come only from a recorded live run -- with none recorded,
  there is no comparison to report honestly or otherwise.
- **Fixtures.** 23 rows (3 `demo`, 10 `validation`, 10 `test`) across all three backends'
  response files (`fixtures/responses.json`, `responses-atlas.json`, `responses-north.json`),
  including an adversarial case (an embedded instruction trying to steer the grader, twice), a
  conflicting case (a statement that names a control but admits no recent verification, twice),
  and a stateful case (a resubmission whose repeated low confidence escalates instead of
  reviewing again).
- **Leak check** at every granularity this recipe has a label for (`verifiable`,
  `names_control`, the `specificity` cutoff, and the composed outcome), reporting fire counts,
  false positives and false negatives for two cheap surface probes (digit presence, an
  audit-word regex) on both splits.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/50-model-comparison-and-calibration/` (the generated
  README regions are the integration worker's step, not this PR's)
- [ ] README regenerated -- not yet; expected, see below
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (outputs committed)
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` + `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MODEL`)

  are fabricated adapters this recipe never calls live

  states its mode for every backend in the `setup` cell
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference -- none was
  made; see "What was and was not measured" in the README and in the notebook
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the adversarial/conflicting/stateful hard cases, and carry
  gold labels (for the 20 scored rows; the 3 `demo` rows carry none, as the format requires)

  side effects)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels; this issue names no baseline to compare against (and this
  recipe draws no comparison at all, by design)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (detailed below)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, no key, no network, outputs committed -- verified by
  re-execution (see below) and `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` against an independently
  re-executed copy
- [x] Live mode opt-in, same question definitions -- `get_backend(fixtures=...)` is used only
  for `jev`; the other two backends are always built as plain `ReplayBackend`s
- [x] Fixtures synthetic, include the named hard cases, carry gold labels, pass the validator

  read once, after calibration is frozen on `validation`

  the exact live request count (41) and reports no results, since none was recorded
- [x] State/provenance/policy rules enforced in `helpers.py`, covered by tests that hold for any
  model answer (28 tests in `tests/test_helpers.py`, including three that flip one stored
  decision on real committed fixtures and show the composed outcome changes)
- [x] Fixtures include adversarial, conflicting and stateful cases; the notebook walks through
  one of each (`d01`/`d02` for composition, `d03` for the stateful escalation; the adversarial
  and conflicting rows are in `validation`/`test` and discussed in the fixture comments)

  metric is labelled a pipeline check
- [x] README states what it teaches, how to run it, what was and was not measured live
- [x] PR changes only this recipe's folder; CI expected green except `Catalog` (see below)

## Decisions a later builder will have to live with

- **Two alternative backends**, `atlas-compact` and `northstar-7b` (fabricated names, no real
  companies), both built as plain `ReplayBackend`s regardless of `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE`. Only `jev`
  is ever eligible for live mode; `get_backend(fixtures=...)` is called only for it, because that
  function ignores its `fixtures` argument and always returns a live backend under
  `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` -- calling it for the other two names would have silently tried to call
  them live too.
- **One shared `gate_width` per backend**, calibrated by pooling both `Noul` propositions'
  validation answers into one `select_confidence_threshold` call, rather than calibrating
  `verifiable` and `names_control` separately. This keeps the calibration to exactly two
  `select_confidence_threshold` call sites in the notebook (one per threshold kind), which is
  what keeps the `threshold_objective_pin` guard check tractable: each site's objective is
  pinned once, in `tests/test_helpers.py::test_the_notebook_calibration_cells_pin_min_coverage_not_target_accuracy`,
  by reading the committed `calibrate` cell's own source.
- **`min_coverage` (not `target_accuracy=1.0`)** for both calibrations, per the corrected
  guidance against forcing validation accuracy to 1.0 by construction. `CHOICE_MIN_COVERAGE =
  GATE_MIN_COVERAGE = 0.80`.
- **The Noul gate is measured, not asserted, to be inert or not.** The notebook's "Where the
  Noul gate bends" cell sweeps a 101-point grid of `g` on `validation` against `helpers.triage`'s
  own composed outcome (with `choice_threshold` pinned to 0 so only the Noul gate's own effect
  shows), for each backend, and reports the first `g` at which any outcome changes and the count
  changed at `g=1.0`. No general inertness rule is stated anywhere in the recipe.
- **The leak check uses two cheap features** (digit presence, an "audit/review/ISO/SOC" regex)
  at every granularity (`verifiable`, `names_control`, the `specificity` cutoff, and jev's own
  composed `FLAGGED` outcome). None reaches 1.0 with zero false positives transferring to
  `test`; the full fp/fn/fire-count table is printed in the notebook's `leak` cell.
- **`SPECIFICITY_CUTOFF = 2`** is a bare Python constant, not calibrated from data -- it is a
  business rule about how specific a statement must be before it is worth flagging, independent
  of anything a backend answers.

## Unfinished / out of scope

- **README regeneration** is the integration worker's step, not this PR's (CONTRIBUTING.md's
  generated-README exception); `Catalog (README is current)` is expected to be red until then.

title: Recipe 49: Multi-agent task assignment
body:
Closes #49
Refs #78

## What this adds

`recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/`: one `Score` per (agent, subtask) pair (72 scored
pairs across two independently-shaped scheduling scenarios, plus 2 unscored demo pairs), and a
deterministic Python scheduler (`helpers.assign`) that combines that score with capability,
dependency and budget — none of which Jev is ever shown. The central deliverable is
`tests/test_constraints.py`: a property test that measures, not merely asserts, that all three
constraints hold for any scores (300 random score matrices per constraint, with the count of
iterations where the constraint actually *binds* asserted non-zero), plus a mutation proof per
constraint (disable its enforcement one at a time, show the invariant redden, and show the
mutation actually changed the schedule before interpreting the failure).

Four quantities, since this recipe's "one Score per pair" shape makes them all different from
each other: **input rows / requests / questions are all 74** (one Score request per (agent,
subtask) pair, no battery, cached by example id so each is decided once); **task-level units are
12** (6 validation subtasks + 6 test subtasks — "assignment quality against gold" is one unit
per subtask, smaller than the request count, the opposite relationship from a recipe that
batches several questions into one request).

## Decisions a later builder will have to live with

- **Two separately-scored evaluations, not one.** Pair-level ("does Jev's modal suitability
  level for this one pair match gold?", 72 units, feeds the confidence threshold) and task-level
  ("did the scheduler's actual pick for this subtask match the best gold-capable agent?", 12
  units, feeds "assignment quality against gold"). They answer different questions and are
  reported separately rather than conflated.
- **The confidence gate is chosen with `min_coverage`, not `target_accuracy=1.0`**, and the
  notebook's own sweep cell shows it is piecewise constant across the whole feasible range on
  this pool (the single low-confidence validation pair happens to be correct, so the lowest
  threshold dominates on both coverage and accuracy everywhere). Pinned by parsing the committed
  notebook cell's own source (`tests/test_threshold_pin.py`) for the `min_coverage` spelling,
  not by a value-change mutation (which this pool's piecewise-constant shape would make inert).
- **The fuzz's fixed scenario cannot witness dependency binding on its own.** `sprint-1`'s own
  numbers always leave just enough supply upstream of any dependency chain for the *parent* to
  succeed, so scarcity always resolves at a chain's deepest leaf (a "no eligible agent" review,
  not a dependency block) — true for any scores, and disclosed as such in the notebook's own
  printed output (dependency binds: 0, with the reason stated). `tests/test_constraints.py`
  measures dependency binding on a second, dedicated, deliberately smaller scenario built
  specifically so a parent can starve one wave before it is itself processed; there it is 300 of
  300 (deterministic by that scenario's own numbers, not score-dependent, which is disclosed
  rather than overclaimed as variable).
- **Baselines are genuine attempts, not strawmen, and both lose.** Capacity (structured
  fields only, zero requests) and lexical cue (reads the same prose Jev reads, zero requests) are
  both reported on both splits; neither ties or beats the mechanism (validation 3/6 mechanism vs
  1/6 capacity vs 2/6 cue; test 4/6 mechanism vs 3/6 capacity vs 1/6 cue). Neither has a
  continuous knob to sweep (capacity's tie-break is forced by this fixture set's uniform
  capacities; the cue word lists are the whole baseline). The surface-form leak check (the same
  cue heuristic, plus a direct regex check of whether cue sign alone predicts structured
  capability) found no leak: 31 of 72 pairs, 11 false positives — nowhere near the zero-false-
  positive signature of an actual leak.
- **The strong-form test and the fuzz/mutation tests are in separate files** so a decorated
  function near the strong-form test cannot make the recipe guard's text-scanning extraction
  raise on unrelated source; `tests/test_helpers.py` keeps the strong-form test last and nothing
  decorated anywhere near it.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/` (verified:
  `git diff --name-status $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD` lists only this folder)
- [ ] README regenerated — not yet; per the generated-README exception this is the integration
  worker's step, after handover. `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until then.
- [ ] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` scope check — same as above, expected to already
  pass for this branch's own diff (no symlink/mode/type change anywhere; every mode is `100644`)
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same question
  definitions; README states the exact live call count (74) against the default budget (25) and
  tells the reader to raise `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS`
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); notebook states its mode
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost anywhere; every reported number is labelled
  a pipeline check in an offline run
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (a confidently wrong pair, a deliberately
  adversarial incapable-agent pair, a subtask nobody is capable of, a dependency chain, budget
  exhaustion), and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; nothing is executed, everything is a simulated assignment
  (`jev_cookbook.simulation.Budget`/`ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue`)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels; the issue names no specific baseline, so two were built and
  both reported honestly (neither wins)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, outputs committed — re-executed twice,
  byte-identical both times; `check_notebook_fresh.py` confirms a fresh run matches, and (proven
  separately) can report a tampered copy as stale
- [x] Live mode opt-in, same question definitions — `get_backend`/`build_questions` unchanged by
  mode
- [x] Fixtures synthetic, hard cases included, gold-labelled, pass the validator —
  `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment` → valid
- [x] Every response fixture's provenance recorded; notebook states its mode — `run_header` cell
- [x] Evaluation: assignment quality against gold (task-level, `evaluate_outcomes`) and the
  constraint test (`tests/test_constraints.py`)
- [x] State/provenance/policy rules enforced in `helpers.py`, covered by tests holding for any
  model answer — `helpers.assign`'s three `enforce_*` guards, proven by the 300-trial fuzz and
  by mutation
- [x] Fixtures include adversarial/conflicting/stateful cases, notebook walks through at least
  one — the "Python's part" cell/discussion walks the real `sprint-1` cascade: a capability
  override of an adversarially-scored incapable agent, a judgment error among genuinely
  available candidates, and budget exhaustion blocking a subtask whose own dependency had
  already succeeded
- [x] No Jev quality/latency/cost claim without recorded live inference; synthetic metrics
  labelled pipeline checks
- [x] README states what it teaches, how to run it, what was/was not measured live
- [x] PR changes only this recipe's folder; CI pending on this head

## How it was verified

All commands run from the repository root of `/workspace/worktrees/recipe-49` (branch
`recipe/49-multi-agent-task-assignment`), head `07d4fe43f30e66a33ecbd25831d71fd2fb666fdd`.

```bash
# Python 3.14 venv (.venv), installed -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt for figure comparison
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment
# -> fixtures valid (mode replay)

python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment
# -> executed notebook.ipynb offline; re-run twice, byte-identical both times (md5sum compared)

python tools/check_notebook_fresh.py recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/notebook.ipynb <fresh-copy>/notebook.ipynb
# -> matches a fresh offline run (rc 0); then one output hand-tampered in the fresh copy and
#    re-run -> STALE, naming the exact cell/output that differs (rc 1), proving the check can fail

ruff check recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/      # All checks passed!
ruff format --check recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/   # 8 files already formatted

pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k "49-multi-agent-task-assignment" -rX -q
# -> 15 passed, 772 deselected

pytest recipes/49-multi-agent-task-assignment/tests/test_constraints.py -q -s
# -> binding counts of 300 trials: capability 287, budget 294, dependency 300; 4 passed

python tools/check_hygiene.py                           # Hygiene check passed: 529 file(s) scanned.
python tools/render_catalog.py --check                  # README.md is out of date (expected: see below)

# Bare pytest (the full suite, under the shared HEAVY.lock), both interpreters:
pytest -q            # .venv  (3.14): 4324 passed, 6 skipped, 48 deselected, 31 xfailed, 121.64s
pytest -q            # .venv310 (3.10): 4324 passed, 6 skipped, 48 deselected, 31 xfailed, 144.08s
```

`python tools/render_catalog.py --check` reporting the README stale is expected and not a defect
here: adding this notebook makes the generated catalog regions stale until the integration
worker regenerates them in this same pull request, per the generated-README exception in
CONTRIBUTING.md; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red on this head until then.

## What I declined, and why

- A third zero-request baseline (round-robin) was considered and dropped: capacity and cue
  already cover "no information beyond structure" and "reads the same text, cheaply" respectively,
  and a third weak baseline would not change the rule-19 verdict (the mechanism wins outright on
  both splits).
- I did not add a confidence gate that varies by subtask or by agent (e.g. a stricter gate for
  budget-critical agents); the brief's build notes ask for one deterministic scheduler under
  capability/dependency/budget, and a per-agent gate would be a different, more elaborate design
  than what was asked for.

## Out-of-scope findings (reported here, not only in a code comment)

- None of the shared `jev_cookbook` helpers were missing anything this recipe needed; no
  foundation issue to file. `helpers.simulation.Budget` (a plain, named-counter budget with
  `can_spend`/`spend` raising `BudgetExceeded`) was exactly the right fit for a per-agent work
  budget, and `ReviewQueue`/`ActionLog` fit the "review" and "assigned" outcomes with no
  adaptation needed.
- While exploring `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`'s `threshold_objective_pin` check
  (`_threshold_pin_obligations`, `_pinned_objective_spellings`), I found it is considerably more
  sophisticated (AST taint-tracing through assignments, several credited pin shapes) than a
  cursory read suggests; no defect found in it, just noting for whoever reads this that it is
  worth reading in full before assuming a simple `"min_coverage" in source` string check is the
  whole story — it very nearly is, for this recipe, but the module's own regression tests show
  several ways a naive version of that check can be fooled.

title: Recipe 48: Document revision consistency
body:
Closes #48
Refs #78

## Summary

A `Choice` selects among three externally supplied sentence-revision candidates plus the named
`keep_original` fallback. A two-proposition `Noul` battery (`introduces_new_fact`,
`breaks_reference`) then checks only the candidate actually picked for consistency with the
surrounding paragraph -- a request that always comes *after* the choice, and is skipped entirely
when the choice is gated or names `keep_original`. Python composes both answers
(`helpers.decide`) over `jev_cookbook.simulation.Store`, a versioned key-value store that never
deletes.

## Checklist (from `.github/pull_request_template.md`)

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, no key, no network; outputs committed
- [x] Live mode is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), same question definitions
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, gold-labelled, include the named hard cases, pass the validator
- [x] Every response fixture records provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states its run mode
- [x] Evaluation: stage-one selection agreement with gold; consistency-flag precision/recall;
      task-level outcome coverage/accuracy/risk; a version-history/rollback test
- [x] Policy rules enforced in `helpers.py`, covered by tests that hold for any model answer
      (every revision option swept; a 101×101 Noul grid on both sides of the confidence band)
- [x] Fixtures include adversarial, conflicting and stateful cases; the notebook walks through
      a two-round demo covering all three
- [x] No Jev quality/latency/cost claim; every synthetic metric is labelled a pipeline check
- [x] `README.md` says what this recipe teaches, how to run it, what was/was not measured live
- [x] This PR changes only `recipes/48-document-revision-consistency/`; `Catalog (README is
      current)` is expected red until the integration worker regenerates it (see
      CONTRIBUTING.md's generated-README exception) -- not a defect of this PR

## Decisions a later builder should know about

- **Two separate confidence thresholds, not one.** `choice_threshold` gates stage one
  (`select_confidence_threshold(..., min_coverage=0.9)`); `consistency_gate` gates stage two,
  pooled over both propositions of every `validation` item stage one answered with a real
  candidate (`min_coverage=0.9` again). Both are pinned in `tests/test_helpers.py` by parsing
  the committed notebook cell source (keyword *and* value), independently of each other.
- **The Noul gate is a measured property of this composition, not an asserted general rule.**
  `helpers.decide_consistency`'s gate changes `helpers.decide`'s own outcome only on the
  "reject side" (a confident `false` reading too low-confidence to trust) and never on the
  "accept side" (a confident `true` reading is already heading to review on the business tag
  alone) -- measured over a 101×101 grid in both the notebook and `tests/test_helpers.py`, never
  derived algebraically.
- **The per-proposition business thresholds (`0.5` for both) are fixed, not swept with
  `select_threshold`.** `breaks_reference` has no positive example in `validation`'s applied-
  eligible rows, which makes an F1 sweep degenerate (`select_threshold` raises). `0.5` is
  justified in the notebook by inspecting validation's own distribution (every gold-`True`
  stored noul sits at 0.85+; every gold-`False` one sits at 0.12 or below). A larger validation
  split with a positive `breaks_reference` example is what would let a future revision use
  `select_threshold` genuinely, which I flag as a limitation rather than working around it.
- **A rule-19 "dominated headline" result is reported, not hidden.** On the committed `test`
  split, a cheap surface-cue baseline (percent signs, round numbers, urgency phrases) beats
  Jev's raw consistency tag (0.8333 vs 0.6667), and Jev's own tag only ties the always-consistent
  floor. The notebook's "Baselines" section states this plainly, names the hard case
  (`t-cand1-wrongconsistency`, a cue-free broken reference) that would show the mechanism's
  value and that Jev also misses on this data, and flags that the cue list was chosen with
  sight of the fixtures (so some of its strength is circular) rather than claiming a clean win.
- **`helpers.task_correct` closes a "full-path trap"**: comparing only the composed outcome's
  *class* (`applied`/`kept_original`/`review`) would score a confidently-wrong stage-one pick as
  correct whenever the wrong candidate happens to be itself consistent and gold is also
  `applied` elsewhere. `t-cand2-wrongchoice` is exactly this row; `task_correct` also checks the
  applied candidate's own identifier against gold.
- **Surface-form leak check.** Candidate length and paragraph word-overlap are reported as
  baselines (both well short of a perfect score on `test`); a length-delta check between the
  chosen candidate and the original sentence shows the gold-consistent and gold-inconsistent
  ranges overlap on this split, so no length cutoff recovers the label. The one real rival
  (the cue baseline above) reads the candidate's own text for a plausible signal, not a
  template artefact, and is reported as a baseline rather than dismissed.
- **`fixtures/responses.json` holds exactly 36 entries**, matching `len(responses.json)` to the
  notebook's own `request_count` (the README's live-call-count sentence states this). Two rows
  whose stage-one choice never clears any plausible gate (by construction: a near-uniform
  four-way distribution) carry no stage-two response at all, rather than an unused one, so the
  stored count never drifts from what a live run would actually spend.

## How it was verified

Both commands below were run from the repository root in a `uv`-managed venv (`uv venv --python
3.14 .venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev,live]"` and `uv venv --python 3.10 .venv310 && uv pip
install -e ".[dev]"`); all commands were run on both, with identical results unless noted.

```bash
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/48-document-revision-consistency
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/48-document-revision-consistency   # heavy; under the shared slot
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
pytest                                                                       # heavy; under the shared slot
pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k "48-document-revision-consistency" -rX
pytest tests/test_recipe_sources.py -k "48-document-revision-consistency"
python tools/check_hygiene.py
python tools/render_catalog.py --check   # expected red; see the generated-README exception above
```

Freshness: executed a fresh copy with `tools/execute_notebook.py` into a scratch directory and
compared with `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` against the committed notebook (0 problems); then
deliberately tampered one committed stream output and re-ran the comparison, which reported
`STALE: notebook.cells[2].outputs[0].text: 3 items committed, 1 in the fresh run` and exited 1 --
proving the check can fail before trusting it passing.

Results: `pytest` (bare, root) -- 4403 passed, 5 skipped, 48 deselected, 31 xfailed (pre-existing,
unrelated to this recipe) on Python 3.14; same counts on Python 3.10. The recipe guard: 15 passed
for this recipe's slug, no allowlist entry added or needed, on both interpreters. `ruff check .`
and `ruff format --check .`: clean on both. Fixture validator: `fixtures valid (mode replay)`.
Hygiene: `Hygiene check passed`. Catalog check: red, as expected pre-integration.

title: Foundation: key the scripted-recipe guard skips on the property each check means, not responses.json
body:
Refs #249

Not all acceptance criteria are met as predicted by the issue — see "Decisions" and "Item 2" below for why `Refs` rather than `Closes` is correct here.

## What this adds

Three of the recipe guard's scripted-recipe skips were keyed on `fixtures/responses.json`'s existence, a correlate of "this recipe's answers are stored" rather than of what each check actually means. This re-keys two of the three skips on their real property, documents the third (which was already correctly keyed), and enumerates all three in the module docstring with individual reasons. Diff is `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` only — no recipe file, including the template, was touched.

### Item 1 — `G1(c)` (`stored_answers_strong_form`, line ~511)

**Property this check is now about:** does this recipe freeze a confidence or business threshold at all (a real `select_confidence_threshold(`/`select_threshold(` call somewhere in its committed notebook or `helpers.py`) — not whether its answers happen to be stored in `responses.json`.

The skip is now keyed on `_threshold_pin_obligations(recipe_dir(recipe))`, the same real-call detector `threshold_objective_pin` already uses (AST-level, walks the committed notebook cells and `helpers.py`, resolves import aliases) — reused rather than re-implemented, per the house guidance against enumerating spellings.

**Measured outcome — differs from the issue's prediction, and I want to flag that clearly rather than paper over it.** The issue states "with the skip removed, 36 recipes pass and recipe 36 alone fails" and expects an allowlist entry naming #249. I re-ran this exactly as described (skip removed entirely, then re-keyed) against the current published set (47 recipes + template) and recipe 36 **passes**, with 48/48 passing and 0 skipped. Tracing it down: PR #246's own fix round (comment "strong-form test name misses `G1(c)`'s anchor") renamed the test function from `test_scripted_answers_are_not_all_right_...` to `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right_above_the_frozen_confidence_gate` *before merge*, specifically to satisfy `STRONG_FORM_DEF`'s substring match. The issue's "would FAIL" measurement was taken against an earlier revision of that PR, before its own fix round landed; the defect it names was already closed by the time recipe 36 reached `main`. **No allowlist entry is added** — adding one for a check that genuinely passes would itself be a hard failure under `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`'s `strict=True` xfail (an unexpected pass raises `XPASS(strict)`), which is a decisive, mechanical confirmation that recipe 36 really does pass this check today, not just my own reading of the code.

**Proof the changed skip can both fire and not fire:**
- *Fires* (no threshold frozen): `test_stored_answers_strong_form_skip_fires_only_when_no_threshold_is_frozen` (new regression test, right after the parametrized check) — a throwaway `tmp_path` copy of recipe 36 with its one `select_confidence_threshold(` call and its import stripped; `_threshold_pin_obligations` returns `[]` on the mutated copy and is asserted non-empty on the unmodified copy first (so the mutation is proven to have taken, not merely assumed).
- *Does not fire* (threshold frozen, check runs for real): the parametrized case `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right_is_the_strong_form[36-card-game-action-selection]`, which is PASSED (not SKIPPED) in every run above — the live, continuously-run proof for this direction.

### Item 2 — README live-call count (`readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers`, line ~1159) — investigated, NOT implemented; reasoned deferral

The issue's own suggestion is to derive the README's stated live-call count from the notebook's actual `decide()` calls rather than from `len(responses.json)`, which would make the check apply to scripted recipes and close #213's gap (a doubly-decided example collapsing to one entry in a dict keyed by replay state).

**Investigation, and why I did not implement it:**

- `len(responses.json)` is already a proxy, not a direct count, even for non-scripted recipes: it counts *distinct decided states*, by construction of `build_fixtures.py`. Recipe 36's own numbers are the clean counterexample — 96 scored rows, 290 real `decide()` calls (measured by PR #246's reviewer via hand-instrumentation), only 72 distinct states. The proxy and the real count differ by 4x on data already in this repository.
- There is no committed artifact today, for any recipe, that holds the real `decide()`-call count. `ReplayBackend`/`ScriptedBackend` (`src/jev_cookbook/backends.py`) keep no call counter (`requests_made` exists only on `LiveBackend`, `src/jev_cookbook/live.py:587`). The only way to recover the true count is to execute the notebook's real control flow with a counting wrapper — which is literally what the PR #246 reviewer did by hand.
- **A static route (fixtures row count × call-sites, no execution) does not generalise.** It works for a simple "one call per row" recipe, but recipe 36's own count is a function of card-game simulation dynamics (episode length varies by game state) — not a closed form over `inputs.jsonl`'s row count. This is the same shape of trap as the Wave-3 brief's rule 19 "never let a formula be the derivation" and rule 16's four-times-corrected quantity confusion (rows vs. requests vs. questions vs. units): a formula that fits today's simple recipes breaks on the next irregular one, silently, which is exactly the "a check keyed on a shape rather than a property" failure #249 itself exists to stop.
- **A "committed-output" route** (read an already-executed, already-committed count from a notebook cell, the way `measured_cell_prints_n_offline` reads a committed `N:` line, with no execution performed by the guard itself) would work in principle, but no currently published recipe's committed output carries such a counter — it would require (a) a shared counting-backend wrapper (fine, shared code) **and** (b) retrofitting every recipe's notebook to use and print it, which means editing and re-executing every one of 46+ recipes. That is squarely a recipe-files change and a cross-recipe sweep, both outside this foundation PR's permitted diff (`tests/` only, no recipe files) and outside this issue's scope.
- `#213` — the issue this gap is actually tracked under — already names the right fix location in its own body: *"instrumenting the backend during the offline execution CI already performs is the cheap route, since replay and live take the same path through `decide`"*. That is the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job, which already executes every notebook; adding a counting assertion there is close to free marginal cost. The shared `Tests` leg (where `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` runs) explicitly does not execute notebooks and should not start doing so for one check.

**Conclusion: this needs a different home — #213's own per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job, not this guard's `Tests` leg.** I have not implemented a static or execution-based route here. What I did do, in scope: reworded the skip's docstring and message to name the real property ("no committed artifact this check can read a real call count from," not "no responses.json") and to point at #213 and #249 for the next reader, so the skip is at least honestly described rather than silently proxy-keyed. The acceptance criterion "the README live-call check applies to scripted recipes, **or a recorded decision explains why it cannot**" is met by the second half.

### Item 3 — `build_fixtures_scaffold` (line ~316) — left as a skip, docstring improved

**Property:** does this recipe's scaffold produce a `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` to hold byte-identical to anything. `tools/new_recipe.py --mode scripted` (`build_scripted_fixtures_text`) never writes `responses.json` and never writes that test file — genuinely vacuous for a scripted recipe, confirmed by reading `tools/new_recipe.py` directly rather than trusting the issue's characterization. Skip is unchanged in mechanism (still keyed on `responses.json`'s absence, which **is** the real property for this one check), but the function's own docstring and the skip message now say why, naming #249.

### Item 4 — module docstring

The `"... none are published yet"` line is gone (false the moment recipe 36 merged, which it already has). Replaced with an enumeration of all three scripted-recipe skips, each with its own property and reason — see the module docstring in the diff, right before the `from __future__ import annotations` line.

### Item 5 — full published set, each skip condition temporarily removed

Measured against the current published set (47 recipes + template; the only scripted recipe is 36 — confirmed by scanning every `recipes/*/fixtures/` for a missing `responses.json` beside a committed `notebook.ipynb`):

| check | skip lifted | result |
|---|---|---|
| `stored_answers_strong_form` (G1(c)) | entirely, then re-keyed on the property | **0 newly-failing recipes.** 48/48 pass either way. Recipe 36 passes (see item 1's measured-outcome note above). |
| `build_fixtures_scaffold` | entirely | **1 newly-failing recipe: `36-card-game-action-selection`** — `AssertionError: no tests/test_build_fixtures.py`. Expected and vacuous (item 3); not a defect, no allowlist entry (it's the correct, honest outcome of a check that doesn't apply, not drift to hide). |
| `readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers` | entirely | **1 newly-failing recipe: `36-card-game-action-selection`** — crashes with `FileNotFoundError` on the missing `responses.json` once the skip is removed (not a clean `AssertionError`, which is itself evidence this check's current shape cannot be extended to a scripted recipe without the item-2 redesign). Expected and vacuous; not a defect, no allowlist entry. |

**No allowlist entries were added by this PR.** `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` is unchanged (still 31 entries, diff is empty on that file) — every lifted skip either produces no new failure (item 1) or produces the already-understood, non-defect vacuous failure the issue itself labelled correct (items 2 and 3).

## Decisions a later builder/reviewer will have to live with

- **Item 1's allowlist expectation was not followed, on measured evidence contradicting it.** I verified this three ways: a direct Python probe calling the guard's own functions, the real parametrized pytest case (`PASSED`, not `SKIPPED`), and a from-scratch removal of the skip condition entirely (not just the re-keyed version) over the whole published set, all agreeing recipe 36 passes. I'm reporting this prominently rather than silently adding a speculative entry, per "never weaken a check" and the allowlist's own `strict=True` design, which would have rejected a fabricated entry anyway.
- **Item 2 is a deferral, not an implementation.** I changed only the skip's wording/documentation, not its mechanism. The right next step is on `#213`, in the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` job, not here.
- **`_threshold_pin_obligations` is reused, not duplicated**, for item 1's skip condition — it is defined later in the same module (line ~1429 after this change) but that's a forward reference resolved at test-run time, not at class-body or import-ordering time, so it's safe; both call sites (the pre-existing `threshold_objective_pin` check and this skip) now agree on what "this recipe has a real threshold call" means, which is exactly the kind of one-definition-of-the-property discipline #249's general point asks for.
- **No recipe file was touched, including the template** — the template already has a confidence gate and `responses.json`, so it is unaffected by the item-1 re-keying either way; it was never skipped before and is not skipped now.

## How it was verified

All commands run from `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-249`, two clean venvs (`uv venv --python 3.14 .venv`, `uv venv --python 3.10 .venv310`, both `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`, no `[ml]` — no notebook was executed locally).

```
source .venv/bin/activate
ruff check .                                   # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                          # 364 files already formatted
python tools/render_catalog.py --check         # rc=0
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX -q
  # 690 passed, 3 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest -q
  # 4287 passed, 6 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed   (bare pytest, CI's own invocation, py3.14)

source .venv310/bin/activate
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest -q
  # 4287 passed, 6 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed   (bare pytest, py3.10)
```

The 6 skips on both interpreters: 3 pre-existing and unrelated (`typesafe_sdk` not installed x2, `pre-commit`/environment ruff not installed), 1 pre-existing and unrelated (recipe 16's named `ESCALATE` exemption), and the 2 from items 2 and 3 above, both now worded to name the real reason and both pointing at #249/#213.

Both full-suite runs were the one heavy job per hold, in the canonical `/workspace/worktrees/_scratch/HEAVY.lock`, acquired in its own bounded command and released by an ownership-checked trap in the same command as the `pytest` call (not a separate acquire command — so the trap never fires before the heavy job it protects). Checked `/proc/*/cwd` across all worktrees before each acquire; nothing else was running either time. Both runs completed and the lock was released before this PR was opened.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — this is a foundation pull request; no recipe folder was touched.

## Out of scope — for the orchestrator, not for this branch

- **#213 itself** (the real fix for item 2) needs a design decision about where a counting wrapper lives in `src/jev_cookbook/backends.py` and how the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job would assert against it, plus a cross-recipe sweep to retrofit every notebook once that design is chosen. Not mine to do here.
- **The issue's own "would FAIL" measurement for item 1 was stale by the time this issue was filed** (PR #246's fix round had already renamed the anchor-missing function). Worth a note on #249 itself so a future reader doesn't re-derive the same surprise; I'm not editing the issue, just flagging it here per the house rule on reporting out-of-scope findings in the PR/report rather than only in a code comment.
- **`_find_function_body` (line 442) still has the #272 decorator-folding defect**: it scans forward by regex to the next `\n(?:def |class )` rather than using the parser's own `end_lineno`, so a decorated neighbour folds into the extracted body and `ast.parse` can raise a `SyntaxError` that blames the recipe rather than the extraction. Not touched here and not exercised by anything in this change (recipe 36's one match is a prefix match with no intervening decorator before the next `def`), confirmed by the new regression test passing.

title: Bump ruff from 0.16.10 to 0.17.0
body:
Bumps [ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) from 0.16.10 to 0.17.0.
Release notes

Sourced from ruff's releases.

0.17.0

Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-09.

The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and ruff wheels are now code-signed. macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting, and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.

Breaking changes

  • Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 (#28792)

    Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through target-version or requires-python. When checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15 instead of 3.14.

  • Update the default rule set (#28786)

    Several of the flake8-datetimez rules (DTZ001, DTZ005, DTZ006, DTZ007, DTZ011, DTZ012, and DTZ901) are no longer enabled by default, while undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage (F406), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.

  • Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 (#27295)

    JUnit output now uses a skipped attribute instead of disabled on <testsuite> elements and includes a skipped attribute on the root <testsuites> element.

  • [flake8-import-conventions] Add datetime as dt as a conventional alias (ICN001) (#28790)

  • Support Unicode dummy variable names (#28722)

    The default lint.dummy-variable-rgx now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as _次, as dummy variables.

  • Update to Unicode 17 (#21229, #28784)

    Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes ("\N{...}").

  • Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI (#27810)

    The default full output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review, regardless of the unsafe-fixes setting. Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.

  • Remove the Python dependency from conda-forge builds (conda-forge/ruff-feedstock#361)

    The conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, now supports linux-riscv64, win-arm64, and linux-ppc64le platforms, and now includes shell completions. However, no longer depending on Python means that python -m ruff and import ruff will no longer work. Use ruff directly from PATH instead. PyPI installations and those from the standalone installer are unaffected.

  • Remove support for ruff-lsp (#28750)

    Support for ruff-lsp, the legacy Python language server deprecated in Ruff v0.9.5, has been removed. The Ruff VS Code extension now always uses the native language server; ruff.nativeServer is deprecated and ignored. See the migration guide.

Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

  • lazy-import-mismatch (TID254)
  • lazy-import-immediately-resolved (TID255)
  • os-path-commonprefix (RUF071)
