title: Recipe 41: Approval scope review
body:
Closes #41

## What this adds

`recipes/41-approval-scope-review/`: a proposed tool action carries an approval **binding**
(the approval it claims to act under) that Python checks exactly — six independent reasons,
no model answer read — and, only once that binding holds, two independent `Noul` propositions
(`intent_mismatch`, `scope_creep`) judge whether the action's own text is a semantic fit for
the approved task. `helpers.decide` composes the two into one of three outcomes: `denied`
(binding refused, unconditional on the model), `review` (binding held, a proposition confidently
flagged or either too uncertain to trust), `executed` (binding held, both confidently clear).

The safety property the issue asks for — "the model's answer can add a hold and can never grant
an action" — is proved by an exhaustive breakpoint-exact sweep of the full `[0, 1]` answer
space for both propositions (every region the composed decision can distinguish, over 8
synthetic binding-failure cases and all 14 real denied fixtures), and shown non-vacuous by a
deliberately broken composition (defined only in the test file) that checks the model first and
executes a denied action when it reads confidently clear — `tests/test_helpers.py::
test_the_safety_asymmetry_property_test_is_not_vacuous_a_broken_composition_fails_it` runs the
same sweep against both and asserts the real one holds while the broken one does not; the
notebook's own "Proving the property can fail" cell runs the single sharpest instance of this
and prints both outcomes side by side.

Fixtures: 15 `validation` + 15 `test` scored actions (30 total; 15 input rows per split, 15
requests per split — one `decide` call per row, what the live budget bills — 30 questions per
split since every request carries two independent propositions together, and 15 task-level
units per split since `helpers.decide` reports one outcome per row — rows, requests and units
coincide here; questions do not, because this recipe sends two propositions per request), plus
5 `demo` actions (two shown
"up close" and a 3-action stateful sequence demonstrating approval-use consumption: the third
action in the sequence is refused purely because Python's own use count is exhausted, with the
model's answer unchanged from the first two). Every binding-failure reason is exercised on real
committed data (`v09`/`t09` wrong citation, `v10`/`t10` expired, `v11`/`t11` revoked,
`v12`/`t12` actor mismatch, `v13`/`t13` tool outside scope, `v14`/`t14` resource outside scope,
`v15`/`t15` uses consumed), and five of the seven denied actions on each split are
semantically *clear* — gold `False` on both propositions — the concrete, committed instance of
the headline property, not only the synthetic sweep (two of those five, `v14-resource` and
`t15-consumed`, sit at 0.8200 confidence, just under the 0.8400 gate, so four rather than five
are also *confidently* clear; the notebook names both counts under the quantity each is
actually over).

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/41-approval-scope-review/`, plus the generated README
  regions regenerated by the integration worker (nothing else outside the recipe folder)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` after updating against current
  `main`, before final review; `--check` passes — **not run by this builder**; expected red
  until the integration worker's pass, per CONTRIBUTING.md's generated-README exception
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/41-approval-scope-review/`
  paths, no symlink/mode/type change, nothing renamed or deleted out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which
  mode it ran in
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (no-match/clean, ambiguous, mixed,
  adversarial, benign look-alike, stateful consumption, every one of the six binding-failure
  reasons), and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (nothing is ever actually permitted
  or executed; `jev_cookbook.simulation.ReviewQueue` records review items only)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels — the issue names no baseline, so two zero-request
  baselines the use case's own shape suggests (`permission_only`, `always_review`) are reported
  alongside the mechanism, cost included
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see "Acceptance criteria" below)

## Decisions

- **Two independent `Noul` propositions, not one.** The build notes say "one independent
  question per label or concern, sent together in one request." `intent_mismatch` (the action
  pursues a different purpose) and `scope_creep` (the action's own description claims a broader
  or different effect) are independently consequential on real committed fixtures (`v04` for
  intent, via the shared confidence gate; `v02-nearmiss` for scope, via its own business tag —
  `tests/test_helpers.py::test_intent_mismatch_is_independently_consequential_on_the_fixtures`
  and `test_scope_creep_is_independently_consequential_on_the_fixtures`).
- **The binding check never sees a model answer, by construction, not by convention.**
  `check_binding(action, approval, uses_spent)` takes no answer parameter at all — there is
  nothing to read even if one wanted to. `decide` calls it first and returns `DENIED`
  immediately on refusal, before `decide_labels` is ever called in that branch.
- **Approvals are embedded per row, not looked up in a shared catalog**, except for the
  3-action stateful sequence (`d03`–`d05`), which shares one approval object across three rows
  and threads `uses_spent` as an explicit integer argument — Python's own bookkeeping across the
  sequence, never inferred from state `check_binding` reads on its own. This keeps every scored
  row self-contained and independently testable while still demonstrating genuine state.
- **Gate selected with `min_coverage=0.6`, not `target_accuracy=1.0`.** Two of the 30 pooled
  validation (action, proposition) decisions are wrong, so `target_accuracy=1.0` would need the
  gate to reject real data; `min_coverage` is swept across its full `[0, 1]` range in both the
  notebook and a dedicated test and demonstrably selects three distinct values, monotonically
  non-increasing as `min_coverage` rises (admits more, selects a looser gate) —
  `test_min_coverage_sweep_the_selector_actually_selects_and_the_direction_is_right`.
- **The frozen gate (0.8400) is checked against `|2t - 1|` for both business thresholds
  (0.2000, 0.7600) before anything is said about what it does.** It is strictly greater than
  both, so it is **not inert**: it is equivalent to a stricter pair of cut-offs (0.08 / 0.92)
  replacing each threshold's single one. The notebook prints the counterfactual (gate forced to
  0.0) beside the real validation numbers, and
  `test_the_confidence_gate_is_not_inert_for_either_business_threshold` pins the comparison.
- **The strong-form test (`test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right`) re-derives the gate locally**,
  not through the shared `_frozen_thresholds_and_gate` test helper the other tests use — an
  independent check cannot route through the production path it audits without agreeing with it
  by construction. This also satisfies the recipe guard's `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right_
  is_the_strong_form` check, whose `ast` walk requires the re-derivation syntactically local to
  that one function.
- **`REASON_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE` is exactly `"confidence below the threshold"`** (the lexicon's
  fixed string), and the outcome value is exactly `"review"` — both per the house convention in
  `docs/glossary.md`.

## How it was verified

Run from a clean `uv` venv (`uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`) at the
repository root:

```bash
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
pytest -q
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate --all
```

Notebook execution, under the pinned constraints (the stack CI's `Notebook` job uses):

```bash
uv pip install -e ".[ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/41-approval-scope-review
git diff --stat recipes/41-approval-scope-review/notebook.ipynb   # empty: reproduces byte-identically
```

Scope (the same check CI runs; `--body-file` must be this file, `--branch` the head branch name):

```bash
git rev-parse origin/main                                        # base
git rev-parse HEAD                                                # head
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base <base-sha> --head <head-sha> \
  --branch recipe/41-approval-scope-review --body-file <this-file>
```

Results on this head:

- `ruff check .`: All checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .`: 322 files already formatted.
- `pytest -q` (full suite): 3773 passed, 7 skipped, 40 deselected.
- `pytest recipes/41-approval-scope-review -q`: 55 passed.
- `pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -q -k 41`: 14 passed, 599 deselected (no allowlist entry).
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/41-approval-scope-review`: fixtures valid
  (mode replay).
- `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/41-approval-scope-review` under the pinned
  constraints, run twice: `git diff --stat` empty both times (byte-identical reproduction).
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` over every tracked file in the recipe folder: passed, 9 files
  scanned.
- `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD`: only `recipes/41-approval-scope-review/**` paths,
  every mode `100644`, no rename or deletion out of scope.

## Report

**The safety-asymmetry property.** `check_binding` takes no model-answer argument; `decide`
calls it first and returns `DENIED` unconditionally on refusal, before `decide_labels` is ever
called. Proved exhaustively: a breakpoint-exact grid (13 × 13 = 169 points per case, built from
the frozen thresholds and gate — every value where a business threshold or either edge of the
confidence-gate band can flip the outcome, with one point strictly below, at, and strictly above
each) swept over 8 synthetic binding-failure cases (each of the 6 independent reasons, plus one
with all 6 at once) — 1,352 (case, point) combinations, all `DENIED` — and separately over all
14 real committed denied fixtures at the same grid, all `DENIED`. `tests/test_helpers.py` adds a
dense 201×201 (40,401-point) grid over those same 14 real fixtures (565,614 evaluations) as a
second, independent sweep. **What failed when the composition was broken:** a test-only mutant,
`_broken_decide`, checks the model's two propositions *before* the binding and executes whenever
both read confidently clear, never calling `check_binding` in that branch. On the wrong-citation
case with the most favourable possible answer (both propositions at 0.02), the real composition
still returns `DENIED` and the mutant returns `EXECUTED`;
`test_the_safety_asymmetry_property_test_is_not_vacuous_a_broken_composition_fails_it` asserts
`_property_holds(helpers.decide, ...)` is `True` and `_property_holds(_broken_decide, ...)` is
`False` over the identical sweep — the assertion that goes red under the mutation is the
`_property_holds(_broken_decide, ...) is False` line (equivalently, swapping `_broken_decide`
into the main exhaustive test makes its `assert result.outcome == helpers.DENIED` fail on the
wrong-citation case).

**Four quantities, and the cohort comparison.** Input rows per split: 15 `validation`, 15
`test` (cohort range measured from committed fixtures across the published set: 12–81, an
**input-row** range, not comparable to a question count). Requests per split: 15 each — one
`decide` call per row, what the live budget bills and `len(responses.json)` counts. Questions
per split: 30 each, since every request carries two independent propositions
(`intent_mismatch`, `scope_creep`) together. Task-level units per split: 15 each, one outcome
per row from `helpers.decide`. Rows, requests and units coincide here (no grouping, one
request per row); questions do not, because this recipe sends two propositions per request —
exactly the shape that makes the four worth keeping separate rather than one number.

**Gate vs. `|2t − 1|`, and the counterfactual.** Business thresholds (F1, `validation`):
`t_intent = 0.6000`, `t_scope = 0.8800`. `|2·0.6 − 1| = 0.2000`; `|2·0.88 − 1| = 0.7600`. Frozen
gate (`min_coverage=0.6`, pooled): `0.8400`, strictly greater than both bounds — **not inert**
for either proposition; equivalent to a stricter pair of cut-offs, `0.0800` and `0.9200`,
replacing each threshold's single one. Counterfactual on `validation` (gate forced to `0.0`,
everything else frozen): coverage rises `0.5333 → 0.6000`; accuracy and risk are unchanged
(`1.0000` / `0.0000` either way on this split).

**The `min_coverage` sweep.** Swept across its full `[0, 1]` range (0.00, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.65,
0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 1.00): three distinct gates (`0.8800`, `0.8400`, `0.0400`), monotonically
non-increasing as `min_coverage` rises — confirms the selector is not a no-op and that raising
`min_coverage` admits more answers and selects a *lower* threshold, the direction three recipes
have stated backwards before.

**Every threshold's two pin sites.** `t_intent`/`t_scope`: (1) `tests/test_helpers.py::
test_the_frozen_business_thresholds_and_gate_are_pinned_to_their_values` (value), (2)
`test_notebook_pins_f1_as_the_business_threshold_objective_for_both_propositions`, which parses
the committed notebook's code-cell source for `objective="f1"` (keyword) appearing exactly twice
and asserts `"target_accuracy"` is absent. Gate: (1) the same value-pin test
(`0.8400000000000001`), (2) `test_notebook_pins_min_coverage_not_target_accuracy_for_the_gate`,
which parses the committed source for the literal `"min_coverage=0.6"`. I did not ship a
permanent "mutate the notebook text" test for these (the committed source IS the thing being
parsed, so there is nothing to mutate independently of editing the recipe itself); I verified by
hand that changing either the keyword or the value in a scratch copy of the notebook source
breaks the corresponding assertion, and that changing only the `tests/test_helpers.py` pinned
float (not the notebook) breaks the value-pin test alone — two different assertions, confirmed
to go red independently.

**Costs beside every accuracy.** `test` split, 15 actions: mechanism (this recipe) — coverage
`0.6667`, accuracy `0.9000`, risk `0.1000`, 15 requests. `permission_only` baseline (enforces
binding only, no model) — coverage `1.0000`, accuracy `0.6667`, risk `0.3333`, 0 requests.
`always_review` baseline (refuses a bad binding, never auto-executes otherwise) — coverage
`0.4667`, accuracy `1.0000`, risk `0.0000`, 0 requests. Two of those three baseline numbers
are structural, not measured: `always_review` accepts exactly the actions `check_binding`
refuses, and `gold_outcome` returns `denied` for exactly those same actions via the same
function, so its accuracy and risk cannot come out any other way for any gold labelling;
`permission_only` never reviews, so its coverage cannot either. Neither baseline dominates the
mechanism on coverage and risk together, which is true but says less than it looks like given
that. The sharper, decision-level comparison: beyond what `always_review` would ever
auto-execute (nothing), the mechanism auto-executes 3 actions (2 right, 1 wrong); against
`permission_only`, the model's two propositions cut wrong auto-executions from 5 to 1, at the
cost of one correct auto-execution held back for review instead of granted automatically
(`t06-lookalike`).

**Rule-13-style sweeps, and how each check was validated to be able to produce a hit.** (1) No
issue-citation sweep (`grep`-equivalent `re` scan for `#[0-9]+`, `issue`, `wave N`, `the
reviewer`, `the orchestrator`, `cell id`, case-insensitive) over every recipe file and every
notebook markdown cell: zero hits; validated by running the identical pattern against a planted
string containing each token, which matched all of them. (2) A numeral-cross-check of every bare
metric quoted in this report and in the notebook's markdown against the committed code-cell
output: all traced to a specific printed line (not merely "a number appearing somewhere" — each
was matched with enough surrounding context, per the coincidental-match lesson, to the specific
cell that establishes it). (3) The byte-identical re-execution (above) was run twice, and I
additionally confirmed the second run's `git diff --stat` was empty rather than trusting the exit
code alone.

**Figure count per cell.** The notebook commits one `image/png` output, in cell
`eval-frontier`: the `test`-split coverage/risk frontier across the mechanism and both
zero-request baselines (`plot_risk_coverage`), with each point annotated. The `print`s in that
cell precede the `plot_risk_coverage` call, so the figure is the cell's last expression and is
the committed result. The rest of the recipe's content (binding refusal, a composed
three-outcome decision, an exhaustive discrete sweep) stays tabular, which is the right call
for that data; the one place a chart earns its keep is the three-way coverage/risk comparison
this figure now shows.

**The single `get_backend` call site.** `notebook.ipynb`, cell `setup`:
`backend = get_backend(fixtures=responses_path())` — called exactly once, with an inline
comment marking it as such. Every request after that goes through a notebook-local `ask()`
wrapper that appends to `request_log` on every attempt (never deduplicated by id); the
`measured` cell asserts `len(request_log) == len(set(request_log)) == len(load_responses()) ==
len(examples)` (35 == 35 == 35 == 35), so a double-decide on any id would be caught by the first
equality, not hidden by a dict keyed on id.

**Out-of-scope finding.** Nothing found in shared code or convention that needed working around.
One minor thing worth naming for whoever next scaffolds a Level-4 recipe: `tools/new_recipe.py`'s
scaffold leaves `tests/test_helpers.py`'s placeholder `test_questions_are_built_by_python` and a
placeholder `helpers.py`/`build_fixtures.py` with no guidance that a *second* independent
`Noul`-proposition recipe (two questions in one request) needs its `answers_for`/`ROWS` shape
designed around a `(p1, p2)` tuple per row rather than the single-probability shape the template
comment implies — I worked this out from recipe 26's own `build_fixtures.py` rather than from
any scaffold hint. Not a defect, just something a future scaffold improvement could shorten.

**PR number and head SHA:** filled in by `gh pr create`'s own output; head SHA at the time of
opening is `93ab6f8e5f84d6fefec9df307ac6690c0d09210a`.

title: Recipe 40: Hierarchical classification
body:
Closes #40

## What this adds

`recipes/40-hierarchical-classification/`: a two-level taxonomy recipe. Jev answers a `department`
`Choice` (three real departments plus the use case's `unclassified` fallback) and, for a real
department, a `topic` `Choice` scoped to that department's own topics. `helpers.resolve_path`
composes the two stages: when the department answer's own confidence clears a frozen
`branch_margin`, it commits to the single top-ranked department (greedy); otherwise it carries the
top two real departments forward, asks a topic question for each, and scores every candidate full
path — including the fallback, always a candidate at no extra request — as
`department_probability * topic_probability`. `helpers.gate_path` then accepts the winning path
only when that composite confidence clears a second, independent `review_gate`, sending anything
below it to review.

The notebook reports leaf accuracy (exact `department.topic` match) and request count for this
policy against the two baselines the issue names: the greedy single path (the same
`resolve_path`, with branching turned off) and a flat classifier that asks one combined question
per document. It also reports department-level accuracy separately from full-path leaf accuracy
(they disagree on one real test fixture), and a deliberate "shared topic name" trap: two
departments share a bare topic name, and one test fixture is confidently assigned to the wrong
department under that shared name, which only a full-path comparison (not a bare-topic-name one)
catches.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/40-hierarchical-classification/` (verified: no other path
  changes; the generated README regions are the integration worker's job, not this branch's)
- [ ] README regenerated — not applicable to this branch; the generated-README exception means the
  integration worker does this later in the same pull request, and `Catalog (README is current)`
  is expected to be red until then
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/40-hierarchical-classification/`
  paths, every mode `100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which mode
  it ran in
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (branching rescues, the shared-topic-name
  trap, a within-department mistake, a genuinely unclear case sent to review), and carry gold
  labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (`ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue`)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels, with both baselines the issue names (greedy single path,
  flat classifier), request counts included
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met

## Decisions

- **Four requests per example, not one.** Every document's fixtures store a `department` answer,
  a `topic` answer for each of the two real departments its own department probabilities rank
  highest, and a `flat_topic` answer for the flat baseline — regardless of whether the frozen
  policy actually explores both departments on a given document. This keeps the comparison fair
  (greedy, branching and flat all see the identical underlying model answers for every document)
  and keeps the live-call budget exact: this notebook's own `decide()` call counter
  (`_requests["n"]`, printed in "What was and was not measured") totals exactly 124, equal to
  `len(fixtures/responses.json)`. The *policy's* own request count (`ResolvedPath.requests`,
  1–3 depending on branching) is reported separately and is the honest per-deployment figure; it
  is lower than 124 because a deployed policy does not fetch what it does not need.
- **`branch_margin` and `review_gate` are two independent `select_confidence_threshold` calls**,
  not one threshold reused twice. `branch_margin` is chosen from department-level correctness and
  confidence on `validation` (`min_coverage=0.65`); `review_gate` is chosen one stage later, from
  full-path leaf correctness and the composed path confidence on `validation`, after resolving
  every validation path with `branch_margin` already frozen (`min_coverage=0.75`). Both are pinned
  two ways: the exact value each produces on the real fixtures
  (`test_the_threshold_objectives_are_pinned`), and the exact keyword text in the committed
  notebook cell (`test_the_notebooks_threshold_objectives_match_this_files_pinned_keywords`,
  parsing the notebook JSON directly, following the pattern recipe 37 uses). I proved both halves
  are load-bearing by mutation (see "How it was verified").
- **The headline metric compares full paths, never bare topic names**, because two departments
  share a bare topic name (`general_question`) on purpose. `t13-shared-name-trap` is built so the
  policy confidently lands on the wrong department whose own topic happens to share that bare
  name with the correct answer; `accuracy` over full paths scores it wrong, and a bare-name-only
  comparison (computed in the notebook purely to show the contrast, never as this recipe's metric)
  would have scored it right. `tests/test_helpers.py::test_the_shared_topic_name_would_be_a_false_match_on_a_real_fixture`
  proves this divergence on that real fixture.
- **Greedy is `resolve_path` with `branch_margin=0.0`**, not a second implementation. Confidence
  is never below 0, so this parametrisation never branches, which is exactly the single-path
  baseline the issue names, covered by the same tests as the branching policy.
- **`unclassified` is never gated as an exemption.** It is a real, scored candidate in every
  `resolve_path` call (CONTRIBUTING.md section 4 part (a)–(c) would let it qualify, the same shape
  recipe 38's `insufficient_information` and the template's `none` already discuss), but this
  recipe gates it through the same `review_gate` as everything else rather than claim the
  exemption — recipe 38's own choice, reused here.

## How it was verified

```bash
# from the repository root, inside a venv with `.[dev,ml]` installed under the notebook constraints
uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt

python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/40-hierarchical-classification
# -> recipes/40-hierarchical-classification: fixtures valid (mode replay)

python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/40-hierarchical-classification
# -> 40-hierarchical-classification: executed notebook.ipynb offline
# (run twice; `git diff --stat -- recipes/40-hierarchical-classification/notebook.ipynb` was
# empty after `git add`, confirming byte-identical re-execution)

pytest recipes/40-hierarchical-classification
# -> 34 passed

pytest -q
# -> 3752 passed, 7 skipped, 40 deselected

pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k "40-hierarchical" -q
# -> 14 passed (every non-catalog-audit check this recipe guard runs)

ruff check .
ruff format --check .
# -> All checks passed. / 322 files already formatted.

python tools/check_hygiene.py
# -> Hygiene check passed: 466 file(s) scanned.

python tools/render_catalog.py --check
# -> README.md is out of date. Run: python tools/render_catalog.py
# Expected red: the generated-README exception means the integration worker regenerates it in
# this same pull request, never the recipe builder.

# from a checkout of this branch, so gh infers which pull request to read:
gh pr view --json body --jq .body > /tmp/pr-body.txt
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --branch recipe/40-hierarchical-classification --body-file /tmp/pr-body.txt
# -> scope ok: recipe pull request for #40 (40-hierarchical-classification): 9 changed paths
# (re-run against the final head if the branch gets another commit)
```

Threshold-objective mutation proofs (each reverted afterward, not committed):

- Swapping the notebook's `min_coverage=branch_min_coverage` keyword for `target_accuracy=1.0`
  turns `test_the_notebooks_threshold_objectives_match_this_files_pinned_keywords` red while
  `test_the_threshold_objectives_are_pinned` stays green (it re-derives independently of the
  notebook's own text).
- Changing the pinned value in `tests/test_helpers.py`
  (`branch_margin == pytest.approx(0.7866666666666666)` to `pytest.approx(0.5)`) turns
  `test_the_threshold_objectives_are_pinned` red while the keyword-text test stays green.
- Changing the notebook's own `branch_min_coverage = 0.65` literal to `0.85` turns the
  keyword-text test red (it pins the value text too, not only the keyword).
- Swapping the review objective's keyword the same way turns the same keyword-text test red at
  its `review_min_coverage` assertion specifically.

Independent-consequence proofs, on real committed fixtures (`tests/test_helpers.py`):

- `test_branching_rescues_a_real_fixture_greedy_gets_wrong` (parametrised over `t11`/`t12`):
  flipping only the branch decision (greedy vs. the frozen `branch_margin`) changes the
  composed outcome from wrong to right on both real fixtures.
- `test_the_shared_topic_name_would_be_a_false_match_on_a_real_fixture`: comparing full paths vs.
  bare topic names disagrees about `t13` on real data.
- `test_a_department_correct_fixture_can_still_have_the_wrong_full_path`: `t15` has its
  department right and its full path wrong, the per-level/end-to-end divergence the notebook
  reports separately.
- `test_the_notebooks_pooled_evaluation_lists_share_one_unreordered_source`: the notebook's
  `evaluation-test` cell pools four lists over the test split (`test_gold`, `test_resolved`,
  `test_greedy`, `test_flat`) and the rest of the evaluation section indexes all four in
  parallel. This test parses the committed cell's own source (not a reconstruction with its
  own comprehensions) and pins that each list is built directly over `test_examples` or
  `test_fetched` with no reordering. Proof by mutation: reversing the notebook's own
  `test_gold` comprehension (`reversed(test_examples)`) reddens only this assertion; a fix-
  round review found that an earlier version of this test, which rebuilt the lists with its
  own comprehensions, stayed green under that same mutation because it held `doc_id`
  alignment by construction rather than checking the notebook's real source.

Figure count: 3 `plot_*` calls, 3 cells, 1 `image/png` output per cell (`answer-plot`,
`evaluation-curve`, `evaluation-matrix`) — checked directly against the committed notebook JSON,
not assumed.

`get_backend` is called exactly once, in the `setup` cell; every request in every later cell
reuses that one `backend` object through a counting `decide()` wrapper.

Unfinished: nothing. The one expected-red check is `Catalog (README is current)`, per the
generated-README exception in CONTRIBUTING.md — not a defect in this branch.

title: Foundation: wave 3 close-out inbound-link sweep
body:
Refs #163
Refs #214

## What this adds

Wave 3 close-out: the inbound-link sweep `docs/development.md` and `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`
describe as a by-hand audit after a wave's recipes all publish. `G1(f)` clause 2 requires every
published recipe to be the target of at least one other published recipe's "Next steps". The
check is `test_every_recipe_is_linked_from_some_other_recipes_next_steps`, marked
`catalog_audit` and deselected from the default run, because a new recipe's own pull request can
never satisfy it (no recipe may link forward to one not yet published, and a recipe PR may only
touch its own folder).

Measured on `main` at `5caf98f`, eleven recipes had zero inbound links: `28-skill-selection`,
`30-citation-verification`, `31-patch-risk-triage`, `32-regression-test-selection`,
`33-schema-field-mapping`, `34-evidence-relationship-labels`, `35-semantic-feature-extraction`,
`36-card-game-action-selection`, `37-research-domain-tagging`, `38-abstention-and-review-queues`,
`39-document-extraction-cascade`.

This PR adds exactly one new "Next steps" link to each of those eleven, from a different,
already-published, already-public recipe — one link per source, spread across eleven distinct
sources so no single recipe gains more than one new outbound link. **Nothing else changes**:
every edit is confined to the existing `## Next steps` markdown cell of the source notebook
(`next-md` or `next-steps`, per recipe), adding one clause or bullet to the existing
"Neighbouring recipes" sentence. No code cell, no fixture, no helper, no test, no README, and no
shared code changed anywhere.

This is a sweep PR on already-published recipes, not a recipe PR: branch
`sweep/wave3-inbound-links`, closing no recipe issue (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s scope rule and
`BUILDER_RULES.md`'s "Sweep PRs on published recipes" section). It references #163 (the
foundation-sweep tracker) and #214 (which tracks this wave-3 inbound-link audit).

## The eleven source → target pairs, with the reason for each

| # | source (gains the new link) | target (gains its first inbound link) | why this jump |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `17-passage-reranking` | `28-skill-selection` | Both score a retrieved candidate on a graded relevance rubric; 28 is the same `Score` pattern applied to skill descriptions instead of passages, and sends an unresolved task to the same `review` outcome 17's confidence gate sends a low-confidence score to — reached there by a business-cutoff-and-margin check, not a confidence gate, which 28's own evaluation shows would be inert on its task. |
| 2 | `20-claim-support-classification` | `30-citation-verification` | 20's own notebook already cites TypeSafe's citation-checking cookbook as the source of its `relation` question; 30 is that exact pattern applied specifically to a claim and its cited passage, after Python resolves the citation identifier. |
| 3 | `19-ci-failure-classification` | `31-patch-risk-triage` | 19 diagnoses why a build failed; 31 is the next step a team actually takes once a build fails for a code reason — triaging whether the patch that caused it is risky enough to need closer review before merging. |
| 4 | `31-patch-risk-triage` | `32-regression-test-selection` | Both are about one patch. Once 31 flags a patch risky, 32 is "which tests should I actually run" — scoring candidate tests against the behavior the patch changed. |
| 5 | `22-cmdb-asset-matching` | `33-schema-field-mapping` | Same shape: map a differently-worded description to a fixed, canonical target (a CMDB record vs. a schema field), each with its own no-match-shaped fallback (`no_match` vs. `ambiguous`/`unmapped`). |
| 6 | `25-change-evidence-review` | `34-evidence-relationship-labels` | Both are evidence-sufficiency judgments. 25 asks "is there enough evidence for this change"; 34 narrows the same habit to "what specific relationship does this one passage of evidence support." |
| 7 | `06-multiple-topic-labels` | `35-semantic-feature-extraction` | Identical decision shape — several independent `Noul` propositions over one piece of text, sent together. 35 takes that same battery and feeds the resulting feature vector into a trained classifier instead of a per-label threshold. |
| 8 | `27-function-selection` | `36-card-game-action-selection` | Same catalog-`Choice`-with-validation shape; 36 puts it inside a running simulator, enumerating only the actions legal on a given turn instead of a fixed function catalog. |
| 9 | `15-sensitive-text-triage` | `37-research-domain-tagging` | Both share the same `noul_confidence` gate sending an unconfident answer to `review` instead of a forced guess; 37 applies it across three independent domain propositions behind one shared gate, and adds its own further filter 15 has no counterpart to — access control deciding, before any request is built, whether a passage reaches Jev at all. |
| 10 | `04-support-ticket-routing` | `38-abstention-and-review-queues` | 38's own README calls itself "a support ticket router that can abstain" — it echoes 04's `unclear_request` fallback with its own `insufficient_information` fallback (the same never-routed-automatically shape) and a validation-chosen confidence threshold, built out into a whole router organized around abstaining to review. |
| 11 | `14-source-span-selection` | `39-document-extraction-cascade` | Both pick a candidate span or say the field is absent (`not_stated` / `not_found`). 39 adds the next stage: verifying the chosen span really states the field before accepting it. |

Each source was chosen to motivate a genuine next read (not "see also recipe N"), and no two
pairs share a source, so the eleven new links are spread across eleven different recipes rather
than piling onto one or two.

## Protocol followed

- Cut from `origin/main` at `5caf98f` (`git rev-parse origin/main`).
- Verified the starting eleven-recipe set myself before acting, with a small script reading
  every published recipe's notebook JSON directly (not relying on the issue's list) and applying
  the exact `](../NN-slug/)` pattern `tests/test_recipe_guard.py::NEIGHBOUR_LINK` uses, scanning
  markdown cells only, excluding self-links and `_template`. Self-tested the pattern first
  against a planted link string before trusting its silence on the real tree (see "How it was
  verified").
- Every edit is a `next-md`/`next-steps` markdown-cell `source` replacement only. Verified with
  `git diff --raw` that every changed path is `100644 → 100644`, no symlink, rename, or deletion,
  and with a cell-by-cell JSON diff (see below) that no code cell's `source`, `outputs`, or
  `execution_count` changed in any of the eleven files, and that every notebook's cell-id list
  and order is byte-identical before and after.
- Re-executed all eleven touched notebooks offline, from a clean kernel, under the pinned
  constraints (`.[ml] -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`, matching `notebooks.yml`), and
  diffed the result against the pre-execution committed file: byte-identical in every case,
  including every `image/png` output. A markdown-only edit cannot change a code cell's output by
  construction (the code and fixtures are untouched), and the clean-kernel run confirms it
  empirically as well, not only structurally.
- No fixture, helper, or shared code changed, so there was nothing new for the shared evaluation
  helpers to recompute; the existing recipe-local tests (part of the full suite below) already
  cover that every reported figure in each touched recipe still comes from `helpers.py` and the
  committed fixtures, unchanged.
- Ran the fixture validator across the whole catalog (`--all`): all 39 recipes plus `_template`
  valid.

## Decisions

- Chose `sweep/wave3-inbound-links` as the branch name per this task's own brief, not
  `foundation/<topic>`; `tools/check_recipe_scope.py`'s allowlist only ever applies to a branch
  literally named `recipe/<slug>` with a `Closes #N` body, so any other branch name — this one
  included — is classified as a non-recipe (foundation-equivalent) pull request for `Scope`
  purposes regardless of its specific prefix.
- Added each new link as a new bullet or trailing clause onto the source's existing
  "Neighbouring recipes" sentence, never replacing or shortening an existing link — nothing
  already there was redundant with what was added.
- Picked eleven distinct sources (no repeats) so the new links read as individually-motivated
  jumps rather than one or two recipes becoming link hubs; `31-patch-risk-triage` is both a
  target (from 19) and a source (to 32), which is allowed and reads naturally — it is the real
  midpoint of a two-step "a build fails → the patch is risky → which tests to run" chain.
- Did not touch the root `README.md`; this sweep does not touch the catalog, so
  `render_catalog.py --check` needed no re-run beyond the confirmation below.

## Results: before and after

`pytest -m catalog_audit tests/test_recipe_guard.py`, the wave close-out audit this sweep exists
to make green (run on the pre-sweep commit, `5caf98f`, and then again on this PR's head):

- **Before:** `11 failed, 28 passed, 559 deselected in 0.21s` — the eleven recipes named above, by
  name, in the failure list.
- **After:** `39 passed, 559 deselected in 0.09s` — all 39 recipes now pass.

(The `559 deselected` figure is the same in both runs: it is `test_recipe_guard.py`'s own count
of every *other* parametrised case in that one file, not evidence of anything about this check on
its own — see the module's docstring on why a bare deselected count must never be read as a pass
count.)

Full default suite (`pytest -q`, no marker — this is also what per-PR CI runs), on both legs:

title: Recipe 36: Card-game action selection
body:
Closes #36

## What this adds

`recipes/36-card-game-action-selection/`: a seeded two-player card game ("Card Duel", `helpers.CardDuel`, a `jev_cookbook.simulation.Simulator`). Each turn Python enumerates exactly the cards left in the player's hand and offers them as a fixed-description `Choice`; the simulator rejects any answer outside that set. A confidence gate (`helpers.gate_turn`) decides whether to trust the model's own choice or substitute a rule-based action, and `helpers.play_game` composes many such turns into one task-level win/lose/tie outcome. This is a scripted/simulator recipe (`jev_cookbook.ScriptedBackend`, no stored responses) scaffolded with `python tools/new_recipe.py 36 --mode scripted`.

Evaluation is reported two ways, kept explicitly apart because they are over two different quantities:

- **Per question** (one scored example per decided turn: 40 validation turns across 10 seeded games, 56 test turns across 14 seeded games): accuracy of the model's raw choice against a rule-based reference action, a confidence gate chosen on `validation` with `select_confidence_threshold(..., min_coverage=0.75)` and reported on `test` with `evaluate_selective` (coverage 0.7143, accuracy 0.9250, risk 0.0750 — non-zero by construction, see "How it was verified" below), a confusion matrix over all five possible bids, and a risk-coverage curve.
- **Task level** (one unit per seeded game: 10 validation + 14 test games): every seeded game played end to end under four policies — the random legal policy, the rule-based policy, the confidence-gated model policy, and (shown only as a counterfactual disclosing what the gate buys, never as a third baseline) the same model policy left ungated — reporting win/loss/tie and mean score for each, plus an independent replay-based proof that none of the 480 validation- and test-game actions played across all four policies was ever illegal.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/36-card-game-action-selection/` (verified: `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only paths under that folder; `tools/check_recipe_scope.py` passes — see below)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` — **not applicable to this builder**: per the generated-README exception, the integration worker regenerates it inside this same pull request after this branch is handed over; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until then
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (`tools/execute_notebook.py` strips `JEV_COOKBOOK_*`/`TYPESAFE_*`; executed twice, byte-identical the second time)
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions (`get_backend` reads `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE` and, when set, builds a live backend around the same `build_state`/`build_questions`; `get_backend` is called exactly once, in the setup cell)
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance; the notebook states which mode it ran in — **no `responses.json` exists** (scripted recipe; `helpers.script`'s answers are always `synthetic`, stated in the run header and the "What was and was not measured" section)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference (every reported number carries a `check` suffix; the rule-based baseline's constant win rate against the fixed opponent is explicitly disclosed as structural, not a result)
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases, and carry gold labels (the hard case this use case names is the single-remaining-card forced turn, where Python resolves directly without a `Choice`, per `docs/backends.md`'s "Single-option Choice"; every scored turn's gold label is the rule-based action, independently re-derived from its own committed fields in `tests/test_helpers.py`)
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (`CardDuel.step` is the only place a card is "played"; nothing outside the simulator is touched)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels, with the baseline the issue names (random legal policy and rule-based policy, both over the committed seeded games)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

### Acceptance criteria, checked against evidence

- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, outputs committed — executed twice with `tools/execute_notebook.py`; `git diff --stat` empty after the second run
- [x] Live mode is opt-in and uses the same question definitions — see above; README's "Switch to live" states the real call count (290) a live run would make
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases, carry gold labels, pass the validator — `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/36-card-game-action-selection` → `fixtures valid (mode scripted)`
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance, notebook states mode — scripted recipe, no stored responses; run header and "measured" cell both state `scripted`
- [x] Evaluation: win rate over seeded games against both baselines, zero illegal actions — task-level cell reports win/loss/tie and win rate for the random and rule-based baselines plus the model's gated policy on `validation` and `test`; the `evaluation-task-zero-illegal` cell independently replays every one of 480 validation- and test-game actions (across all four policies) through `Simulator.replay` (which re-checks legality from scratch) and asserts the count
- [x] Deterministic composition lives in a Python function with tests — `helpers.play_game`, tested in `tests/test_helpers.py` (composition regression pin, illegal-action rejection, replay reproducibility)
- [x] Evaluation is at task level, not only per question — both the per-turn (`evaluation-validation`/`evaluation-test`/`evaluation-matrix`/`evaluation-risk-coverage`) and task-level (`evaluation-task-games`/`evaluation-task-zero-illegal`) cells are present and clearly separated by which quantity (turns vs. games) each is over
- [x] No statement about Jev's quality/latency/cost without recorded live inference; synthetic metrics labelled as checks — every reported number carries `{check}`; `validation` numbers also carry `{selection}`
- [x] README says what it teaches, how to run it, what was/was not measured live — see README sections
- [x] PR changes only the recipe folder and CI is green — scope check passes locally; full local `pytest` (3552 passed, 7 skipped, 36 deselected), `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` all clean on this head; `Catalog (README is current)` is the one check expected red (generated-README exception)

## Decisions

- **Game design.** "Card Duel": both sides hold cards 1..5; a hidden, seeded prize-order deck is revealed one card per turn; higher bid wins the prize as points, a tie wins nothing. The fixed opponent bids the card closest in value to the prize (ties to the higher card), deterministically from its own remaining hand — never from the player's actions — so every policy this recipe compares sees an identical opponent and prize sequence for a given seed.
- **No fabricated `fallback`/`none` option.** The issue's boilerplate decision-design line ("including the fallback outcome this use case names") does not name one explicitly for this recipe, and there is no natural "no suitable bid" case: a legal hand always has at least one card. The recipe's actual analogue is CONTRIBUTING's own "Single-option Choice" rule: when exactly one card remains, Python resolves it directly without building a question, which is the single-option forced-resolution mechanism the contract already specifies for this shape of case. I did not invent an unneeded option to satisfy boilerplate wording literally.
- **The confidence gate's fallback, not a deferral.** On a low-confidence turn, Python plays the rule-based action instead of the model's own pick (a card game cannot skip a turn) and records the turn for [review] with the reason `"confidence below the threshold"`. This is a confidence-only rule (the gate is the only review branch), so `evaluate_selective` describes it exactly, and the strong-form test in `tests/test_helpers.py` re-derives the threshold independently with the same `min_coverage=0.75` keyword the notebook freezes it with.
- **Per-turn examples come from a canonical rule-based rollout.** Each seeded game's fixture rows are generated by rolling the rule-based policy forward once; the gold label at each turn is exactly what that rollout played there. The model's raw choice is then scored against that same state (teacher-forced accuracy). The task-level section is a *separate* simulation: each policy plays its own full game from scratch, so a model-driven policy's later turns can see different hand states than the fixture rollout whenever its earlier choices diverge from the rule-based reference.
- **The rule-based baseline's win rate (and score) is disclosed as structural, not reported as a comparison.** Against the fixed opponent, the rule-based policy wins every seeded game in this notebook (and, in a wider, uncommitted sweep of 500 additional seeds I ran locally while designing the recipe, every one of those too) with an identical final score every time. This is a property of the two fixed strategies, not of which seed was drawn, and the notebook and README both say so next to the number rather than presenting it as if it varied. The model's gated policy (14-0 on `test`, mean score 9.57 vs. the baseline's constant 10.00) and the random policy (0-14-0) are the two real, falsifiable comparisons.
- **The "ungated model policy" is shown but is not one of the two baselines.** It exists only to disclose what the confidence gate buys (win rate 0.50 vs. the gated policy's 1.00 on `test`), and the notebook and README both say explicitly that it is not a baseline, to avoid it being read as a third required comparison.
- **A directional claim in an early draft was false and is fixed.** Before opening this pull request I checked every comparative/directional sentence in the notebook's markdown against the committed output, not only every bare number. One sentence read "several right turns miss [the gate] (sent to review even though the raw choice was correct)" — checking it directly against the committed `test` data showed this never happens on this fixture set (every turn the confidence gate holds back is, in fact, wrong; the gate's whole printed risk comes from 3 confidently-wrong turns that still clear it). The sentence is corrected in `evaluation-note-md` to state exactly that, verified against the committed numbers. The same pass also caught the task-level section undercounting its own policies ("three policies" in three places, when the cells build and report four) and the zero-illegal-actions replay check covering only `test`'s games while a neighbouring cell claimed it covered "every turn this notebook actually played" — both fixed (the replay check now covers `validation` and `test` alike, 480 actions across both splits and all four policies).

## Unfinished / open questions

- Nothing left unfinished in this recipe. One design question for a reviewer: the task-level section's two model-driven policies call the backend far more than the per-turn evaluation does (290 live calls in total if run live), because playing out whole games under a policy that decides its own turns necessarily visits states beyond the ones the per-turn fixtures score. I considered capping `VALIDATION_SEEDS`/`TEST_SEEDS` lower to shrink that live-call count, but kept 10 and 14 games (consistent with this wave's examples/units sizing) and disclosed the real number in the README instead of understating it.
- **Out-of-scope finding (not fixed here, no issue filed):** `src/jev_cookbook/simulation.py`'s `Simulator` base class is otherwise exactly the right fit for this recipe and needed no changes. I did not find anything missing from the shared simulation or evaluation toolkits for this recipe's needs.

## How it was verified

```bash
uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
uv pip install -e ".[ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt   # exact stack the Notebook job installs

python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/36-card-game-action-selection
# -> recipes/36-card-game-action-selection: fixtures valid (mode scripted)

python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/36-card-game-action-selection
git diff --stat -- recipes/36-card-game-action-selection   # empty: a second run changes nothing

ruff check .
ruff format --check .
pytest -q
# -> 3552 passed, 7 skipped, 36 deselected

pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k "36-card-game-action-selection" -rX -q
# -> 11 passed, 3 skipped (the skips are the build_fixtures_scaffold/stored_answers_strong_form/
#    readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers checks, which skip by design for a scripted
#    recipe with no fixtures/responses.json); no xfail entries

python tools/render_catalog.py --check
# -> "README.md is out of date" (exit 1) -- expected and not fixed here; the generated-README
```

title: Recipe 39: Document extraction cascade
body:
Closes #39

## What this adds

`recipes/39-document-extraction-cascade/`: a two-stage extraction cascade over a short purchase
document with two fields, `invoice_number` and `total_amount`.

- **Stage 1** (one request): a `Choice` per field with at least one candidate span (Python's own
  deterministic extractor, `helpers.extract_candidates`), plus the shared `not_found` fallback.
  The two fields' `Choice` questions are independent of each other and travel together in one
  request.
- **Stage 2** (a later request, built only from stage 1's own answers): a `Noul` per field stage
  1 named a real candidate for, verifying the selection against its own source text. A field's
  `Noul` instructions are fixed text; the candidate being verified lives in the state, not the
  instructions. The two fields' stage-2 propositions are independent of each other and travel
  together, bundled, whenever more than one field reaches stage 2.
- `helpers.plan_requests` makes the request boundary a printed value (`notebook.ipynb`,
  "The request boundary"), not only a rule taken on faith: three documents are shown making all
  three shapes this takes (two requests bundling two fields each; zero requests; two requests
  where the second bundles only one field, because the other field's stage-1 answer was
  `not_found`).
- Python composes a field result (`not_found`, `extracted`, or sent to review for being
  **uncertain** — confidence below the gate — or **inconsistent** — verification below the
  business threshold) and then a document result (`accepted` only when neither field is in
  review). Both composition functions are in `helpers.py`
  (`compose_document_outcome`/`finalize_field`) with tests.
- Evaluation is reported at both levels the acceptance criteria name: **field-level** (one row
  per (document, field) pair — field-level accuracy, review rate, error rate among records not
  sent to review) and **task-level** (one row per document — accepted/correct over the composed
  outcome).

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/39-document-extraction-cascade/` (the generated README
      regions are for the integration worker, not this PR)
- [ ] README regenerated — not applicable to this PR; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected
      red until the integration worker runs `tools/render_catalog.py` against current `main`
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/39-document-extraction-cascade/`
      paths, all mode `100644`, no symlink, rename, or deletion out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions (README, "Switch to live")
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which
      mode it ran in (the run header, and the "What was and was not measured" cell)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (decoys of every kind, full and partial
      no-match, an explicit `not_found` choice over a present decoy, two verification mistakes
      in each direction, and the one confidently-wrong-and-unverified error the frozen gate
      does not catch), and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (nothing is simulated at all: this
      recipe only extracts and verifies, no container of any kind)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels; the issue names no baseline to compare against
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network, and its outputs
      are committed — executed with `tools/execute_notebook.py`, outputs committed, reproduced
      byte-identically on a second execution (modulo one Unicode-escaping artifact from my own
      manual text edit between the two runs, corrected by the second run to the tool's own
      canonical form — not a reproducibility gap in the tool's own output).
- [x] Live mode is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` with `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same
      question definitions as the offline run — `get_backend` is the only place the backend is
      chosen, called exactly once in the notebook.
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases named in the build notes, carry gold
      labels, and pass the fixture validator — `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate
      recipes/39-document-extraction-cascade` passes.
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance, and the notebook states which mode it ran
      in — every stored answer is `Provenance.synthetic()`; the run header and the "measured"
      cell both state the mode.
- [x] Evaluation: Field-level accuracy, the review rate, and the error rate among records not
      sent to review — printed in "Field-level evaluation" as coverage/accuracy/risk from
      `evaluate_outcomes`, for both splits.
- [x] The deterministic composition lives in a Python function with tests —
      `compose_document_outcome`/`finalize_field`/`field_result`/`decide_document` in
      `helpers.py`, tested in `tests/test_helpers.py`.
- [x] Evaluation is at task level, not only per question — "Task-level evaluation" reports
      document-level coverage/accuracy/risk separately from the field-level numbers.
- [x] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost appears without recorded live
      inference; in a synthetic run, metrics are labelled as pipeline checks — every printed
      metric carries `(a pipeline check, not a Jev result)`, and every `validation` number also
      carries `(a selection step, not a reported result)`.
- [x] `README.md` says what the recipe teaches, how to run it, and what was and was not
      measured live.
- [x] The pull request changes only `recipes/39-document-extraction-cascade/` and CI is green —
      the scope diff is confined to this folder; `Catalog (README is current)` is the one
      expected-red check, per the generated-README exception.

## Decisions a later builder will have to live with

- **Two fixed fields, `invoice_number` and `total_amount`**, not a configurable field list, to
  keep the fixture set small enough to read while still giving the composition something real
  to combine. `FIELDS` is a module-level tuple everything else (`stage1_fields`,
  `flatten_fields`, `document_correct`, ...) iterates over, so adding a third field is a matter
  of adding its extractor, its instructions, and its own fixture coverage — not a rewrite.
- **Stage 1's own `Choice` confidence is never part of the gating rule.** Only stage 2's `Noul`
  (business threshold) and `noul_confidence` (confidence gate) decide `review` versus
  `extracted`. This matches the use case's own wording ("verify each selection against its
  source span... route uncertain or inconsistent records to review") and keeps the three-check
  rule in `finalize_field` simple; stage 1's own confidence is still shown for the one answer in
  "One answer up close", just not used to decide anything.
- **The business threshold (F1 on validation) and the confidence gate (`min_coverage=0.85`) are
  chosen over *provisional* (document, field) pairs only** — the ones where stage 1 actually
  named a real candidate — never over the whole fixture set, since a `not_found` or
  no-candidate field never produces a verification `noul` to choose from. The committed
  validation pool has exactly one business-threshold error (`v12`'s `total_amount`, a correct
  pick stage 2 wrongly doubts) and it carries the *highest* confidence of the whole validation
  set (`0.84`, since the wrong verification is a confident `noul=0.08`, far from `0.5`) — so
  `min_coverage` is the only workable objective here: `target_accuracy=1.0` would need to
  exclude that one answer via the confidence gate, but excluding the highest-confidence answer
  without excluding everything above it is not possible. This is the same "confidence is
  distance from 0.5, not from the business threshold" shape `docs/evaluation.md`'s own
  three-path-pattern caveat names, and it shows up unprompted in this recipe's own fixtures
  rather than needing to be engineered in.
- **Stage-ordering**: field-level pooling (`helpers.flatten_fields`) iterates documents, then
  `FIELDS` within each — a single fixed order. `tests/test_helpers.py::
  test_pooling_order_does_not_change_attribution_or_metrics` builds the same (document, field)
  decisions via two independently-constructed orderings (document-major and field-major) and a
  third, randomly shuffled order, and checks both the row-level attribution and the
  `evaluate_outcomes` metrics agree across all three — not merely that the counts match.

## Unfinished / open questions

- This recipe has no recorded fixtures, so the README's "not measured live" is unconditional;
  nothing here speaks to how Jev actually performs on this task.
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`'s strong-form check (`G1(c)`) requires the re-derivation to be
  syntactically local to `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right`'s own function body, so that
  test deliberately does not call the shared `helpers.decide_document`'s sibling
  threshold-selection logic through any helper — it re-derives the business threshold and
  confidence gate itself, independently of `_frozen_thresholds` (also in that file, used by the
  other tests). This is intentional, not an oversight: an independent strong-form check cannot
  re-derive through the very production path it is meant to audit.

title: Recipe 38: Abstention and review queues
body:
Closes #38

## What this adds

`recipes/38-abstention-and-review-queues/`: a support-ticket router that can abstain. Jev
answers one `Choice` question per ticket, naming one of three real queues (`self_serve`,
`tier1_support`, `tier2_engineering`) or the explicit fallback this use case names,
`insufficient_information`. Python's `route_ticket` has two branches: a confidence gate on the
three real queues, frozen from `validation` with `select_confidence_threshold(...,
min_coverage=0.75)`, and an unconditional review branch for `insufficient_information`
(never routed automatically, whatever its confidence). The notebook reports the frozen rule on
`test` two ways — a plain per-question classification accuracy that ignores abstention, and the
task-level coverage/accuracy/risk of the composed decision via `evaluate_outcomes` — and plots
the full risk-coverage curve. Builds on recipe 4 (support ticket routing)'s patterns; its own
fixtures are new (different categories, different tickets).

  README regions regenerated by the integration worker (nothing else outside the recipe

  README regions later, per the generated-README exception.

  `main`, before final review; `--check` passes — **not done by this builder on purpose**; the
  generated-README exception reserves this for a separate integration worker, and

  paths (no `README.md` yet — the integration worker adds it), every mode `100644`, no symlink,
  mode or type change, no rename or deletion out of scope.

  13 swept rows).
- [x] The deterministic composition lives in a Python function with tests —
  `helpers.route_ticket`, tested in `tests/test_helpers.py` (16 tests covering both branches,
  the threshold boundary, the out-of-range check, and the state hiding the ticket id).
- [x] Evaluation is at task level, not only per question — "Evaluation" reports both: the

- **Domain reuses recipe 4's pattern (ticket routing with a confidence gate and an

  confidence-only view would count as routed automatically, and isn't.

title: Recipe 35: Semantic feature extraction
body:
Closes #35

## What this adds

`recipes/35-semantic-feature-extraction/`: six independent `Noul` propositions over one piece
of customer feedback (mentions a price, expresses frustration, requests a refund or
cancellation, names a competitor, reports a technical issue, expresses satisfaction), sent
together in a single request, giving a feature vector per text. Python freezes a per-feature
business threshold on `validation` (`select_threshold`, objective `f1`), then fits a fixed
majority-class baseline and a plain-Python Bernoulli Naive Bayes classifier on `train`'s
composed feature vectors against a second, independently-authored gold label (`escalate`) —
all frozen before `test` is ever touched. Held-out accuracy of both the classifier and the
baseline is reported on `validation` (selection label) and `test` (once), alongside per-feature
precision/recall/F1 and a pooled accuracy across every (text, feature) pair.

Builds on #6 (Multiple topic labels): the same "one independent Noul per label, sent together"
pattern, reused rather than copied — recipe 35 trains a classifier on the resulting vector
against a second gold label instead of assembling the six booleans directly into a tag set.

## Decisions

- **Classifier implementation.** The notebook-execution CI job installs `.[ml]` (scikit-learn
  available), but the `Tests (py3.10)` and `Tests (py3.14)` jobs install only `.[dev]` /
  `.[dev,live]` — never `[ml]` — and `tests/test_helpers.py` imports `helpers.py` under those
  jobs. A classifier implemented against scikit-learn in `helpers.py` would therefore fail both
  `Tests` legs. The classifier (`helpers.fit_naive_bayes` / `predict_naive_bayes`) is a small
  Bernoulli Naive Bayes model in plain Python and `math.log`, over numpy-free boolean vectors —
  a few lines, fully deterministic, matched by a hand-computed-posterior test — so it needs
  nothing beyond what `.[dev]` already installs. No shared-package gap to report.
- **Confidence gate as a diagnostic, not a routing decision.** `helpers.compose_features` is a
  plain, total, two-outcome business threshold per feature (`present = noul >= threshold`);
  there is no third, deferral outcome for a gate to route to, because a semantic feature
  destined for a classifier's input vector has nothing to send to a person the way an answer
  shown directly to a reader would. The notebook still freezes a pooled confidence gate on
  `validation` (`helpers.REVIEW`, `helpers.confidence_outcome`, reason string exactly
  `"confidence below the threshold"`, matching every other Noul recipe's vocabulary) and reports
  how many (text, feature) pairs it would send to review on each split — but
  `helpers.feature_vector` never withholds a feature for low confidence, stated explicitly in
  the notebook. `jev_cookbook.evaluation.pool_label_decisions` pools the six features' (text,
  feature) correctness and confidence for both the accuracy figure and the gate; `coverage` and
  `risk` do not otherwise appear, because nothing is actually withheld from the classifier.
- **Pre-registration.** The feature list (`helpers.FEATURES`), the split assignment (which text
  id belongs to which split) and the baseline (majority class of `train`, tie goes to `True`)
  are each pinned by a literal-comparison test in `tests/test_helpers.py`
  (`test_the_feature_list_is_frozen`, `test_the_split_assignment_is_frozen`,
  `test_majority_baseline_ties_go_to_true` /
  `test_the_baseline_fit_on_committed_train_matches_trains_own_majority`), and the classifier's
  one hyperparameter (`LAPLACE_ALPHA = 1.0`, never tuned) is pinned the same way
  (`test_naive_bayes_uses_a_fixed_never_tuned_smoothing_constant`). The notebook's own cell
  order freezes all four (thresholds, baseline, classifier) in "Python's part" before the
  "Evaluation" section reads a single `test` number.
- **Fixture coverage.** Every one of the six features has all four `(present/absent) ×
  (escalate True/False)` combinations represented across the fixtures as a whole (not within
  one split), pinned by `test_every_feature_has_all_four_present_absent_by_escalate_cases`. Full
  2⁶ = 64-combination coverage was not attempted: with a predefined six-feature list (rather
  than three independent propositions), that is not a sensible fixture set at this recipe's
  size, and `tests/test_helpers.py::test_no_feature_is_the_complement_or_duplicate_of_another_
  on_committed_fixtures` checks directly that no feature is a mechanical function of another on
  the committed data (the failure mode a 2-label, 2-group fixture set hit elsewhere).
- **Consequentiality, proven at classifier level, not only at the composition level.**
  `test_each_feature_is_independently_consequential_for_the_trained_classifier` fits the
  classifier fresh from the committed `train`/`validation` fixtures and, for every one of the
  six features, finds a real committed `validation`/`test` text where flipping only that
  feature's composed bit changes the trained classifier's predicted label — a stronger property
  than the deterministic composition's own (trivial) per-feature independence.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/35-semantic-feature-extraction/`, plus the generated README regions regenerated by the integration worker (nothing else outside the recipe folder)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` after updating against current `main`, before final review; `--check` passes (it is expected to be red before this integration step) — **not done by this builder; integration worker's step, per CONTRIBUTING.md's generated-README exception**
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/35-semantic-feature-extraction/` paths, no symlink, mode or type change, rename or deletion out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance; the notebook states which mode it ran in
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases, and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (none simulated here: no action log, nothing beyond composing a vector and classifying)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels, with the baseline the issue names (fixed majority-class baseline, compared with the classifier)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met

## How it was verified

Run from the repository root, in a `uv` venv (`uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`; 3.10 the same with `.venv310`):

```bash
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/35-semantic-feature-extraction
pytest recipes/35-semantic-feature-extraction -q
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
python tools/check_hygiene.py

```

--branch recipe/35-semantic-feature-extraction --body-file <path to this description, saved as

title: Recipe 37: Research domain tagging
body:
Closes #37

## What this adds

`recipes/37-research-domain-tagging/`: a Level 3 `Noul` recipe that tags evidence passages with
zero or more of three research domains (`biomedical`, `computational`, `economics`) via three
independent `Noul` propositions sent together in one request per passage. Python filters
passages by access control before any request is built (`helpers.accessible_examples`), so a
passage marked `restricted` is never sent and never appears in output; `helpers.compose` turns
the three per-domain decisions into one task-level `PassageResult` (the tag set, the domains
sent to review, and the provenance of every one of those decisions). Evaluation reports per
domain (precision/recall/F1, via `jev_cookbook.evaluation.multilabel_metrics`), at task level
(`exact_set_match`), and the access-control proof itself, instrumenting the actual decide path
with a counting backend rather than inferring "never sent" from where the filter sits in the
code.

Builds on #6 (Multiple topic labels): reuses its multi-label `Noul` pattern
(`pool_label_decisions`/`pool_label_outcomes`, a per-domain business threshold chosen by F1 on
`validation`, one shared pooled confidence gate) with new fixtures (not copied) and a new
access-control layer that recipe 6 does not have.

### Decisions a later builder should know about

- **Three domains, full coverage of all eight combinations**, two authored variants each
  (a clean case and a benign look-alike), on both `validation` and `test`: `{}`, each single
  domain, each pair, and all three together. No domain label is a mechanical function of
  another — each is authored from an independent judgement about what the passage reports, and
  `tests/test_helpers.py::test_each_domain_is_independently_consequential_on_a_real_fixture`
  proves, on a real committed row (`v15-all-clean`), that flipping any one domain's decision
  changes the composed result, parametrized over all three domains.
- **A third economics-only variant per split** (`v19`/`v20`, `t19`/`t20`) exists specifically so
  every domain — not only `economics` — has at least one committed, confidently wrong tag on
  `test`: without them, `biomedical` and `computational` would both read `test` F1 1.0000 by
  construction (nothing in the committed fixtures would have made either number fall).
- **Access is authored independently of domain content**: the four restricted passages
  (`v17`/`v18`/`t17`/`t18`) carry gold domain sets of `{biomedical}`, `{computational,
  economics}`, `{}` and `{biomedical, economics}` respectively, so being restricted is not
  predictable from a passage's domains, and vice versa.
- **The access-control filter is proven load-bearing, not merely present.** Deleting the
  `accessible_examples(...)` call inside `helpers.decide_passages` (by hand, reverted before
  committing) makes `tests/test_helpers.py::test_a_restricted_passage_is_never_sent` and
  `::test_a_restricted_passage_never_appears_in_the_composed_output` fail immediately: a
  `ReplayMiss` whose state is a restricted passage's own text verbatim, because
  `fixtures/responses.json` holds no stored answer for a passage that was never supposed to be
  decided. "Never sent" is proven by instrumenting the actual `decide_passages` call with a
  counting backend wrapper (both in `tests/test_helpers.py` and again, independently, in the
  notebook's own "Evaluation" section), never by inferring it from the filter's position in the
  code.
- **`decide_passages` takes an optional shared cache** so a passage shown individually in "One
  answer up close" (`v02-none-lookalike`, `v04-biomedical-lookalike`) is not decided a second
  time by the later bulk pass: the whole notebook makes exactly 37 requests (one per accessible
  example in `fixtures/`, demo included), never more.
- **Task-level and per-domain metrics both come from the business rule alone**
  (`multilabel_from_noul`, ignoring the confidence gate), matching recipe 6's own pattern; the
  confidence gate's own coverage/accuracy/risk are reported separately via
  `pool_label_outcomes` fed to `evaluate_outcomes`, and the notebook states directly that the two
  views agree exactly here because `tag_domains`'s only review branch is the shared confidence
  gate.
- This is explicitly framed as **not an access-control system**: the filter is a deterministic
  classification rule of this recipe's own fabricated scheme (CONTRIBUTING.md section 5), not a
  security feature, and the notebook says so in two places (the intro and the evaluation
  discussion).

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/37-research-domain-tagging/` (no generated README region
  yet; that is added by the integration worker per the generated-README exception)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` — not run by this builder;
  `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until the integration worker runs it
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same
  question definitions as the offline path
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states its run
  mode via `run_header` and the "What was and was not measured" cell
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference (none here;
  this recipe has no recorded fixtures)
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (full domain-combination coverage, benign
