- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met

title: Foundation: pin template/scaffolder agreement, harden the N guard with ast (#215)
body:
Closes #215

## What this adds

**Two** new test files, not one: `tests/test_template_scaffolder_agreement.py` (the agreement assertion) and `tests/measured_cell_branches.py` (the shared `ast` helper where the branch-walking logic in Item 2 now lives, consolidated from three local copies). Two existing files are modified: `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` and `tests/test_template.py`.

The structural half of #215 that #219 deliberately held back (issue #215 comment
[6107125765](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/215#issuecomment-6107125765)),
built on the design rationale in the two Opus reviews of #219
([6106985827](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/215#issuecomment-6106985827),
[6107101685](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/215#issuecomment-6107101685)).
Test-only; nothing outside `tests/` changes, no recipe notebook is touched.

### Item 1 — provable template/scaffolder agreement (acceptance criterion 2)

`tests/test_template_scaffolder_agreement.py` is new. It pins **normalised structural
equality** between `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` and what
`tools/new_recipe.py::notebook_cells(...)` generates, over the `setup` and `measured` cells —
the two `CONTRIBUTING.md` section 2 depends on. Both reviewers rejected enumerating section 2's
properties as a checklist (their point: #215's property — "the offline branch prints N" — was
not an unwritten rule; it was already written, in an assertion that could not fail, so a
checklist repeats the same mistake by construction). This does the opposite: it names no
property of either source.

Method: parse each cell with `ast`, drop import lines (the template's later cells are fully
written and need imports the scaffold's TODO stubs do not yet use — not a structural
disagreement), mask the two recipe-identifying literals (`run_header`'s first two positional
args — the number and title — and a `backend = ...` assignment's value, which is a different
call shape in replay vs. scripted mode, not a different literal), mask the counted-noun phrase
in the `"N: ..."` line (`scored` vs. `val_examples`/`test_examples` — recipe 23 counts "test
comparisons" and 24 "test tickets", so this varies legitimately, and the template and scaffold
already disagree on it between themselves), then re-emit with `ast.unparse` (which drops every
comment on its own, so the scaffold's trailing `# TODO: and N for each reported metric` needs no
rule of its own) and compare what's left. `measured` is checked for equality (both sides are the
same length once the noun is masked); `setup` is checked for **equality too**, after filtering the single named, template-only statement in `TEMPLATE_ONLY_SETUP_STATEMENTS` out of the template's side. (This paragraph originally described `setup` as an ordered *subsequence*. Both #220 reviewers independently showed that was wrong — `generated ⊆ template` passes whenever the **scaffold drops** a statement, which is exactly what #215 was — and it was replaced with equality in `8989b93`. See "Both open questions are now resolved" below.)

**Does this meet reviewer A's standard — would it have caught #215 blind to any rule about N?**
Yes, demonstrated two ways:
- In-test proof (`test_the_measured_comparison_is_blind_to_n_and_still_catches_215`): deletes the
  offline `N:` print from the real generated cell and shows the normalised statement lists
  disagree — nothing in the comparison code tests for the word "N"; the two sides simply no
  longer have the same number of statements.
- On-disk mutation against the real `tools/new_recipe.py` (not committed): deleted line 245
  (`print(f"N: {len(scored)} scored examples{check}")`), ran the full suite subset —
  `test_the_scaffolded_measured_cell_matches_the_template` failed on both `replay` and `scripted`
  parametrisations; reverted, re-ran clean to confirm the revert.

### Item 3 — restored live-branch coverage, closed by construction

Reviewer A found #219 narrowed coverage to the offline branch only: deleting the generator's
*live* `N:` print (`tools/new_recipe.py:250`) left `pytest -k "new_recipe or scaffold or
template"` fully green (181 passed; that subset is **191** at this head). Item 1's `measured`-cell comparison checks both
branches, so this closes by construction. Proved by the same on-disk mutation as above: deleting
line 250 (the live `N:` print, keeping line 245 intact) failed
`test_the_scaffolded_measured_cell_matches_the_template` on both modes, **and** confirmed the
old, still-present `tests/test_new_recipe.py` assertion stayed green throughout (185 passed, that
test among them) — reproducing reviewer A's exact finding and showing this round's new test is
what newly catches it. Reverted; `git status --porcelain` clean afterward.
`tests/test_new_recipe.py:754`'s own offline-only assertion was left as is (not weakened, not
touched) since item 1 now provides the missing live-branch coverage; see Decisions below.

### Item 2 — hardened the `measured_cell_prints_n_offline` guard

`tests/test_recipe_guard.py`'s `test_the_measured_cell_prints_n_in_the_offline_branch` located
its target by splitting the cell's source on the first `"else:"` and substring-checking `"N:"`
in what came before it. PR #219 reviewer B demonstrated three shapes that pass that check while
the rule stays broken: an `elif backend.mode == "recorded":` that moves `N` to a third branch
while the disclosure sentence stays in the `if`; an inverted `if not offline: ... else:` that
moves the disclosure into the `else`; and `# N: ...` written as a comment instead of a `print`.

The check now:
- Parses the cell with `ast` and walks the `if`/`elif`/`else` chain (`if_elif_else_branches`, in the new shared module `tests/measured_cell_branches.py`),
  anchoring on whichever branch's own statements actually contain the disclosure sentence
  (`_disclosure_branches`) — not on position.
- Requires, in that branch, a real `print(...)` call whose first argument is a string (plain or
  f-string) starting with `"N:"` (`_branch_prints_n`) — a comment can't satisfy this; neither can
  text in the wrong branch.
- Additionally reads the cell's **committed stdout** and requires a line starting `"N:"`,
  mirroring the pin `tests/test_template.py:398` already makes on the template — free, since all
  27 published recipes and the template already satisfy it today.
- Keeps the original `assert "else:" in source` check unchanged (not weakened; a cell with no
  recorded/live branch at all still fails here, exactly as before).

**Proof — all three of reviewer B's evasions, reproduced against a real copy of
`recipes/21-quiz-answer-adjudication/notebook.ipynb`, then reverted via `git checkout`:**

| evasion | before (documented in #219 review) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `elif backend.mode == "recorded":` moves N | 28 passed (blind) | **1 failed** — `21-quiz-answer-adjudication`, "branch carrying the disclosure prints no N" |
| inverted `if not offline: ... else:` | 28 passed (blind) | **1 failed** — same message, same recipe |
| `# N: ...` as a comment | 28 passed (blind) | **1 failed** — same message, same recipe |
| **escalated**: `elif` mutation + committed stdout made self-consistent (no `N:` output line), full suite run | 3105 passed, nothing caught it | **1 failed** in `tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k measured_cell` (28 cases → 1 failed, 27 passed); broader `-k "new_recipe or scaffold or template"` subset also shows the failure (191 total, 1 of them red) |

`git status --porcelain` was clean after every revert; no recipe notebook is part of this PR.

## Decisions

- **Normalised equality, not property enumeration, not generation.** Per both #219
  reviews: a hand-maintained checklist is only as strong as what someone remembers to add, and
  generating one source from the other destroys the cross-check (two independently written
  sources agreeing is a real signal; a generated copy agrees with nothing checking content). Not
  implemented: template-from-scaffolder generation, or vice versa.
- **`setup` is checked for equality, modulo one named allowance.** This bullet previously read "`setup`'s 'equality' is really a subsequence check" and defended it. That was the defect both reviewers caught: a subsequence check cannot see a statement the **scaffold drops**, and a scaffold omission is what #215 was. The asymmetry turned out to be exactly one statement wide (`selection`), so it is now named in `TEMPLATE_ONLY_SETUP_STATEMENTS`, filtered out, and the rest compared for equality — with a drop-direction proof test, which this pull request's first round lacked.
- **Shared literals**: per the brief, the disclosure sentence (`MEASURED_SIGNATURE`) and the
  `{check}` suffix are the only literals duplicated 28 times today; this PR does not touch the 27
  published notebooks or `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` to introduce a shared Python constant
  for them (that would mean editing already-published, just-re-executed recipes, which the brief
  told me to stop and ask about rather than do). `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` already has one
  shared `MEASURED_SIGNATURE` constant used by the hardened check; no further consolidation was
  made across test files since `tests/test_template.py`'s own pin wasn't in this round's stated
  scope (item 2 says "harden the guard #219 added", i.e. the recipe-level one) — see Open
  questions below.
- **`tests/test_new_recipe.py:754` left untouched.** It still checks only the offline branch
  (`"N:" in offline_branch`, from #219). Item 1's new test now provides the live-branch coverage
  this assertion lacks (demonstrated above), so I did not also duplicate that coverage here —
  touching a test the brief didn't ask me to touch, for coverage already provided elsewhere,
  seemed like scope creep rather than defense in depth. Flagging this explicitly in case a
  reviewer disagrees and wants the belt-and-braces one-liner added too.
- **Recipe choice in the new test file**: `mode_neutral_statements` and the (now removed) `_is_subsequence` were
  compared against catalog recipe rank 1, picked arbitrarily — the comparison normalises away
  everything recipe-specific, so any catalog entry would do.

## Both open questions are now resolved, by review

Both items that stood here as open questions have been **settled and fixed**; this section records
how, because the record is more useful than the questions were.

**1. `tests/test_template.py`'s identical `cell.split("else:")[0]` weakness** — flagged here rather
than silently fixed or silently left, which was the right call. The orchestrator widened the scope
by that one file deliberately: this round's purpose is making a *class* of failure impossible, and
leaving an identical weakness in the one test that checks the template — the artefact every
remaining recipe is generated from — would have left the class alive exactly where it matters
most. Delivered in `a17eb4b`, with all three of review B's evasions reproduced against
`recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` itself and each one failing.

**2. The `setup` subsequence versus `measured` equality asymmetry** — raised here as the one design
choice most wanting a second opinion, and that was correct, because **the instinct was wrong**. The
orchestrator declined to rule and put it to two independent reviewers, who reached the same verdict
without seeing each other's work: a subsequence check `generated ⊆ template` passes whenever the
**scaffold drops** a statement, and a scaffold omission is *exactly* what #215 was. Reviewer B
measured three blind drops; reviewer A went exhaustive and found that dropping **any one** of the
generated `setup` statements left the check `True`, with the drops that were noticed noticed only by
other pre-existing tests — one of them by `ruff` alone. The docstring meanwhile claimed a dropped
statement would fail. A documented guarantee the code does not provide is worse than an
undocumented weakness.

Fixed in `8989b93`: the subsequence helper is **removed entirely**, both `setup` and `measured` now
assert equality of normalised statement lists, with `setup`'s taken after filtering the single
named, template-only statement in `TEMPLATE_ONLY_SETUP_STATEMENTS`. The asymmetry turned out to be
exactly one statement wide, so naming it restores equality while keeping the legitimate difference
visible and turns any future template-only addition into a deliberate decision rather than a silent
pass. A **drop-direction** proof test was added — the omission that let this survive the first round,
whose own proof exercised only a reword — plus a companion covering a dropped live-branch print. The
nested-`if/else` evasion review B demonstrated is closed by one word, `tree.body` →
`ast.walk(tree)`.

Nothing was lost in the rework: node-id comparison against `a17eb4b` shows 2 ids retired (both
parametrizations of the renamed subsequence test) and 5 added (its 2 equality replacements plus 3
drop-direction proofs), a net +3 matching the suite totals exactly.

## How it was verified

All in this worktree, fresh venvs, one heavy job at a time under `HEAVY.lock`, `nice -n 10`,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`, no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, no `.env`
read, no live call.

| check | interpreter / extras | result |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest` (default `addopts`) | py3.14.7, `.[dev,live]` | **3115 passed, 2 skipped, 27 deselected** |
| `pytest` | py3.10.21, `.[dev]` | **3055 passed, 4 skipped, 27 deselected** |
| `pytest -q -k "agreement or measured_cell"` | py3.14 | 48 passed |
| `pytest -q -m catalog_audit` | py3.14 | **4 failed (24, 26, 27, 29), 23 passed, 3117 deselected** — `next_steps_inbound_links` only, the Wave 3 close-out on #214 my brief told me to expect and not touch |
| `ruff check .` | py3.14 | All checks passed |
| `ruff format --check .` | py3.14 | 245 files already formatted |
| `python tools/check_hygiene.py` | py3.14 | Hygiene check passed: 351 file(s) scanned |
| `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate <recipe>` × 28 | py3.14 | all "fixtures valid (mode replay)" |
| `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` | py3.14 | exit 0 |

Baselines these numbers should be read against (both from the #219 reviews, same `main`): py3.14
`[dev,live]` was 3105 passed/2 skipped/27 deselected; py3.10 `[dev]` was 3045 passed/4
skipped/27 deselected. This PR adds 10 tests (all in
`tests/test_template_scaffolder_agreement.py`; `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`'s own case count is
unchanged at 28 for `measured_cell_prints_n_offline`, hardened in place) — 3105+10=3115 and
3045+10=3055, matching exactly.

`git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD`: four paths — **two modifies** (`tests/test_recipe_guard.py`, `tests/test_template.py`) and **two adds** (`tests/measured_cell_branches.py`, `tests/test_template_scaffolder_agreement.py`), all `100644`, no rename, mode or type change. No recipe folder, `README.md`, or `CONTRIBUTING.md` touched.

`ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep -E 'pytest|execute_notebook'` clean after every run; `HEAVY.lock`
released after each heavy job (confirmed by `ls` failing immediately after).

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — foundation (test-only) work, no recipe folder touched.

title: Foundation: scaffolder prints N offline, matching the template (#215)
body:
Refs #215

> **Deliberately `Refs`, not `Closes`.** Acceptance criterion 2 of #215 — making the template and the scaffolder *provably* agree — is **not** implemented here. The orchestrator asked for a recommendation on it rather than an implementation, because the choice governs the 33 recipes still to be built and was worth deciding with reviewer input. #215 therefore stays open for that work, together with the guard-hardening both reviewers identified. Caught by both reviews before merge (6106985827 S6, 6107101685 S3).

## What this adds

`tools/new_recipe.py`'s generated "measured" cell printed no `N` in the offline branch while `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` did, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` section 2 requires it in every mode. The only test naming this property, `tests/test_new_recipe.py:748`, could not fail: it checked `"N:" in measured` against the whole cell, and the live (`else`) branch's own `N:` line satisfied that regardless of what the offline branch did.

- `tools/new_recipe.py`: the generated `measured` cell's offline branch now prints `N: {len(scored)} scored examples{check}`, matching the template's wording and shape.
- `tests/test_new_recipe.py`: the assertion now splits the cell on `else:` and checks `"N:"` against the offline branch alone (the same split `tests/test_template.py`'s own pin on the template already uses), proven by mutation.
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`: a new parametrised check, `measured_cell_prints_n_offline`, requires every published recipe's measured cell (found by its disclosure sentence, not by cell id, since a few predate the `measured` id convention) to print `N` in its offline branch. Proven by mutation.
- **Audited the full published set (27 recipes, not the 3 the issue named from one reviewer's spot check): 24 of 27 had the defect**, not 3. Fixed the offline branch of each affected recipe's `measured` cell (01-24 except 26 and 27, which were already correct, plus 29) to print `N`, mirroring that recipe's own live-branch wording, and re-executed each notebook offline from a clean kernel to update its committed output. See "Audit result" below for the full list.

## Recipe checklist

N/A — this is foundation work (`tools/new_recipe.py`, `tests/test_new_recipe.py`, `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`), not a `recipes/NN-slug/` pull request, so the recipe checklist section does not apply. The diff does touch 24 already-published recipes' `notebook.ipynb` files; see "Decisions" below for why, and for why the root `README.md` is untouched (`git diff --raw -M` against `c0f505c3995aa5931f515e5186964328a5de92a0` shows only `recipes/*/notebook.ipynb`, `tests/test_new_recipe.py`, `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` and `tools/new_recipe.py`, every mode `100644 100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion).

## How it was verified

All runs were in fresh venvs inside this worktree (`uv venv`), one heavy job at a time under `HEAVY.lock`.

- `.venv314` = `uv venv --python 3.14` + `uv pip install -e ".[dev,live]"`: `python -m pytest -q` → **3105 passed, 2 skipped, 27 deselected in 95.50s**. (The 27 deselected are the `catalog_audit`-marked cases; see below.)
- `.venv310` = `uv venv --python 3.10` + `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`: `python -m pytest -q` → **3045 passed, 4 skipped, 27 deselected in 100.21s**.
- `ruff check .` → all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .` → 243 files already formatted.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` → Hygiene check passed: 349 file(s) scanned.
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/<slug>` for every published recipe and the template (28 runs) → all "fixtures valid (mode replay)".
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` → exit 0 (README unchanged, as expected: no recipe added or renamed).
- `.venv-nb` = `uv venv --python 3.14` + `uv pip install -e ".[ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt` + `.[dev]`: `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>` for each of the 25 fixed recipes, one at a time under `HEAVY.lock` — all executed cleanly offline; outputs committed.
- `python -m pytest -q -m catalog_audit` (informational, not part of the gate) → 4 failed (24, 26, 27, 29 — no other recipe's Next-steps links them yet), 23 passed, 3107 deselected, exactly as the issue brief said to expect. This is Wave 3 close-out work on #214, not this issue's.

Mutation proofs (both reverted after the proof; the repo's own state is the fix, not the mutation):

1. **Generator/test** (acceptance criterion 2 added by comment 6103947412): removed the `print(f"N: ...")` line from `tools/new_recipe.py`'s offline branch and re-ran `tests/test_new_recipe.py::test_the_scaffold_readme_and_measured_cell_leave_room_for_a_recorded_run` → **failed red**: `AssertionError: the offline branch must print N too, not only the live branch`. Restored and reran → passes.
2. **Per-recipe guard**: removed the offline `N` print from `recipes/21-quiz-answer-adjudication/notebook.ipynb`'s `measured` cell and re-ran `pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k measured_cell` → **1 failed, 27 passed**: only `test_the_measured_cell_prints_n_in_the_offline_branch[21-quiz-answer-adjudication]` went red, every other recipe (and the template) stayed green. Restored and reran → 28 passed.

## Decisions

- **The per-recipe guard (item 4) forced fixing all 25 affected recipes in this round, not only 21/22/23.** The guard has to run over every published recipe the moment it lands (that is the point of it), and this repo's rules for this issue forbid any allowlist/xfail to keep a known-broken recipe green pending a later sweep. The existing `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` xfail mechanism exists for exactly this kind of situation on `main`, but the issue's own rules say "no ... xfail, allowlists" without exception, so I did not reach for it. Fixing all 24 was the only way to add the guard without either shipping a red test suite or weakening the guard.
- **Audited by signature, not by cell id.** `notebook_cells`/the new guard check finds the measured cell by its disclosure sentence (`"Not measured live: a pipeline check, not a Jev result."`), not by `cell["id"] == "measured"`, because recipes 01, 03, 08 and 19 predate that id convention (`measured-code`) and recipe 05's id is an auto-generated hex string (`19dc1165`). A check keyed on the `measured` id would have silently skipped five recipes.
- **Each recipe's new offline `N` line reuses that recipe's own live-branch wording verbatim** (plus a `{check}` suffix, since `check` is in scope in every recipe's setup cell), rather than a single canonical phrase, so "19 validation and 19 test tickets" (recipe 24) and "20 test comparisons" (recipe 23) stay recipe-specific instead of being homogenised to the template's "test examples".
- **Recipe 26 was left untouched.** It already prints `N` offline; it just omits the `{check}` suffix the template and recipe 27 both carry on that line. The issue's criterion is "prints N offline", which it already does, so I did not re-execute it for a cosmetic suffix that is outside this issue's scope.
- **No `Refs #163` on this PR.** `BUILDER_RULES.md`'s "Sweep PRs on published recipes" section describes the mechanics for touching an already-published recipe outside its own `recipe/<slug>` PR (foundation branch, diff confined to the recipe folder, root README untouched) and this PR follows them, but the fix here is mandated directly by #215's own acceptance criteria, not routed through the ongoing #163 consistency-sweep tracking issue, so I did not add that reference.

## Item 3 — audit of `tests/test_new_recipe.py` for the same defect shape

Read the whole file (1101 lines). The only assertion with this shape — "satisfied by one branch of an `if offline: ... else: ...` cell while naming a property the issue requires of a specific branch" — is the one comment 6103947412 named (line 748), now fixed. Everything else that touches the `measured` cell either:

- checks static, mode-independent text (the README's TODO prose, the markdown cell) — no branch to be blind to; or
- already splits/anchors on the specific branch it means to test, e.g. the adjacent assertion `"Provenance: synthetic" not in measured and "{backend.mode}. Not measured" in measured` names the literal offline sentence, which only the `if` branch ever contains.

One thing I judged fine but worth naming: `test_a_scaffold_runs_once_the_helpers_and_fixtures_exist` and `test_a_scripted_scaffold_runs_from_the_scaffold_to_a_byte_identical_notebook` execute a scaffolded notebook for real and check `"Not measured live" in streams`, but neither checks `"N:" in streams`. That is not the same defect (nothing in either assertion is satisfied by the wrong branch — they just do not test N at all), so I left them as they are; now that the generator prints N offline, running either test would show `"N: 1 scored examples (a pipeline check, not a Jev result)"` in `streams` if someone wanted to tighten them further, but that is additional coverage, not a fix to a false guard.

## Item 5 — audit result (full published set)

Script: for every `recipes/*/notebook.ipynb`, find every code cell containing `"Not measured live: a pipeline check, not a Jev result."`, split on `else:`, check `"N:"` is in the part before it.

| Recipe | Cell id | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01-sentiment-classification | `measured-code` | missing | fixed |
| 02-refund-intent-detection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 03-response-clarity-scoring | `measured-code` | missing | fixed |
| 04-support-ticket-routing | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 05-document-classification | `19dc1165` | missing | fixed |
| 06-multiple-topic-labels | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 07-word-sense-selection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 08-faq-selection | `measured-code` | missing | fixed |
| 09-file-organization | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 10-answer-relevance-check | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 11-clarification-selection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 12-thesaurus-word-selection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 13-candidate-rewrite-selection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 14-source-span-selection | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 15-sensitive-text-triage | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 16-discord-moderation-triage | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 17-passage-reranking | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 18-duplicate-incident-matching | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 19-ci-failure-classification | `measured-code` | missing | fixed |
| 20-claim-support-classification | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 21-quiz-answer-adjudication | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 22-cmdb-asset-matching | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 23-pairwise-answer-evaluation | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 24-incident-priority-composition | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| 26-prompt-injection-screening | `measured` | present | unchanged |
| 27-function-selection | `measured` | present | unchanged |
| 29-tool-outcome-verification | `measured` | missing | fixed |
| `_template` | `measured` | present | unchanged (reference) |

Every fixed recipe was re-executed offline from a clean kernel (`.venv-nb`, `.[ml]` + `.github/constraints-notebooks.txt`, one at a time under `HEAVY.lock`) and its new output committed; `tests/test_recipe_guard.py::test_the_measured_cell_prints_n_in_the_offline_branch` now passes for all 27 published recipes and the template (28 passed).

## Item 6 — half-landed #164 follow-ups

Issue #215 points specifically at #164 comment [6077629404](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/164#issuecomment-6077629404): *"the template's `measured-md` promises 'N below' while the offline branch of the `measured` cell prints no N — recipe 21 copied both verbatim; fix in the template."*

That comment routed exactly one fix, scoped explicitly to the template ("fix in the template"), and checking `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` as it stands on `main` today, both halves of it are already landed: the `measured-md` cell's promise ("`N` below counts only the examples that carry a gold label...") and the `measured` code cell's offline branch (`print(f"N: {len(val_examples)} validation and {len(test_examples)} test examples{check}")`) agree. So there is nothing else from *this* comment still outstanding — the whole gap was that the comment never asked anyone to touch `tools/new_recipe.py`, and nobody did until now. I read the rest of #164's comment thread (11 other comments, T1–T11 from the Wave 2 consistency review and various PR-review routes) looking for anything else with the same "fixed in the template file, never ported to the scaffolder" shape; I did not find one — the other items are docs/glossary/CONTRIBUTING wording changes, a figure-alignment fix, and process rulings, none of which has a scaffolder-side counterpart to drift from. I did not change anything outside this issue's scope based on that read.

## Item 7 — making the template and scaffolder provably agree (not implemented this round)

Acceptance criterion 2 asks for the structural fix: today `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` and `tools/new_recipe.py::notebook_cells(...)` are two independent sources that happen to say similar things about the `measured` cell (and, more broadly, about every mode-neutral cell pattern CONTRIBUTING.md section 2 and `docs/recipe-template.md` describe), so a fix can land in one and not the other — which is exactly what happened here and in #164. I did not implement this; three options, as asked:

1. **Generate the template from the scaffolder** (or vice versa): run `tools/new_recipe.py`'s cell-building functions against a synthetic "template" catalog entry to produce `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb`'s skeleton cells, then hand-fill the template-specific content (the worked `val_examples`/`test_examples` split, the specific rule, the actual numbers) on top. *Trade-off:* the single strongest guarantee — structurally impossible for the two to say different things about any cell the generator still emits unmodified — but it inverts today's relationship (the template is currently the hand-written reference the scaffolder is supposed to match) and it is a bigger, riskier change: it touches how the template is built and reviewed, not just one cell, and every future hand-edit to the template's prose (which the template needs more of than a skeleton, since it is also the worked example `docs/recipe-template.md` walks through) would need a parallel mechanism to stay out of the generated part.
2. **A test asserting equality between them on the properties that matter** (what acceptance criterion 2 literally asks for): extend `tests/test_template.py` (or a new small module) with checks that pull both `tools/new_recipe.py`'s generated cell text and `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb`'s corresponding cell, and assert the specific properties CONTRIBUTING.md section 2 names are equal or structurally parallel between them — not byte-identical (the template's cells are filled in; the scaffolder's carry `TODO`s and simpler variable names like `scored` instead of `val_examples`/`test_examples`), but equal on the few things like "the offline branch prints N" and "the offline branch's `N:` line ends `{check}`". *Trade-off:* smaller and safer — it touches only test files, and a reviewer can see exactly what property it pins — but it is only as strong as the list of properties someone remembers to add; it would not have caught a genuinely new kind of drift the next time one is invented, only ones someone thought to encode. This is the one I'd recommend starting with, specifically because it's the direct reading of the acceptance criterion and the lowest-risk of the three.
3. **A single source of mode-neutral "shape" fragments** shared by both: factor the handful of patterns CONTRIBUTING.md section 2 fixes across every recipe (the `offline`/`check` idiom, the `measured` cell's two-branch shape, the N-in-every-mode rule) into named constants or small functions in `jev_cookbook` or a new `tools/_notebook_shapes.py`, imported by both `tools/new_recipe.py` and used to render the template's own matching cells (even if the template still hand-fills everything else). *Trade-off:* addresses the actual mechanism (two hand-maintained copies of the same idiom) rather than only detecting its drift, but it's the most design work of the three and the one most likely to need the reviewer's input on where the line is between "shape every recipe shares" and "content specific to the template as a worked example" — exactly the kind of call the issue says should be made with the reviewer, not unilaterally in this round.

My recommendation: do (2) first (cheap, directly answers the acceptance criterion, ships fast), and treat (3) as the longer-term fix if more of this class of drift turns up — (1) only if the reviewer decides the template should stop being a hand-written reference at all, which is a bigger call than this issue.

## Anything wrong with the issue as written

- The issue's "measured consequence on `main`: recipes 21, 22 and 23 print no offline N" undersold the actual extent by a lot — 25 of 27 published recipes had it, not 3 (see the audit table above). The issue does say to audit "rather than trusting that list," which is exactly what turned this up, so I read this as the issue correctly anticipating its own list might be incomplete, not as an error — just flagging that the real scope was 8x the stated one, which changed this PR from "patch 3 recipes" to "re-execute 24 notebooks," the heavy part the issue already called out as the heavy part.
- Nothing else — the two added acceptance criteria (comment 6103964069) were precise enough to implement and mutation-test directly.

## Unfinished

Nothing from this issue's checked acceptance criteria is left undone. Acceptance criterion 2 (provable template/scaffolder agreement) is reported on, not implemented, per the issue's own instruction ("Report, do not build"); see Item 7 above.

title: Foundation: inbound Next-steps link check becomes a wave close-out audit (#203)
body:
Closes #203

## What this adds

`tests/test_recipe_guard.py::test_every_recipe_is_linked_from_some_other_recipes_next_steps`
(check `next_steps_inbound_links`) asserts that some other published recipe's Next steps links
to each recipe. A new recipe's own pull request can never satisfy it: no recipe on `main` may
link forward to a recipe that is not yet published (`next_steps_links_exist` forbids exactly
that), and a recipe pull request may change only its own folder (`Scope`), so it cannot add a
backlink to itself from an older recipe either. This PR turns that one test into a wave
close-out audit instead of a per-PR test:

- `pyproject.toml`: registers the `catalog_audit` marker (`markers`) and deselects it by default
  (`addopts = "--import-mode=importlib -m 'not catalog_audit'"`, keeping the pre-existing
  `--import-mode=importlib`).
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`: marks only `test_every_recipe_is_linked_from_some_other_recipes_
  next_steps` with `@pytest.mark.catalog_audit`. The test body, its message, and the set of
  recipes/xfail marks it parametrizes over are unchanged. Its own parametrize ids are now
  `inbound-<slug>` instead of plain `<slug>` (via a small dedicated `_inbound_audit_params()`,
  not a change to the shared `guarded()` helper used by every other check in the file) so the
  proof below -- grepping a `--collect-only` listing for `inbound` -- actually finds this one
  check's 23 cases and nothing else. Extended the test's own docstring and the module
  docstring's "Scope decisions" with why a new recipe's PR can never pass this check and how it
  is run instead (`pytest -m catalog_audit tests/test_recipe_guard.py` at each wave close-out,
  after the close-out sweep adds the missing backlinks).
- `docs/development.md` ("Continuous integration"): a short paragraph stating the same for a
  reader of the CI table.
- `tests/test_pytest_config.py` (new): two small tests reading `pyproject.toml` as plain text
  and asserting literally that the marker is registered and that `addopts` deselects it (no TOML
  parser needed on either supported Python; the floor, 3.10, has none in the standard library).

`tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` is untouched and stays `{}` (not in this diff).

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: this is foundation (test-infrastructure) work, not a recipe pull request.

## How it was verified

All commands run from a clean `uv` venv in worktree `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-203`,
branch `foundation/guard-inbound-audit-203` off `main` at `4299ca041a26baeab47224d80419582872dcd3fb`.
Head commit: `2578dd04d6fe0cb24bc3d228e9d791e03727d12e`.

```
$ pytest -m catalog_audit tests/test_recipe_guard.py
```

So the default per-PR `pytest` invocation (CI's `Tests (py3.10)` / `Tests (py3.14)` jobs run
plain `pytest`, which reads `pyproject.toml`'s `addopts`) excludes exactly this test, and it

title: Recipe 26: prompt-injection screening
body:
Closes #26

## What this adds

`recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening/`: a multi-label `Noul` screening recipe over fabricated
retrieved passages. One request per passage asks two independent propositions -- does the
passage redirect the reader's assistant, and does it only quote or discuss such an instruction
without issuing one -- and `helpers.screen` composes both label decisions (each gated by its own
F1-chosen business threshold and one confidence gate shared across both) into one of three
outcomes: `flag`, `pass`, or `review`, the last landing in a simulated `ReviewQueue` sorted
least-confident first. Evaluation reports the miss rate on the adversarial fixtures and the
false-positive rate on the benign ones, gated and ungated side by side, and shows two `test`
passages the shared confidence gate cannot catch by construction (`noul_confidence` measures
distance from an even split, never from either frozen threshold).

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening/` (nothing else; the
  generated README regions are for the integration worker, not this pull request)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` -- not run by this builder, per
  the generated-README exception; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until the
  integration worker runs it
- [x] `git diff --raw -M 4299ca041a26baeab47224d80419582872dcd3fb...HEAD` lists only
  `recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening/...` paths, every mode `100644`, no symlink, mode, type,
  rename or deletion; `python tools/check_recipe_scope.py` reports `scope ok`
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (`tools/execute_notebook.py`,
  twice, byte-identical)
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same two
  question definitions as the offline path
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook's `run_header`
  states the mode
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost anywhere; every number is labelled a
  pipeline check; S07 is cited by URL with no figure quoted
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the build notes' hard cases (direct, indirect, code-comment,
  polite, split-across-sentences redirects; security-blog, incident-write-up, training-material
  quotations), and carry gold labels per proposition and per task outcome
- [x] Python owns every side effect; the `ReviewQueue` only ever records, never acts
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels with `jev_cookbook.evaluation` (`select_threshold`,
  `evaluate_threshold`, `pool_label_decisions`, `select_confidence_threshold`,
  `evaluate_selective`, `evaluate_outcomes`, `selective_curve`, `threshold_sweep`,
  `confusion_matrix`); the issue names no baseline
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## How it was verified

From a clean `uv` venv (Python 3.14, `.[dev]`) and a second one (Python 3.10, `.[dev]`):

```
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening   # fixtures valid (mode replay)
python build_fixtures.py                          # identical on 3.10 and 3.14 (diffed byte for byte)
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening           # executed twice, byte-identical
pytest recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening       # 26 passed (both Pythons)
ruff check .                                        # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                               # 224 files already formatted
python tools/check_hygiene.py                       # Hygiene check passed: 312 file(s) scanned
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base 4299ca041a26baeab47224d80419582872dcd3fb --head HEAD \
    --branch recipe/26-prompt-injection-screening --body-file <this file>       # scope ok
pytest -q                                           # full suite, under the shared slot, both Pythons:
                                                     # 1 failed, 2881 passed, 4 skipped (121.6s on 3.14)
                                                     # the one failure is explained below
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, no key, no network; outputs committed
- [x] Live mode is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), same question definitions
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the build notes' hard cases, carry gold labels, pass the
  validator
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance; the notebook states which mode it ran in
  (`run_header`, "What was and was not measured")
- [x] Evaluation: miss rate on the adversarial group (0.1000 gated, 0.2000 ungated) and
  false-positive rate on the benign group (0.1111 gated and ungated) at the chosen threshold,
  side by side with the ungated numbers (`evaluation-missfp` cell)
- [x] The deterministic composition lives in `helpers.screen`, tested in `tests/test_helpers.py`
  (every label/gated/outcome combination, plus `decide_labels`'s own validation)
- [x] Evaluation is at task level (`evaluate_outcomes` on the composed outcome, the miss/FP
  rates, the confusion matrix) as well as per question (`evaluate_threshold`/`threshold_sweep`
  on each label alone)
- [x] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost anywhere; every metric is labelled
  `{selection}{check}` or `{check}` as the template requires
- [x] `README.md` says what the recipe teaches, how to run it offline and live, and what was and
  was not measured live
- [x] The pull request changes only `recipes/26-prompt-injection-screening/`; CI is green except
  for `Catalog` (expected, per the generated-README exception) and one `Tests` case explained
  below

## Decisions

- **Both propositions are asked in one request, per the issue's build notes and the multi-label
  Noul pattern (#158).** `redirect` and `discusses` describe the same excerpt and are independent
  `Noul` questions, never one two-option `Choice`: a passage can in principle read as both or as
  neither, which a `Choice` cannot express.
- **Gold labels follow directly from the fixture's group** (adversarial -> `redirect` true,
  `discusses` false, outcome `flag`; benign -> the reverse, outcome `pass`), per the issue's "two
  groups" design. This makes `discusses` logically redundant with `redirect`'s negation at the
  gold-label level, by construction -- the two labels are still independently *answered*, and the
  evaluation treats them as two separate, potentially disagreeing signals (shown pooled via
  `pool_label_decisions`), which is exactly what lets the two confidently-wrong `test` fixtures
  (below) disagree with each other on different labels.
- **The shared confidence gate's own frozen value (0.77) is chosen with `target_accuracy=1.0` on
  the pooled (passage, label) decisions**, not `min_coverage`: with only one wrong pooled decision
  on `validation` (`va08`'s `redirect`, confidence 0.76), every `min_coverage` from 0 to 1 picked
  the same degenerate gate (the minimum observed confidence, 0.40), because nothing forced a real
  trade-off. `target_accuracy=1.0` instead picks the lowest threshold with perfect accuracy on the
  answered subset, which lands at 0.77 -- just above `va08`'s own 0.76 -- and gives a populated
  band either side of it (confidences from 0.40 to 0.96 appear on `validation`, with several
  distinct values close to the frozen gate, so there is no empty gap around it).
- **Two `test` fixtures are confidently wrong on purpose and both evade the gate, by construction,
  to exhibit the gate's own documented blind spot** (`docs/evaluation.md`, "Noul three-path
  pattern": "the gate is structurally blind to this shape of error"): `ta10` (`redirect` 0.89, just
  under the 0.90 threshold, confidence 0.78) is a missed attack; `tb05` (`redirect` 0.91, just
  over the threshold, confidence 0.82) is a wrongly-flagged quotation. One `validation` fixture
  (`va08`, `redirect` 0.88, confidence 0.76) is the mirror case the gate *does* catch, by one
  hundredth of a point of confidence -- shown up close in "One answer up close" and named directly
  in `evaluation-note-md`, so the contrast is visible rather than asserted.
- **The task-level outcome's selective coverage/accuracy/risk is reported with
  `evaluate_outcomes(accepted, correct)`**, per the issue's own design note, even though this
  rule's only review branch is the shared confidence gate (so `evaluate_selective` would agree on
  every field but `threshold` -- not exercised here, since the issue names `evaluate_outcomes`
  specifically). The pooled, per-(passage, label) confidence-only view is reported separately with
  `pool_label_decisions` + `evaluate_selective`, at a different granularity (one row per label
  decision, not per passage), and the notebook says so (`evaluation-pooled-md`) rather than
  implying the two numbers are the same quantity.
- **`helpers.excerpt` bounds the state at 320 characters**, cut at a word boundary. One `test`
  fixture (`ta05`) is deliberately longer than that, with the redirect instruction placed early
  enough to survive the cut and padding placed after it that does not; `tests/test_helpers.py`
  pins both the general truncation behaviour and this specific fixture.
- **The review queue excludes `demo` rows and is sorted once, by `helpers.review_sort_key`
  (the lower of the two labels' own confidence), before any item is submitted** -- `ReviewQueue`
  itself preserves submission order, so a queue that reads sorted has to be sorted before
  submission, not after (recipe 15's own pattern, cited in `docs/notebook-ci.md`'s lineage of this
  convention).
- **The one explicit `###` subsection beyond the template's nine headings** ("Why one shared gate,
  and its blind spot," under "Python's part") exists because the gate's structural blind spot is a
  single, self-contained point the issue's build notes ask for ("say so and show one"), and nesting
  it under "Python's part" keeps the nine fixed headings intact per `docs/recipe-template.md`.

## Unfinished / known gaps

- **`tests/test_recipe_guard.py::test_every_recipe_is_linked_from_some_other_recipes_next_steps[26-prompt-injection-screening]`
  fails, and is the *only* failing test in the full suite (both Pythons; 2881 passed, 4 skipped
  otherwise on 3.14).** This recipe is brand new: no recipe already on `main` links forward to it
  in its own "Next steps" (a forward link to an unpublished recipe is itself disallowed), so no
  published recipe can satisfy this check for recipe 26 until a later sweep adds an inbound link
  from an existing recipe (the same pattern visible in this repository's history for recipes 1-23,
  fixed up in batched "Sweep" pull requests after the fact). This recipe's own "Next steps" links
  `../15-sensitive-text-triage/` and `../16-discord-moderation-triage/` by slug, matching the
  catalog's decision types for each, and both resolve (`next_steps_links_exist` passes). I did not
  add an allowlist entry to `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` (out of scope for a recipe pull
  request in any case, and the orchestrator's own guidance on this wave confirmed the gap is
  structural, tracked for a foundation fix, not something to work around here).
- `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until the integration worker regenerates the root
  `README.md` against current `main`, per the generated-README exception.
- No shared-package gap was found that this recipe had to work around.

title: Recipe 27: Function selection
body:
Closes #27

## What this adds

`recipes/27-function-selection/`: Jev picks exactly one function from a preapproved catalog of six fabricated functions (`send_email`, `schedule_meeting`, `create_ticket`, `set_reminder`, `update_record`, `lookup_contact`), each held as data in `helpers.py` with a one-line description and a typed argument schema (required/optional, enumerations), or the fallback `no_function`. The seven options are shuffled per request with `jev_cookbook.fixtures.stable_shuffle`, seeded on this recipe's slug and the request id, and the notebook prints a gold-position table over all 38 scored requests confirming the gold function is not concentrated at the front.

The composed rule in `helpers.resolve` gates every option (`no_function` included) on confidence first (`"confidence below the threshold"`), then, for a real function cleared at the gate, runs a second, deterministic stage: `helpers.validate_arguments` checks the arguments Python's own tested extractor (`helpers.extract_arguments`) recovered from the request's `"Arguments: ..."` trailer against that function's own schema, reporting every violation (missing required, wrong type, value outside the enumeration). A valid match is recorded in a simulated `ActionLog`; an invalid one, or a low-confidence one, goes to a simulated `ReviewQueue` naming the reason. `no_function` passes CONTRIBUTING.md section 4's three-part test (worked through in the notebook's "Python's part" section) but is gated like every other option rather than exempted, so no counterfactual needs printing.

Evaluation is at task level as well as per question: per-question selection accuracy (raw choice vs. gold), the use case's named invalid-argument rejection rate, and `jev_cookbook.evaluation.evaluate_outcomes` (never `evaluate_selective`, since the rule's review branch is more than the confidence gate) for task-level coverage/accuracy/risk, where "correct" means the final outcome *and*, for an executed request, which function actually ran, matches what a flawless rule would have done with the same extracted arguments. This catches a confidently wrong selection that a pure confidence-gate or selection-accuracy view cannot: on `test`, one request's gold function is `lookup_contact`, but Jev confidently (0.85) names `send_email` instead, and because the request also happens to supply valid `to`/`subject`/`body` values, stage two's validator finds nothing wrong with the (wrong) function it actually ran — so it is wrongly, confidently executed. That is the `test` split's one task-level mistake (risk `0.0714`); selection accuracy and the invalid-argument rejection rate both read it as fine.

## Decisions

- **`no_function` is gated like every other option, not exempted.** It passes all three parts of CONTRIBUTING.md section 4's test (worked through explicitly in the notebook), but gating a qualifying fallback anyway is compliant and avoids a second review-reason convention; no gated counterfactual is needed because nothing is exempted.
- **Arguments live inside the request text's own `"Arguments: k=v; k=v"` trailer**, recovered by a tested extractor (`helpers.extract_arguments`), never a hand-written dict in `ROWS` — this is what the issue's build notes ask for ("the state is a user request plus the arguments the request supplies").
- **The argument validator checks exactly three violation kinds** (missing required, wrong type, value outside the enumeration), matching the acceptance criteria precisely; it does not flag an unscheduled extra argument as a fourth kind.
- **Task-level correctness requires matching both the outcome *and*, for an executed request, which function executed** — not just whether the final outcome category matches. This is what lets the evaluation catch "confidently wrong, but still executes" as an error, which per-question selection accuracy alone cannot.
- **The gold-position table and per-item shuffle use `stable_shuffle`**, never `random.shuffle` or the catalog's own authored order (docs/fixtures.md's documented-stable requirement).
- **Threshold `0.6000...`**, chosen with `select_confidence_threshold(target_accuracy=1.0)` on `validation`: validation carries one wrong-but-visible-to-the-selector answer at confidence 0.55 (`v14`), which the gate excludes; `test` separately carries the confidently-wrong, schema-valid mistake (`t14`) that the frozen gate does *not* catch, giving the non-zero `test` risk.
- **Next steps** link `04-support-ticket-routing`, `08-faq-selection` and `19-ci-failure-classification` by slug — all `Choice` decisions already published on `main`.

## Known gap: `next_steps_inbound_links`

The full suite was run on both Python 3.10 and Python 3.14, under the shared heavy-job slot: **exactly one test fails, on both interpreters**, `tests/test_recipe_guard.py::test_every_recipe_is_linked_from_some_other_recipes_next_steps[27-function-selection]` (2881 passed, 4 skipped, 1 failed, both times). No other published recipe's Next steps section links `../27-function-selection/` yet, and none can — no recipe on `main` can link forward to one that does not exist yet, so this fails structurally for every newly-added recipe, not something introduced by this recipe's own content. This recipe's own scope (`recipes/27-function-selection/**` only) cannot fix it either: doing so would mean editing another recipe's notebook. No allowlist entry was added (`tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` is unchanged) and no other recipe was touched. Every *other* parametrized case for this recipe in `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` passes. Expect `Catalog (README is current)` red (the generated-README exception) and this one `next_steps_inbound_links` case red in `Tests (py3.10)`/`Tests (py3.14)`; every other check should be green.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/27-function-selection/` (verified with `tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --branch recipe/27-function-selection --body-file ...`: `scope ok`)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` — not run by this builder; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until the integration worker runs it, per the generated-README exception
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/27-function-selection/` paths, all mode `100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (`tools/execute_notebook.py`, twice, byte-identical)
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1`/`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MODEL`/`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`; same `helpers.build_questions`)
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which mode it ran in (`run_header`)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (invalid arguments of each violation kind, no match, ambiguous between two functions, a validation-visible wrong answer, a confidently-wrong-and-executed test answer), and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (`ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue`, never a real call)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels; the issue names no baseline to compare against
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network, outputs committed — verified with `tools/execute_notebook.py`, run twice, byte-identical
- [x] Live mode is opt-in and uses the same question definitions — `helpers.build_questions`/`helpers.build_state` are shared by both paths; README "Switch to live" states the real count (40 calls)
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases named in the build notes, carry gold labels, pass `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/27-function-selection` (`fixtures valid (mode replay)`)
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states its mode (`run_header`)
- [x] Evaluation: selection accuracy (0.9474 both splits) and the invalid-argument rejection rate (1.0000 both splits, 3 hard cases each)
- [x] The deterministic composition (`helpers.resolve`, `helpers.validate_arguments`, `helpers.task_correct`, `helpers.accepted_and_correct`) lives in `helpers.py` with tests in `tests/test_helpers.py`
- [x] Evaluation is at task level (`evaluate_outcomes` on `accepted`/`task_correct`) as well as per question (`accuracy` on the raw choice)
- [x] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference; synthetic metrics are labelled `{check}` (and `{selection}` on `validation`) throughout
- [x] README states what the recipe teaches, how to run it, and what was/was not measured live
- [x] The pull request changes only `recipes/27-function-selection/`; CI is expected to be fully green except `Catalog (README is current)` (red until the integration worker runs) — see the known-gap note above for `next_steps_inbound_links` specifically

## How it was verified

All commands run from the repository root of this worktree, in a `uv`-managed venv (Python 3.10 for `pytest`/`ruff`, Python 3.14 with `.[ml]` and `-c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt` for the notebook execution, per `docs/recipe-template.md` step 6):

```
python build_fixtures.py                                   # from recipes/27-function-selection: wrote 40 examples, 38 labels, 40 responses
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/27-function-selection   # fixtures valid (mode replay)
pytest recipes/27-function-selection                         # 26 passed
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/27-function-selection   # run twice; diff of the two runs is empty (byte-identical)
ruff check .                                                 # All checks passed! (restricted to recipes/27-function-selection; repo-wide also clean)
```
