Refs #19

## What this adds

Sweep #163 batch D: the recipe-side contract fixes for merged recipes 16 (discord-moderation-triage), 17 (passage-reranking), 18 (duplicate-incident-matching) and 19 (ci-failure-classification), driven by the `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` allowlist and the routed issue-#163 comments naming these four recipes. A sweep PR on a published recipe cannot use `recipe/<slug>` (taken by the merged PR), so this is a `foundation/<topic>` branch per "Sweep PRs on published recipes" in `BUILDER_RULES.md`; the diff stays inside the four recipe folders plus the one allowed foundation path, `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` (entries removed only, none added).

Branched from `main` at `7a72248` (pinned), then merged forward to `a9e0bd9` (#188, candidate-threshold deduplication) before the final notebook executions, per the orchestrator's mid-task note — the merge was clean, no conflicts, and `#188`'s own statement that "every frozen gate in every published recipe [is] unchanged" held for all four of this batch's gates (re-verified below).

### Recipe 16 (discord-moderation-triage)

**Allowlist entries removed:** `build_fixtures_scaffold`, `no_issue_citations`, `stored_answers_strong_form`.

**Files touched:** `README.md`, `build_fixtures.py`, `helpers.py`, `notebook.ipynb`, `tests/test_build_fixtures.py`, `tests/test_helpers.py`.

- `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` regenerated byte-for-byte from `tools/new_recipe.py::build_fixtures_test_text` (drops the pre-#162 docstring and adds the inputs/labels regeneration assertion).
- Dropped "the issue"/"The issue" from `helpers.py`, `build_fixtures.py`, `README.md` and two notebook cells (`evaluation-outcomes-md`, `evaluation-outcomes-note`).
- `helpers.py` and the notebook's "Python's part" cell (`python-md`) no longer call `ignore` "no side effect" (it writes an `ActionLog` entry) or treat `review_needed` as a candidate for the no-gate exemption. Reworded to the three-part test: `allowed` is a complete answer (passes (a)) but fails (b) (the `ActionLog` entry) and (c) (a wrongly-allowed violating message stays live, unwarned); `review_needed` fails (a) outright (naming it is itself a deferral). Both are gated for these reasons, same as `potentially_violating`.
- `"## Simulating the moderator queue"` promoted to a `###` subsection of "Python's part" (the fixed nine-section table of contents).
- `tests/test_helpers.py::test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` rewritten to re-derive the frozen gate with `select_confidence_threshold` on `validation` and assert a confidently wrong `test` answer at or above it (strong form; was the weak "some wrong answer exists" form).
- Also added an inbound Next-steps link from 16 to 19 (see "Cross-recipe Next-steps links" below).

**Numbers:** unchanged. No evaluation code or fixtures changed; only prose, a heading level, one test's derivation style, and `tests/test_build_fixtures.py`'s scaffold text. The notebook was re-executed to confirm this (see "Notebook executions" below); the diff after execution was empty.

### Recipe 17 (passage-reranking)

**Allowlist entries removed:** `build_fixtures_scaffold`, `no_issue_citations`, `metric_lines_carry_check`, `next_steps_inbound_links`.

**Files touched:** `helpers.py`, `notebook.ipynb`, `tests/test_build_fixtures.py`.

- `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` regenerated from the current scaffold.
- Dropped the three "the issue" citations in `helpers.py` (the business-cutoff comment and the two lexical-baseline docstrings).
- The six-row risk-coverage sweep loop in the `selective` cell now carries `{check}` (it reports `test`, so no `{selection}` label applies) — these rows previously carried no disclosure label at all.
- `"## Candidate sets and the lexical baseline"` promoted to a `###` subsection of "Python's part"; `"## Ranking: nDCG and top-1 accuracy"` promoted to a `###` subsection of "Evaluation".
- Inbound Next-steps link added from recipe 18 (see below), giving 17 an inbound link.

**Numbers:** unchanged (the six sweep rows' own figures were already correct; only their printed disclosure label changed). Notebook re-executed; diff after execution was a label-only text change in that one cell, confirmed byte-identical on a second execution.

### Recipe 18 (duplicate-incident-matching)

**Allowlist entries removed:** `build_fixtures_scaffold`, `no_issue_citations`, `validation_lines_carry_selection_and_check`, `metric_lines_carry_check`, `figure_titles_check_only`.

**Files touched:** `build_fixtures.py`, `fixtures/inputs.jsonl`, `fixtures/labels.jsonl`, `fixtures/responses.json`, `notebook.ipynb`, `tests/test_build_fixtures.py`.

- `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` regenerated from the current scaffold.
- Dropped the "the issue" citation in `build_fixtures.py`.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md §5 fix:** `build_fixtures.py` named the real product "Slack" in one fixture's ticket text; row `t10-nomatch-slack` renamed to `t10-nomatch-chatops`, text changed to a generic "internal chat notification integration". Fixtures regenerated from `ROWS` (no `--force` needed; the stored answer was already `synthetic`).
- Added `{check}` to every validation metric line that previously carried only `{selection}` (the gate line in "Python's part", the sweep rows and the figure title in "The gate sweep", and the match-accuracy/coverage/accuracy/risk/false-merge-rate lines in "Evaluation" and "The simulated side effect"). Also corrected a comment that asserted the opposite of the actual rule ("a validation number never carries the `check` label" → corrected to say it carries both).
- `"## The simulated side effect"` promoted to a `###` subsection of "Evaluation".
- Renamed the recipe's `-note`-suffixed discussion-cell ids and the `next-steps` cell id to the template's `-md` suffix convention (`upclose-near-dup-note` → `upclose-near-dup-md`, `evaluation-validation-note` → `evaluation-validation-md`, `evaluation-test-note` → `evaluation-test-md`, `per-class-no-match-note` → `per-class-no-match-md`, `side-effect-note` → `side-effect-rates-md` to avoid colliding with the existing `side-effect-md` heading cell, `next-steps` → `next-md`); no id collisions.
- **§4 counterfactual added:** `no_match` passes all three parts of CONTRIBUTING.md section 4's exemption test (a complete answer; `record_resolution` logs nothing for `no_duplicate`; a wrong `no_match` leaves exactly one ticket unmatched, no more than `review` would also have left pending) — confirmed against `docs/evaluation.md`'s own recipe-18 table. The notebook previously claimed this without showing the cost. New cells (`side-effect-counterfactual-md`, `side-effect-counterfactual`) print `evaluate_selective` (the frozen gate reapplied to `no_match` too, over every answer's own `.confidence`) beside the `evaluate_outcomes` numbers already shown, on both splits.
- Inbound Next-steps link added to 17 (candidate-set/retrieval-baseline kinship).

**Numbers re-derived (notebook executed twice, byte-identical):**
- The `t10` fixture rename changes that one example's replay key; its stored answer (`no_match` at confidence 0.80) and gold label (`no_match`) are unchanged, so no existing evaluation number moves.
- New counterfactual numbers (first appearance, not a change to an existing figure): printed by the notebook itself, not typed here, since the whole point of this fix is that the reader sees them computed from the data in the cell.

### Recipe 19 (ci-failure-classification)

**Allowlist entries removed:** `no_issue_citations`, `stored_answers_strong_form`, `next_steps_inbound_links`.

**Files touched:** `build_fixtures.py`, `fixtures/inputs.jsonl`, `fixtures/responses.json`, `helpers.py`, `notebook.ipynb`, `tests/test_helpers.py`.

**Orchestrator ruling 4** (`docs/evaluation.md`, "Coverage counts delivered answers", tracked from #164 and #163 comment 6083377550): a confidently-accepted `unknown` diagnosis is still a deferral under CONTRIBUTING.md section 4 part (a) — naming it is itself asking a person to find the real cause — so it must not count toward coverage, whatever its confidence.

- `helpers.py`: new `accepted_and_correct(diagnoses, gold)` builds the narrower `accepted` array `evaluate_outcomes` needs (`True` only for the three substantive outcomes; `False` for `unknown` and for a confidence-gated `review` alike). `classify`'s docstring no longer claims `evaluate_selective` "reports the same split" — it does not, now that an accepted `unknown` and a gated `review` are excluded from coverage for different reasons.
- Notebook: both evaluation cells (`eval-validation-code`, `eval-test-code`) switch from `evaluate_selective` to `evaluate_outcomes(accepted, correct)`; `eval-md`, `eval-validation-discuss` and `eval-test-discuss` rewritten for a first-time reader.
- **Numbers re-derived** (every one printed by the notebook itself; independently re-verified against the live backend before writing any prose):
  - Validation coverage: **0.7368 → 0.6316** (14 → 12 of 19; the 2 confident `unknown` builds move out of the answered count). Accuracy and risk **unchanged** at 1.0000 / 0.0000 (both excluded builds were right, so removing them from the denominator costs nothing).
  - Test coverage: **0.7895 → 0.6316** (15 → 12 of 19; 3 confident `unknown` builds move out). Accuracy: **0.8667 → 0.9167** (11 of 12). Risk: **0.1333 → 0.0833** (1 of 12). Reason: `t-tr-05-wrong`'s confident `unknown` no longer counts as a wrong *answered* build (it is a deferral, now excluded from the count rather than a wrong one inside it); `t-dep-02-surfaces` remains the one wrong answer among the 12 that count.
  - **Unchanged:** the confusion matrix, raw-choice accuracy (0.8947), the two baselines, `ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue` tallies on both splits (validation 4/4/4 actions, 5+2 queue; test 5/3/4 actions, 4+3 queue), the frozen gate itself (`0.4400`) and its sweep (19 rows, 14 zero-risk, first risk at `0.3600`) — none of these depended on the accepted/deferral distinction; re-verified independently against the live backend, not only by reading the notebook's own printed output.
- **Review carry-overs** (comment 6079019076, "Suggestions for a later pass"):
  - `--tb=line`'s log (`_regression_log_scattered`, used by `t-tr-05-wrong`) now passes plain file paths (dropped `::test_name`), matching its own docstring's claimed format (`path:lineno: Exception message`).
  - The two collection-stage dependency logs (`_dependency_collection_log`, used by `v-dep-02`, `t-dep-04`) now run under `poetry install` instead of a `pip` command line — `"version solving failed"` is Poetry's/PDM's resolver wording, not pip's, so the tool and the message now agree.
  - `gate-sweep-code` now prints the swept threshold count; `gate-sweep-discuss` no longer states "eighteen distinct steps" where the table has nineteen rows.
  - `dependency_problem`'s and `test_regression`'s criteria descriptions now state the same overlap clause (when an excerpt shows both, the import/module error governs), so either is self-sufficient to a reader of just one.
  - New `tests/test_helpers.py::test_the_scattered_regression_excerpt_carries_both_failures` pins that `t-tr-05-wrong`'s excerpt (not just its full log) carries both `AssertionError` lines, the basis the hedge relies on.
  - `classify`'s membership-check comment now cites `docs/recipe-template.md` (not `docs/backends.md`) for the "equally acceptable alternative to a defensive membership branch" ruling.
- Dropped the "the issue" citation in `build_fixtures.py`.
- `tests/test_helpers.py::test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` rewritten to re-derive the frozen threshold with `select_confidence_threshold` inside its own body (strong form; the guard's `_find_function_body` only sees one function's own text, so the pre-existing, separate `test_a_wrong_test_answer_survives_the_frozen_gate` — kept, still passing, now redundant with the rewritten function — did not satisfy the check on its own). New `test_accepted_and_correct_excludes_a_confident_unknown_from_coverage` pins the ruling-4 helper directly.
- **Fixtures regenerated from `ROWS`** (no `--force` needed; nothing was `recorded`): the criteria-text change (overlap clause) alters every replay key since criteria are shared by every request; the two log-text changes (`--tb=line`, `poetry install`) and the one row-id rename alter their own. `labels.jsonl` is byte-identical (no gold label changed).

### Cross-recipe Next-steps links

Recipes 17 and 19 each had no inbound Next-steps link from any published recipe (`next_steps_inbound_links`). Per the brief, both links come from within this batch (16–19), chosen for genuine kinship rather than merely to satisfy the check:

- **16 → 19**: both route every outcome through the same `jev_cookbook.simulation.ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue` pair, in an operations setting (19) rather than a trust-and-safety one (16).
- **18 → 17**: both assemble a candidate set in Python — a retrieval shortlist (18), a lexical baseline (17) — before any question reaches Jev.

Added as an extra clause to each source recipe's existing "Neighbouring recipes" bullet, not a new bullet; the other links in both bullets are untouched.

## Notebook executions

Every notebook whose cells changed was executed in place with `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>` under the shared heavy slot, twice, and the two runs were byte-identical; a third verification pass (after committing) was also byte-identical and `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` confirmed each against its committed state with no diagnostic beyond the expected figure-match lines. Recipe 16's notebook was executed too (to be certain the prose/heading-only edits produced no output drift) and needed no new commit: the fresh execution was byte-identical to what was already committed.

## Decisions

- Recipe 16/17's `##`→`###` heading fixes and the Next-steps link additions do not change any printed number, so no notebook re-execution was strictly required for them alone, but every notebook in this batch was executed anyway (see above) to be certain.
- Recipe 18's Slack fabrication used a generic replacement ("internal chat notification integration") rather than inventing a plausible fictional product name, since CONTRIBUTING.md's rule is "fabricated names and numbers only" and a bare description needs no invented brand to track.
- Recipe 18's cell-id rename to the template's `-md` convention was scoped to recipe 18 only, per the issue's explicit per-recipe list; recipe 16 (and others outside this batch) still has `-note`-suffixed markdown cell ids (`evaluation-outcomes-note`) that the same PR #186 finding names generically. Leaving it is consistent with the issue's own per-recipe scoping and with `docs/recipe-template.md`'s own description of the suffix convention as "cosmetic, not a correctness rule" with no CI check behind it; not fixed here to avoid widening this batch's diff beyond what was asked.
- Recipe 19's ruling-4 fix does not touch `classify`'s own branching logic, `ActionLog`/`ReviewQueue` population, or the confidence gate's selection — only how the notebook's evaluation cells build the `accepted` array for `evaluate_outcomes`. This was verified independently against the live backend before any prose was written (see the numbers above), not inferred from the review comment's table alone (which predates ruling 4 and reported the old, since-superseded `0.7895` figure as correct in its own time).
- Keeping both `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` (now self-contained, strong form) and the pre-existing `test_a_wrong_test_answer_survives_the_frozen_gate` (same derivation, kept, not removed) in recipe 19's tests is accepted duplication: removing the latter was not asked for, and the guard only requires the former to bind.

## Nothing deliberately left unfinished

Every allowlist entry for recipes 16–19 that `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` listed at the start of this work is removed and its check now genuinely passes (verified by removing the entry and re-running the guard, not merely by fixing the recipe and trusting it). No entry was added.

## How it was verified

- `pytest recipes/<slug> -k ...` and `pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k <slug>` per recipe, on Python 3.14 (`.[dev,ml]` + `.github/constraints-notebooks.txt`) and Python 3.10 (`.[dev]`), all passing.

- `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>` for each, twice (plus a third verification pass after committing), byte-identical every time; `python tools/check_notebook_fresh.py <committed> <fresh>` for each: fresh.

Catalog (README is current) is expected to be red"), which no longer applies now that these recipes are published — 22's README already had the corrected wording ("this recipe is published... a later pull request... leaves the root README.md untouched... Catalog (README is current) stays green"); 20, 21 and 23 now match it. (Flagged by issue #163 comment 6080094734 for 22 specifically, with a note to check the others.)

2. **22's cell-id renames are cosmetic**, per `docs/recipe-template.md`'s own framing ("every id is semantic either way... but it is the first thing anyone diffing two recipes' cells notices"); nothing in the guard or CI keys off these specific ids.

title: Foundation: guard catalog/recipes.json's per-row shape and sources
body:
Closes #151

## What this adds

`tests/test_catalog_shape.py` (new): guards `catalog/recipes.json`'s per-row shape and sources
directly, independent of publication status. Before this, `tests/test_recipe_sources.py` only
parametrized rows whose `notebook.ipynb` exists, and no renderer region prints per-recipe
sources, so an edit that dropped a source id from an unpublished row left every existing check
green (per the Opus review of #149, comment 6071881469).

Checks, for all 60 rows in `catalog/recipes.json`:

- exactly 60 recipes, ranks `1..60` contiguous and in that order;
- every slug is unique and matches the `NN-slug` folder convention, with `NN` equal to its own
  rank;
- `decision_types` is non-empty and drawn only from `{Choice, Noul, Score}`;
- `sources` is non-empty, holds only `S<digits>`-shaped ids, is sorted, duplicate-free, and every
  id it lists is present in the root README's generated `## Sources` table;
- `S02` (Primitives) and `S03` (Confidence) are present on every row, since every recipe asks a
  typed question and every recipe's helpers derive or threshold a confidence.

Mutation-proven: removed `S02` from the unpublished row `24-incident-priority-composition`,
confirmed `test_every_row_lists_primitives_and_confidence[24-incident-priority-composition]`
fails with the exact missing id, then reverted (`git status` clean afterward).

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — foundation/tests-only pull request; no `recipes/` path touched.

## How it was verified

Two reused `uv` venvs (`uv venv --python 3.14` with `.[dev,ml]` under
`.github/constraints-notebooks.txt`, and `uv venv --python 3.10` with `.[dev]`), each installed
editable from this worktree. No `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE` unset, no `.env` read, no
live call.

- `ruff check .` — All checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .` — 216 files already formatted.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` — exit 0, no output.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — "Hygiene check passed: 309 file(s) scanned."
- Targeted: `pytest -q tests/test_catalog_shape.py` — 244 passed, on both 3.14 and 3.10.
- Mutation (above), reverted; clean `git status` confirmed before committing.
- Full suite, once, in the foreground under the shared `HEAVY.lock` slot,
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=MKL_NUM_THREADS=OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`, `nice -n 10 timeout 1500`:
  - py3.14: **2706 passed, 4 skipped, 108 xfailed in 95.89s**
  - py3.10: **2706 passed, 4 skipped, 108 xfailed in 110.00s**
  - Lock released via trap in the same call; no stray `pytest`/`execute_notebook` process of
    mine afterward.

## Decisions

- Put the test in its own new file, `tests/test_catalog_shape.py`, rather than inside
  `tests/test_render_catalog.py`: the issue offered either path, and this check is about the
  catalog's own data shape, not about the renderer the other file exercises against a throwaway
  project tree.
- Read the known source ids from the root README's real, generated `## Sources` table (the same
  technique `tests/test_recipe_sources.py`'s `_readme_source_ids` already uses for a recipe
  README), rather than re-deriving them from `catalog/recipes.json["sources"]` itself. The issue
  asks for "every id present in the README sources table" specifically; reading the catalog's own
  `sources` array instead would make this check vacuous against the one drift case the README
  comparison actually guards (catalog and README disagreeing).
- `S02`/`S03` are required as a flat pair on every row rather than inferred per `decision_types`
  (for example requiring `S03` only for `Noul`/`Score` rows): the issue states "S02 and S03 are
  listed on every row" without a decision-type condition, and the current catalog already
  satisfies this for all 60 rows, so no row needed reclassifying to pass.
- Did not add a check on `category` values (no fixed vocabulary is defined anywhere in the
  catalog or `CONTRIBUTING.md`, unlike `decision_types`), or on `level` matching an entry in
  `catalog["levels"]`: neither is named in the issue's acceptance criteria, and the brief's rule
  not to widen scope beyond the issue applies to what a test checks, not only to which files it
  touches.

## Unsure / possible follow-up

- None of the three prior catalog-drift incidents the issue cites (#142/#145, #147/#149) involved
  rank or slug corruption, only sources; I added the rank/slug/decision_types checks anyway
  because the issue's acceptance text asks for them explicitly ("ranks 1..60... unique slugs
  matching NN-slug... decision_types drawn from {Choice, Noul, Score}").

  `confidence` used in prose with no glossary link, across all five recipes) is real but was not
  in this batch's named work list (only `gold label` was named, in the Wave 1 review's S12 item,
  for 01/02/05/07) and is not gated by any check in `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`.
  Recipe 01 in particular overloads the plain English word "review" with the domain noun
  ("customer review", the text being classified) throughout, which makes a mechanical sweep of
  every occurrence risky to do safely in this batch; flagging it here rather than guessing.
- `##` sibling sections and off-convention cell-id suffixes are a named #163 item, but only for
  recipes 11/16/17/18/22 (per the PR #186 review) — none of 01–05 has this problem.
  `review_value_is_review` / `review_reason_string` exactness was checked for all five; only 02's
  reason string needed fixing (already listed above).
- Recipe 02's threshold-sweep and risk-coverage figures changed pixel content by a small, expected
  amount after merging up to #188 (one near-duplicate candidate collapses); this is upstream's
  fix doing its job, not something to work around.

## How it was verified

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`: clean.
- `pytest recipes/01-sentiment-classification recipes/02-refund-intent-detection
  recipes/03-response-clarity-scoring recipes/04-support-ticket-routing
  recipes/05-document-classification`: 93 passed, on both the 3.14 (`.[dev,ml]` +
  `.github/constraints-notebooks.txt`) and 3.10 (`.[dev]`) venvs.
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/<slug>` for all five: valid (mode replay).
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k "<slug>"` for all five: 70 passed (0 xfailed, 0 skipped) — see
  the allowlist-entries section above.
- Each changed notebook executed twice in place, under the heavy slot, with
  `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>`: byte-identical both before and after merging
  up to `main`'s `a9e0bd9`.
- `python tools/check_notebook_fresh.py <committed-copy> <fresh-execution>` for all five: "matches
  a fresh offline run", every figure "identical bytes".
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed, 310 files scanned.
- `python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --branch
  foundation/sweep-163-a --body-file <this body>`: `scope ok: foundation pull request: the
  recipe allowlist does not apply` (confirmed anyway that the actual diff stays inside
  `recipes/01..05-*/` and `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`).
- Full suite once, under the heavy slot: `pytest -q` → 2498 passed, 4 skipped, 79 xfailed (the
  remaining #163 allowlist entries for recipes outside this batch), no failures.

## Decisions

- `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` is regenerated byte-for-byte from
  `tools/new_recipe.py::build_fixtures_test_text`, which means recipe 01 loses the extra
  `test_a_simulated_recording_produces_a_minimal_diff` test it had accreted; that test's
  assertion is already made by the template's own test suite for the same writer, so nothing is
  lost in coverage.
- The strong-form `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` mirrors each recipe's own notebook
  threshold-selection code exactly (same `select_confidence_threshold`/`select_threshold` calls,
  same split logic), rather than reusing a shared helper, because no such shared helper exists yet
  (consistent with every other recipe's copy of this test).
- Every added `print(...)` for `print_what_you_plot` reuses the template's own
  `confusion_matrix`-table format (dynamic column width from the longest label, rather than the
  template's fixed 8, since recipe 04's category names are longer).

title: Foundation: parametrised recipe guard over every published recipe (#165)
body:
Closes #165

## What this adds

One parametrised test module, `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`, enforcing nine contract rules
from the Wave 2 consistency review ([issue #76 comment
6079429778](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/76#issuecomment-6079429778),
"Route #165") and the PR #186 review's additions (issue #165 comments
[6079443958](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/165#issuecomment-6079443958) and
[6082395702](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/165#issuecomment-6082395702))
over every published recipe at once, plus the allowlist that keeps CI green while #163 works
through the drift this guard found.

Base: `f2b9ca04f798a74b24e02a8a2cd6d6c05077a87f` (`main` tip, PR #186).

### Checks, rule source, and detection

| # | check id(s) | rule source | detection |
| - | - | - | - |
| 1 | `build_fixtures_scaffold` | G1(a) | `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` byte-identical to `tools/new_recipe.py::build_fixtures_test_text(recipe)` for this recipe |
| 2 | `no_issue_citations` | G1(b), CONTRIBUTING.md §6 | no `#NNN` or "the issue" in a recipe file's prose (docstrings + comments in `.py` files via `ast`/`tokenize`; full text of `README.md` and notebook markdown cells, minus double-quoted spans so a fabricated in-fiction `"invoice #312"` isn't mistaken for an issue citation) |
| 3 | `stored_answers_strong_form` | G1(c) | `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right`'s body re-derives the threshold (`x = select_confidence_threshold(...)`/`select_threshold(...)`) and compares `>= x` against that same name — whatever the recipe calls it (`threshold`, `gate`, ...) |
| 4a | `validation_lines_carry_selection_and_check` | G1(d), CONTRIBUTING.md §2 | a `print(` call in a code cell whose text has a rounded-float format spec (`{x:.4f}`) and the word "validation" must contain both `{selection}` and `{check}` literally |
| 4b | `figure_titles_check_only` | docs/notebook-style.md "Title convention" | `title=` on `plot_confusion_matrix`/`plot_threshold_sweep`/`plot_risk_coverage` carries `{check}` and not `{selection}` (`plot_answer_probabilities`'s one-example titles are out of scope — see Decisions) |
| 5 | `print_what_you_plot` | G1(e), docs/notebook-style.md | every `plot_confusion_matrix`/`plot_risk_coverage` call's first-argument name is mentioned inside a `print(` in the same or the immediately preceding code cell |
| 6 | `next_steps_links_exist` | G1(f), docs/recipe-template.md | every `](../NN-slug/)` in any markdown cell resolves to `recipes/NN-slug/notebook.ipynb` on disk |
| 7a | `review_value_is_review` | docs/glossary.md#review | `helpers.REVIEW == "review"`, skipped where `helpers.py` defines no module-level `REVIEW` |
| 7b | `review_reason_string` | docs/glossary.md#review | the literal string `"confidence below the threshold"` appears in `helpers.py` |
| 8a | `readme_sources_match_catalog` | tests/test_recipe_sources.py | README `## Sources` `S`-ids equal `catalog/recipes.json`'s `sources` for that recipe |
| 8b | `readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers` | CONTRIBUTING.md §2 / docs/live.md | the live-call count stated in "## Switch to live" equals `len(fixtures/responses.json)` |
| 9 | `readme_no_dev_ml_install` | docs/recipe-template.md step 6 | the literal substring `.[dev,ml]` is absent from `README.md` |

Checks 1, 3 and 8b skip (not fail) a scripted recipe with no `fixtures/responses.json`; none are
published yet. Checks 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6, 7a, 7b and 9 also run against `recipes/_template`
(never xfailed — it's the reference every rule is written to match, and running the detection
logic against it caught two bugs in my own regexes during development). Checks 1, 8a and 8b are
catalog-shaped and run only over the 23 published catalog recipes.

## Decisions

- **`next_steps_links_exist` checks only that a forward link resolves (R20), not that every
  recipe is the *target* of some other recipe's Next steps (R21).** R21 is a property of the
  whole set, not of one recipe against one rule — a different kind of test from the other eight,
  which are all per-recipe. Left for a follow-up if wanted; not silently dropped.
- **`figure_titles_check_only` is scoped to `plot_confusion_matrix`/`plot_threshold_sweep`/
  `plot_risk_coverage`, not every `title=` in the notebook.** `plot_answer_probabilities`'s titles
  (the "One answer up close" section) describe one example, not a split's metrics, and the
  template's own plain titles there ("A review with conflicting signal") are correct without
  `{check}`. An unscoped title scan over-flagged roughly 35 compliant titles across the recipes.
- **`print_what_you_plot` keys off the plotted call's first-argument *name*, not "any `print` in
  the cell or the preceding one."** The naive "any print nearby" version false-passed recipe 23
  (confusion matrix plotted with nothing printed, but the *preceding* cell happens to print
  unrelated baseline numbers). Keying off the actual plotted variable's name reproduces Wave 2's
  R4 finding exactly and also catches a second instance (recipe 09) Wave 2 never reviewed
  (it scoped to recipes 11–23 only).
- **`stored_answers_strong_form`'s "at or above the threshold" comparison is matched against
  whatever name the recipe assigned the re-derived cutoff to, not a hardcoded `threshold`.**
  Recipes 11, 17, 18, 21 and 22 call it `gate`; a hardcoded name produced four false failures in
  an early draft.
- **The issue-citation check restricts `.py`-file scanning to docstrings and comments (`ast` +
  `tokenize`), not the whole file, and strips double-quoted spans everywhere else.** Several
  recipes' `build_fixtures.py` embeds fabricated ticket/invoice numbers (`"Invoice #4417"`) as
  fixture content; an unscoped `#\d+` scan produced dozens of false positives there and one more
  in a notebook markdown cell quoting a fixture's raw text (`"...invoice #312..."`, recipe 05).
- **`readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers`'s number is read from either of the two prose
  shapes every current README uses** ("makes exactly one call for each of the *N* ...", "makes
  exactly **N** calls/requests"), tolerant of a markdown line wrap and of "call" vs. "request."
  Two compliant recipes (14, 21) don't additionally restate the count as `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_
  REQUESTS=N` (14 because the budget note is itself a sentence with no override needed below the
  default 25's edge case; 21 because its count, 17, is already under the default 25) — an earlier
  draft keyed only off that assignment and wrongly flagged both.
- **No new CI job.** `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` lives in `tests/`, already in `testpaths`, so
  both `Tests (py3.10)` and `Tests (py3.14)` collect and run it with no workflow change.
- **No `tools/check_recipe_guard.py` CLI.** The guard is a normal parametrised pytest module;
  `pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -k <check_id>` or `-k <slug>` already gives a builder
  everything a bespoke CLI would, so I didn't add one (the brief allowed it "if useful," and I
  judged it wasn't).
- **`tests/test_recipe_sources.py`'s source-matching logic is restated, not imported**, in
  `readme_sources_match_catalog` — four lines, with a comment tying the two together — because
  cross-importing a sibling test module under `--import-mode=importlib` with no package
  `__init__.py` is fragile; `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` is loaded by file path for the
  same reason (`tools/new_recipe.py`'s own loader elsewhere in this module uses the same
  mechanism, so this isn't a new pattern in this repository).

## The allowlist (`tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`)

Running the guard the day it lands found real, pre-existing drift across the first 23 recipes —
most of it beyond the Wave 2 review's own scope (11–23 only), since this guard also covers the
six earlier Level 1 recipes (01–10) that review never read. 77 `(slug, check_id)` pairs are
listed, cross-checked programmatically against the guard's own `xfail` output (exact 1:1 match,
no stray or missing entries). By check:

- **`build_fixtures_scaffold`** (18): 01, 03–10, 12–18 ship the pre-#162 `test_build_fixtures.py`
  (R8); 02 has no such file at all despite a replay `fixtures/responses.json`.
- **`no_issue_citations`** (19): 01–04, 06–13, 15–20, 22, 23 — a private issue cited by number or
  by "the issue" somewhere in the recipe's files (R9/R10).
- **`stored_answers_strong_form`** (15): 01–06, 08–10 have no
  `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` at all; 07, 12, 13, 16, 19, 20 ship only the weak
  `assert wrong, "..."` form (R7).
- **`validation_lines_carry_selection_and_check`** (2): 08, 18 print a validation metric line
  with `{selection}` but not `{check}` (R1).
- **`figure_titles_check_only`** (7): 02, 06, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18 — four different conventions
  across the thirteen Wave 2 read, plus two (02, 06) it never read (R2).
- **`print_what_you_plot`** (2): 09, 23 plot a confusion matrix with no printed table (R4).
- **`next_steps_links_exist`** (1): 21 links an unpublished neighbour (R20).
- **`review_value_is_review`** (1): 09 ships `REVIEW = "unsorted"` (PR #186 review MC3).
- **`review_reason_string`** (3): 02, 06, 10 use a different reason string for the confidence
  gate.
- **`readme_no_dev_ml_install`** (7): 02–04, 06–09 quote the pre-#162 combined install line (R15).

None of these are new regressions — they are the pre-existing state of `main`, now visible to CI.
Each entry's reason string ends `see #163`; a sweep pull request on any of these recipes should
fix the recipe and remove the corresponding entry, never the reverse.

## How it was verified

```
ruff check .                              # All checks passed! (both venvs)
ruff format --check .                     # 215 files already formatted
python tools/check_hygiene.py             # 307 files scanned, passed
python tools/render_catalog.py --check    # exit 0
pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py         # 206 passed, 3 skipped, 77 xfailed — py3.10 and py3.14, identical
pytest -q (full suite, once, under the heavy slot)   # 2439 passed, 6 skipped, 77 xfailed in 96s
```

A cross-check script confirmed the 77 `xfail`ed node ids match `KNOWN_FAILURES`'s 77 keys
exactly (set difference empty both directions) — the allowlist is neither missing a known
failure nor carrying a stale one.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work (no recipe folder touched).

## Unsure / possibly worth a second look

- `readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers`'s regex (two prose shapes, "call" or "request")
  covers every current README but is not a parse of a fixed grammar; a future recipe that states
  the count a third way will fail this check for a reason that isn't a real contract violation.
  I'd rather a reviewer sees this now than discovers it as a confusing red check later.
- `no_issue_citations`'s quote-stripping heuristic (drop `"..."` spans before scanning prose) is a
  judgment call, not something CONTRIBUTING.md states; it's there because of one real false
  positive (recipe 05's quoted "invoice #312") and I could not find a sharper rule that still
  catches genuine citations like recipe 02's "Issue #2 asks for...".
- I did not add R21 (inbound Next-steps coverage) as a check; see Decisions above.

title: Foundation: round Noul/Choice confidence to 12 decimals; regenerate recipes 10 and 15 (#172, #163)
body:
Closes #172
Refs #163
Refs #10
Refs #15

## What this adds

The code half of #172, together with the first item of the #163 sweep (recipes 02, 10 and 15's
regeneration), in one pull request as the orchestrator's decision comment on #172
(6083153183) and PR #187's body require: landing the rounding fix alone would make CI
re-execute every recipe notebook on this foundation PR and fail the `Notebook (<slug>)` checks
for 10 and 15 against their stale committed output.

1. **`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`:** `_conf_inputs` now rounds `conf` to 12 decimal places
   immediately after it is built from `_floats(...)` (and the `[0, 1]` range check), before the
   `_same_length` check and before anything derives candidate thresholds from it. `noul_confidence`'s
   own return is rounded the same way. Both are documented in their own docstrings, and
   `selective_curve`, `select_confidence_threshold`, `evaluate_selective` and `outcome_curve` each
   gained a cross-referencing sentence. No public signature changed; the `[0, 1]` guards are
   unchanged (they run, on the unrounded value, before rounding).

   This closes the gap `docs/evaluation.md` already documented: two hand-written mirror-pair
   fixture literals (`0.42`/`0.58`, `0.07`/`0.93`) that are meant to express the same nominal
   confidence can differ by a few ULPs once `noul_confidence`'s `max(p, 1 - p)` arithmetic runs on
   each literal separately, and without rounding `numpy.unique` kept them as two adjacent threshold
   candidates — a duplicate `gate >= 0.86` row — instead of one.

2. **`tests/test_evaluation.py`:**
   - `test_noul_confidence_rounds_ulp_different_mirror_literals_to_the_same_value`: the raw formula
     really does disagree between `0.42`/`0.58` and between `0.07`/`0.93`; `noul_confidence`'s
     rounding makes each pair agree (`0.16`, `0.86`).
   - `test_selective_curve_collapses_ulp_different_mirror_confidence_into_one_threshold`: feeding
     `noul_confidence([0.42, 0.58, 0.07, 0.93])` into `selective_curve` yields 2 thresholds, not 4.
   - `test_rounding_leaves_ordinary_confidence_values_unchanged`: confidences at ordinary precision
     (4 decimals, 0.0, 1.0, a 12-decimal literal) pass through `selective_curve`/`evaluate_selective`/
     `noul_confidence` completely unmoved; rounding only closes a ~1e-16 gap.
   - `test_noul_confidence_is_mirror_symmetric_and_bit_exact_with_choice` (existing) is restructured:
     the mirror-symmetry/bit-exactness-with-`choice_confidence` claim is now checked against the raw
     formula directly (still true, unaffected by rounding — `choice_confidence` itself is untouched
     and unrounded), with one added line confirming `noul_confidence`'s public return is exactly that
     raw value rounded to 12 decimals. This was a necessary, non-weakening update: the old assertion
     compared `noul_confidence`'s (now rounded) return bit-for-bit against unrounded
     `choice_confidence`, which the new rounding deliberately changes.

3. **Recipes 10 (`answer-relevance-check`) and 15 (`sensitive-text-triage`), regenerated in place**
   (`tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>`, each executed twice under the shared heavy slot,
   confirmed byte-identical both times) **— before/after proof:**

   | recipe | sweep rows before -> after | row removed | surviving duplicate half | frozen gate (`<.2f>`) | `evaluate_selective` (test) |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 10 | 20 -> 19 | `gate >= 0.86: coverage 0.200, accuracy 1.000, risk 0.000` | `gate >= 0.86: coverage 0.240, accuracy 1.000, risk 0.000` (bit-identical) | `0.30` (internal float `0.30000000000000004` -> `0.3`) | coverage 0.840, accuracy 0.952, risk 0.048 — identical |
   | 15 | 19 -> 18 | same row, same wording | same surviving row (bit-identical) | `0.30` (same float change) | coverage 0.840, accuracy 0.952, risk 0.048 — identical |

   `git diff` for each notebook is exactly 2-3 lines: the one duplicate text row removed, and the
   embedded PNG of that recipe's own risk-coverage plot updates to match (same curve data feeds
   both; the dropped point is not collinear there). No other printed number in either notebook moved.
   `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` confirms both notebooks match a second, independent fresh
   execution (the two in-place passes), including their figures.

   **Recipe 02 (`refund-intent-detection`) is unchanged, deliberately.** It carries the same
   `0.07`/`0.93` validation mirror pair, but it prints no per-row sweep text (only
   `curve.accuracy[-1]`/`curve.risk[-1]`, the frozen-gate line, and an argmin row — all identical
   before and after rounding), and the point the rounding drops from its risk-coverage curve is
   collinear with its neighbours on that plot. I confirmed this directly: a fresh in-place execution
   under the slot (then restored, not committed — see "Decisions") differs from the committed file
   only in that one plot cell's PNG bytes, and `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py`'s pixel-tolerant
   `compare_png` reports it as `figure matches, 0 unmatched 2x2 blocks of 64x48 cells` — i.e. no
   visible difference, consistent with the collinear point. `recipes/02-refund-intent-detection/`
   is untouched in this pull request's diff.

4. **`docs/evaluation.md`**, one sentence: the "Hand-written mirror probabilities..." paragraph's
   closing sentence now states the landed convention (`_conf_inputs` and `noul_confidence` round to
   12 decimal places) and that the paragraph describes history, not a live problem, in place of the
   old "#172 tracks this as a separate, later change."

## Decisions

- **Rounding convention:** 12 decimal places, at the one shared boundary (`_conf_inputs`) every
  selective-prediction function funnels through, plus `noul_confidence`'s own return (since a
  caller can read `noul_confidence` directly without going through `_conf_inputs`, e.g. to print a
  confidence or pool it elsewhere). A Choice/Score answer's raw `.confidence` attribute is rounded
  only when it reaches `_conf_inputs`, not at its source (`jev_cookbook.answers.choice_confidence`
  is outside this PR's allowed paths and untouched).
- **Recipe 02 reverted, not regenerated:** my own first pass regenerated all three recipes and
  committed a byte-different (but visually identical) PNG for 02 — a false positive from comparing
  against the old committed file's matplotlib-version-dependent bytes rather than isolating the
  rounding fix's actual effect. PR #187's review (comment 6083358924, "M3") caught this with an
  independent before/after derivation on the real fixtures; I reverted recipe 02's notebook to its
  pre-regeneration content and re-verified with `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` that a fresh
  execution still "matches" it, rather than committing a cosmetic PNG change that cannot survive
  CI's own freshness comparison (it would, trivially, but there is no reason to move those bytes).
- **Why `_conf_inputs` got a docstring and the four public functions got cross-references rather
  than one centralized paragraph:** this module already pairs a short paragraph inline with each
  function's own contract (see `select_confidence_threshold`'s sentinel paragraph, for example);
  consistent with that, each caller's own docstring says it rounds, with `noul_confidence` carrying
  the fullest explanation of *why* (the ULP mechanism), referenced by name from the others.
- **Branch and scope:** `foundation/noul-confidence-rounding-172` (not `recipe/10-...` or
  `recipe/15-...`, both already taken by merged PRs) per "Sweep PRs on published recipes" in the
  builder rules; `Refs #163`, `Refs #10` and `Refs #15` alongside `Closes #172`. The diff stays
  inside `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_evaluation.py`, `docs/evaluation.md` and the
  two recipes' own `notebook.ipynb` files; `README.md` is untouched and `render_catalog.py --check`
  passes unchanged.

## How it was verified

All on the base SHA `f2b9ca04f798a74b24e02a8a2cd6d6c05077a87f` (tip of `main` at branch time;
confirmed still current immediately before push).

- `ruff check .` — All checks passed!
- `ruff format --check .` — 213 files already formatted.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — Hygiene check passed: 307 file(s) scanned.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` — passes (no output, exit 0): `README.md` untouched.
- `pytest tests/test_evaluation.py -q` — 173 passed, on both the `uv`-managed Python 3.14 venv
  (`.[dev,ml] -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`) and a Python 3.10 venv (`.[dev]` only).
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/<slug>` for 02, 10 and 15 — fixtures valid
  (mode replay), unchanged.
- `pytest recipes/02-refund-intent-detection recipes/10-answer-relevance-check
  recipes/15-sensitive-text-triage -q` — 81 passed on 3.14 venv; 254 passed together with
  `tests/test_evaluation.py` on the 3.10 venv.
- `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/<slug>` for 10 and 15, each run twice under the shared
  heavy slot, in place: byte-for-byte identical output both times for each recipe. Recipe 02: one
  verification execution under the slot (then restored, not committed).
- `tools/check_notebook_fresh.py` on each of the three recipes' notebooks against an independent
  fresh execution: all three report "matches a fresh offline run" (02's one differing figure cell
  reports `0 unmatched 2x2 blocks`, i.e. visually identical).
- Full suite under the shared heavy slot, one job: `pytest -q` — 2236 passed, 3 skipped, ~88s (run
  twice across the session, once before and once after the recipe-02 correction; both green).
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` — exactly `docs/evaluation.md`,
  `recipes/10-answer-relevance-check/notebook.ipynb`, `recipes/15-sensitive-text-triage/notebook.ipynb`,
  `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_evaluation.py`. No other recipe's committed output
  moved, and `recipes/02-refund-intent-detection/` does not appear in the diff.

## Unfinished / anything that fought back

Nothing unfinished. The one real snag was my own, described above under "Decisions": my first
regeneration pass touched recipe 02 on a false-positive byte diff (old committed PNG, made by a
different matplotlib version, compared against a fresh run) before the #187 review's independent
derivation caught that the dropped point there is collinear and the figure comparison tool itself
reports no visible difference. That is now corrected and the diff is scoped to 10 and 15 only.

title: Foundation: coverage/ReviewQueue and outcome_curve denominator docs for #172 (code fix blocked, see body)
body:
Refs #172, #164, #163

## What this adds

Two of the three items assigned to this PR landed; the third (#172's own code fix) is
**blocked** and reported below rather than merged — see "Why #172's fix is not in this PR."

1. **`docs/evaluation.md`, orchestrator ruling 4 (#164):** states that an accepted-but-queued
   deferral (`unknown`/`needs_review`/a "manual triage" result sent to a
   `jev_cookbook.simulation.ReviewQueue`) counts as review, not coverage, so
   `evaluate_outcomes`'s `accepted` mask must be `False` for such an example. Worked example:
   recipe 19's fallback was corrected from `ActionLog` to `ReviewQueue` for exactly this reason.
2. **`docs/evaluation.md`, the answered-only denominator disclosure:** states that
   `outcome_curve`'s denominator is always the answered subset it was given
   (`len(confidences)`), never the recipe's whole scored split, and that a recipe which
   short-circuits some examples must print both `outcome_curve`'s N and `evaluate_outcomes`'s N
   side by side. Worked example: recipe 14's `test` split has 21 documents, one of which
   `no_candidates` answers before any question is built, so a curve over the answered 20 and
   `evaluate_outcomes` over all 21 report coverage against two different, both-correct totals.
3. **Reconciliation with #186** (requested mid-task, after #186 merged and rewrote
   CONTRIBUTING.md section 4 as a three-part test): re-quotes section 4's three parts in
   "Showing the counterfactual for an exempted option" in place of the old single "no side
   effect" sentence, re-explains recipe 16's `allowed` as failing parts (b) (its `ignore`
   action is logged to the `ActionLog`) and (c) (a wrongly-allowed violating message stays live
   with nobody warned) rather than "not a fallback option," and clarifies beside the
   placeholder-confidence paragraph that the ban on an in-range stand-in bites only on the three
   functions that derive threshold candidates from the array (`select_confidence_threshold`,
   `selective_curve`, `outcome_curve`) — `evaluate_selective` reapplies an already-frozen
   threshold rather than deriving one, so the same disclosed stand-in (#164 ruling 9) is
   permitted there.

No code changed. `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py` and `tests/test_evaluation.py` are untouched.

## Why #172's fix is not in this PR

#172 asks to round confidence to a fixed number of decimals (12) inside the selective-prediction
input boundary (`_conf_inputs`, shared by `selective_curve`, `select_confidence_threshold`,
`evaluate_selective` and `outcome_curve`) so two independently-stored Noul complements (e.g.
`0.93`/`0.07`) that are a few ULPs apart after `noul_confidence`'s arithmetic collapse into one
candidate threshold instead of printing as a duplicate row. The convention itself is sound and
safe — I confirmed it with the real pipeline, not just a synthetic example:

- Computed `selective_curve` on recipes **02**, **10** and **15**'s actual `validation` fixtures
  (via `get_backend`/`load_helpers`/`noul_confidence`, the same code path each notebook uses),
  before and after rounding confidence to 12 decimals consistently (both the threshold
  *selection* step and the threshold *evaluation* step rounded the same way, not one rounded and
  the other not). Result for all three recipes: the rounded curve has exactly one fewer
  threshold row than the unrounded one, and every surviving threshold's coverage, accuracy and
  risk is bit-identical before and after — only the lower-coverage half of the duplicate pair
  (nominal confidence `0.86` in every case) disappears; the higher-coverage half survives
  unchanged. The frozen gate (`select_confidence_threshold` → `evaluate_selective`) also reports
  the same coverage/accuracy/risk before and after, confirming the fix changes nothing a reader
  relies on.
- But recipes **10** and **15** already print this exact duplicate as two identical-looking
  `gate >= 0.86` rows in their **committed** notebook output (`recipes/10-answer-relevance-check
  /notebook.ipynb`, `recipes/15-sensitive-text-triage/notebook.ipynb`, the validation
  confidence-gate sweep cell). Recipe **02** doesn't print a per-row sweep as text, but its
  `validation` fixtures carry the identical duplicate pair feeding `plot_risk_coverage`, so its
  committed plot's underlying curve has one more point than a freshly-executed one would after
  the fix.
- `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml`'s own comment states a pull request's notebook-execution
  matrix selects every recipe notebook once a change touches anything outside recipe folders and
  `README.md` — which a change to `jev_cookbook.evaluation` is. So landing the rounding fix here
  would make CI re-execute 02, 10 and 15 on this PR's head and diff the fresh output against the
  committed one: the fresh run would collapse the duplicate row (and, for 02, render a
  one-point-shorter curve), disagreeing with what is committed, and the per-recipe
  `Notebook (<slug>)` checks would go red on an unrelated foundation PR.

This is exactly the condition #172's own brief asked this PR to stop and report on. The rounding
is correct and ready (the exact change: round `conf` to 12 decimal places inside `_conf_inputs`
right after it is built from `_floats(...)`, before the `_same_length` check, with the rounding
documented in `_conf_inputs`'s own docstring and cross-referenced from `selective_curve`,
`select_confidence_threshold`, `evaluate_selective`, `outcome_curve` and `noul_confidence`), and a
test exists in my working tree (two stored complements differing in the last ULP — `0.42`/`0.58`
and `0.07`/`0.93` — proving one candidate row results) but is **not committed**, because it only
makes sense alongside the code change. Both are being held out of this PR rather than merged.

**What has to happen first (tracked under #163):** a recipe-side regeneration of 02, 10 and 15's
notebook outputs (re-execute each on current `main`, commit the refreshed output — which, today,
without this fix, is a no-op refresh since nothing about their *inputs* changed) so that once
#172's rounding fix *does* land, the very next execution of those three notebooks already expects
the collapsed row and CI stays green. Only then should #172's fix be merged. `docs/evaluation.md`
is updated (this PR) to record exactly this ordering, so the next builder who picks up #172 does
not need to re-derive it.

## Decisions

- **Convention chosen for #172 (not yet merged, see above):** round at the input boundary
  (`_conf_inputs`), to 12 decimal places, rather than inside `noul_confidence` itself (which
  other, non-selective-prediction callers also use and which has its own bit-exactness
  guarantees worth keeping separate, see `test_noul_confidence_is_mirror_symmetric_and_bit_exact
  _with_choice`) or a separate dedupe re-implemented inside each of `selective_curve` and
  `outcome_curve`. Rounding once at the shared boundary means `selective_curve`,
  `select_confidence_threshold`, `evaluate_selective` and `outcome_curve` all agree automatically
  — no consumer can see a confidence that another one rounded differently.
- **`evaluate_outcomes`'s `accepted` mask and ReviewQueue (ruling 4):** documented as a rule, not
  merely illustrated by recipe 19 — any deferral, logged or not, is `accepted=False`.
- **Why I did not widen the allowed paths:** the blocker above is a `recipes/` problem (stale
  committed notebook output), and this PR's allowed paths are `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`,
  `tests/test_evaluation.py`, `docs/evaluation.md` only. Regenerating 02/10/15 is explicitly a
  `#163` sweep job for a different builder, and foundation builders do not execute recipe
  notebooks locally in any case (BUILDER_RULES, "Foundation PRs: no local notebook executions").

## Unfinished

- #172 itself is **not closed**. The rounding fix and its test are investigated, proven safe in
  isolation, and ready to write, but withheld pending a #163 regeneration of recipes 02, 10 and
  15. This PR carries only the two docs items plus the #186 reconciliation.

## How it was verified

- `ruff check .` — All checks passed!
- `ruff format --check .` — 213 files already formatted (covers the Python code blocks inside
  `docs/*.md`, per `docs/development.md`).
- `pytest tests/test_evaluation.py -q` — 170 passed, on both the `uv`-managed Python 3.14 venv
  and a Python 3.10 venv (`.[dev]` only, no `[ml]`), before and after the merge from `main`.
- `pytest -q` (full suite, one heavy job under the shared slot) — 2224 passed, 3 skipped, 90.08s.
- `selective_curve` before/after-rounding comparison on recipes 02, 10, 15's real validation
  fixtures (ad hoc script, not committed) — see "Why #172's fix is not in this PR" above for the
  result.
- No committed file outside `docs/evaluation.md` changed in this branch's own commits (confirmed
  with `git diff --stat` against the merge base).

Base SHA: `9c4f51a139597bfb8486f7cc0bb08cd7473f63c8` (tip of `main` at branch time, before #186
merged as `f2b9ca0`; this branch later merged `origin/main` at `f2b9ca0` to pick up #186's
CONTRIBUTING section 4 rewrite before pushing, per the orchestrator's mid-task addition).

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — foundation work, no recipe folder touched.

## Acceptance criteria (issue #172)

- Round (or dedupe) confidence before candidate thresholds are taken, documented in
  `docs/evaluation.md` and the docstrings — **designed, not merged** (see above).
- Test with two stored complements differing in the last ULP proving one candidate row results
  — **written locally, not committed** (same reason).
- No merged recipe's printed numbers change except the collapse of duplicate rows — **confirmed
  true for the fix in isolation** (02/10/15 before/after comparison above); not applicable to
  this PR's actual diff since the fix isn't in it.

title: Foundation: contract and template follow-ups from the Wave 1/2 reviews (#164)
body:
Closes #164

## What this adds

Foundation issue #164: template, docs and contract follow-ups from the Wave 1 and Wave 2
consistency reviews, mapping each of the orchestrator's twelve rulings into `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`docs/`, `recipes/_template/` and `tools/new_recipe.py`.

Base: `89bdd1a30207a23fc0349ef0795cc13243fe7fdf` (merge of #184).

### Ruling → file/section → test

1. **§4 fallback test** (writes nothing to a container AND leaves no harm standing; a fallback
   that selects "manual triage" is a review outcome; gating anyway is compliant; an exemption
   must show the gated counterfactual) → `CONTRIBUTING.md` §4; `docs/recipe-template.md` "A
   low-confidence fallback option..." bullet; `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` `python-md`;
   `recipes/_template/README.md` "Notes on the contract" → `tests/test_template.py::test_the_fallback_exemption_states_the_two_part_test`.
2. **§3 `Choice` needs ≥2 options** (a forced answer belongs to Python, already enforced in code
   by #175) → `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3; `docs/glossary.md` `Choice` entry → covered by the existing
   `jev_cookbook` construction-time `ValueError` (no new foundation test needed; prose only).
3. **§2 no attributed third-party Jev figure** → `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2 (prose addition).
4. **Coverage definition** (accepted-but-queued counts as review, not coverage) →
   `docs/glossary.md` `coverage`/`review` entries; `docs/recipe-template.md`
   "evaluate_selective"/"evaluate_outcomes" bullet. The authoritative statement belongs in
   `docs/evaluation.md`, which I did not touch — see "Left for docs/evaluation.md" below.
5. **Glossary entries for every lexicon term** (business threshold, confidence gate, review, gold
   label, coverage, risk, selective prediction, accuracy, F1, support, precision, recall) + the
   template links the glossary on first use → `docs/glossary.md` (new entries, restructured
   `threshold` into `business threshold`/`confidence gate`); `docs/recipe-template.md` "The
   lexicon"; `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` `evaluation-md` links `glossary.md#gold-label` →
   `tests/test_template.py::test_gold_label_is_defined_in_prose_not_in_a_code_comment_and_links_the_glossary`.
6. **Template: print-what-you-plot, figure titles, measured-cell N, gold-label prose, `###`
   sections, cell-id suffixes** → `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` cells `evaluation-matrix`
   (prints the confusion-matrix table), `measured` (prints N in the offline branch too),
   `evaluation-md` (gold label defined in prose with the glossary link); `docs/recipe-template.md`
   ("Print what you plot", figure-title bullet, "What was and was not measured" N bullet, the
   `###` extra-section rule, the cell-id suffix convention); `docs/notebook-style.md`
   (print-what-you-plot + title convention) →
   `tests/test_template.py::test_the_confusion_matrix_cell_prints_what_it_plots`,
   `::test_the_measured_cell_prints_n_in_every_mode_the_markdown_promises_it`,
   `::test_gold_label_is_defined_in_prose_not_in_a_code_comment_and_links_the_glossary`; the
   pre-existing `::test_the_confusion_matrix_title_follows_the_mode_and_states_n` still pins the
   `{check}`-only title unchanged.
7. **Scaffold ships `test_build_fixtures.py` and the strong-form
   `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right`** → `test_build_fixtures.py` already shipped with the
   regeneration assertion and no issue numbers before this issue (pre-#162); this PR strengthens
   `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` to the strong form (re-derives the frozen threshold,
   requires a confidently wrong `test` answer) in `recipes/_template/tests/test_helpers.py` **and**
   has `tools/new_recipe.py` emit a working, generic copy of it for every scaffolded replay
   recipe → `tests/test_new_recipe.py::test_the_scaffold_emits_a_stored_answers_guard_for_replay`,
   `::test_the_scripted_scaffold_has_no_stored_answers_guard`,
   `::test_the_scaffolded_stored_answers_guard_passes_against_a_filled_in_recipe`,
   `::test_the_scaffolded_stored_answers_guard_fails_when_no_wrong_answer_is_confident`.
8. **Next-steps neighbours must exist on `main`** (forward links forbidden; the contract's
   blessing of the 404 removed) + **recipe files never cite "the issue"** → `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6;
   `docs/recipe-template.md` "Neighbour links..." bullet; `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb`
   `next-md`; `tools/new_recipe.py`'s scaffolded `next-md` →
   `tests/test_template.py::test_the_next_steps_settle_the_neighbour_link_convention`.
9. **Sentinel confidence reconciled with recipe 14's disclosed stand-in** →
   `docs/recipe-template.md` "A sentinel is not the same thing as a disclosed stand-in" paragraph
   (prose only; bleses a disclosed, in-range, quantified stand-in and keeps the ban on an
   undisclosed or out-of-range one).
10. **`randrange` wording reconciled with `docs/backends.md`** (only `random()` is
    documented-stable) → `docs/simulation.md` "Simulator" bullet; `src/jev_cookbook/simulation.py`
    docstring (wording only — `ToyGrid`'s existing `rng.randrange` call is unchanged and stays
    pinned by `tests/test_simulation.py::test_golden_values_pin_cross_platform_streams`).
11. **`docs/fixtures.md`'s `stable_permutation` cross-linked from the template** (already fully
    documented by #184) → `docs/recipe-template.md` "Per-item order comes from a seed key..."
    bullet.
12. **CONTRIBUTING.md fix-round rule, written for a first-time reader** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
    "Branches, commits, pull requests" (new bullet banning "previously"/"used to be" etc.).

### Left for docs/evaluation.md (owned by #185 / #161 — not touched here)

- The authoritative statement that an accepted-but-queued outcome counts toward review, not
  coverage (ruling 4 / T5): I stated this in `docs/glossary.md` and `docs/recipe-template.md`
  instead, since `docs/evaluation.md` is off-limits for this PR.
- `docs/evaluation.md`'s "Noul three-path pattern" already names "business threshold" and "the
  confidence gate" exactly the way the new glossary entries do; no conflict, nothing to reconcile
  there once #185/#161 land, but worth a cross-check by whoever merges that PR.

## Decisions

- Restructured the glossary's single `threshold` entry into `business threshold` and `confidence
  gate` (per T1's instruction to split it); no other doc linked `#threshold` from outside
  `glossary.md`, so nothing else needed updating.
- `tools/new_recipe.py`'s scaffolded `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` picks the first
  question name (`next(iter(questions))`) and extracts `.confidence`/`.choice` or `.score` by
  duck typing; it documents (in a plain comment, not a `TODO`, so it does not force every builder
  to touch it) that a `Noul`-only recipe should substitute `noul_confidence` and that a recipe
  with more than one scored question should repeat the check per question.
- Updated `tests/test_new_recipe.py`'s `MINIMAL_REPLAY_ROWS` fixture (added a second validation
  row, raised `t1`'s spec from 0.8 to 0.95) so the new scaffolded guard has a genuinely
  confidently-wrong `test` answer to find; added a companion test that weakens it again to prove
  the guard actually discriminates rather than passing regardless of the fixtures.
- Did not touch `docs/development.md`'s "CI's install (Python 3.14)" comment (issue acceptance
  item 7) or the template's `scored = [...]` rewording (item 8) or the dash convention (item 6 of
  the original issue body): none of these were in the orchestrator's twelve rulings, so I left
  them alone per the brief's allowed-path discipline rather than widening scope.
- Did not widen `docs/fixtures.md`'s `replay_keys` gloss (flagged in an issue #164 comment from
  recipe 23's review): that widening is already present on `main` (landed with #184, which this
  branch is based on), and ruling 11 only asked for a cross-link from the template, which I added.

## Commands run (in `.venv`, Python 3.14, `pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`)

- `ruff check .` → All checks passed!
- `ruff format --check .` → 212 files already formatted
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` → Hygiene check passed: 306 file(s) scanned.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` → exit 0
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/_template` → fixtures valid (mode replay)
- `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb` executed twice under the heavy slot (`tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/_template`); byte-identical (`cmp` confirmed)
- Full suite once, under the heavy slot: `pytest -q` → **2177 passed, 3 skipped in 88.91s** (the 3 skips are pre-existing: no `typesafe_sdk` installed, no `pre-commit`/environment `ruff`, unrelated to this change)
- Affected tests on Python 3.10 (`.venv310`, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`): `pytest -q tests/test_template.py tests/test_new_recipe.py tests/test_simulation.py tests/test_recipe_sources.py recipes/_template` → **192 passed**

## Checklist

Foundation work — the recipe checklist does not apply.

- [x] Every acceptance criterion from the orchestrator's twelve rulings is met (mapped above)
- [x] No `.env` read, no live call, no network access
- [x] No API key referenced or required
- [x] Changes stay inside the allowed paths: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/*.md` (not `docs/evaluation.md`), `recipes/_template/**`, `tools/new_recipe.py`, `src/jev_cookbook/simulation.py` (wording only), `tests/test_template.py`, `tests/test_new_recipe.py`, `tests/test_simulation.py` (untouched), `tests/test_recipe_sources.py` (untouched)
- [x] Template notebook re-executed twice under the heavy slot; byte-identical
- [x] Commits signed; trailer present

## Unfinished / stop-and-report

Nothing — all twelve rulings are implemented and tested; see "Left for docs/evaluation.md" above
for the one item that belongs to a different in-flight PR rather than being unfinished here.

title: Foundation: evaluation helpers for multi-label pooling, outcome curves, ranking and fallback metrics (#161)
body:
Closes #161

## What this adds

`jev_cookbook.evaluation` gains the seven deliverables the issue's scope-consolidation comment (2026-10-09) lists, plus the matching docs and hygiene change. Base SHA after merging `origin/main` into this branch: `89bdd1a30207a23fc0349ef0795cc13243fe7fdf` (merge commit `499691caea0aab629fc13f6cc96ac59100567883`).

1. **Multi-label pooling + outcome tally.** `pool_label_decisions` (pools (example, label) decisions into flat `correct`/`confidence` arrays with label attribution kept) and `pool_label_outcomes` (a multi-label outcomes tally compatible with `evaluate_outcomes`) — `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:740` and `:808`. Tested in `tests/test_evaluation.py` by `test_pool_label_decisions_matches_the_hand_rolled_pooling_reference` (identity check against recipe 06's hand-rolled `pooled_correct_and_confidence`), `test_pool_label_decisions_single_threshold_for_every_label`, `test_pool_label_decisions_errors`, `test_pool_label_outcomes_matches_the_hand_rolled_tally_reference` (identity check against recipe 06's `tally_outcomes`), `test_pool_label_outcomes_matches_at_a_second_cutoff_with_some_uncertain`, `test_pool_label_outcomes_errors`.
2. **Hygiene generic username `agent`.** `tools/check_hygiene.py` `_GENERIC_USERNAMES` gains `agent` (this container's own account name) and sibling common words, without weakening the rule for real usernames. Tested in `tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py`: `test_new_names_are_in_the_generic_set_and_pass_the_minimum_length`, `test_generic_username_list_still_excludes_short_words_by_length_alone`, `test_local_usernames_filters_out_each_new_name`, `test_new_generic_account_names_are_never_checked_by_name`, `test_no_account_name_means_the_name_check_stays_off_too`, `test_a_real_username_is_still_flagged_when_agent_is_also_a_reported_name` (real username still caught), `test_a_name_merely_containing_a_new_generic_word_is_still_a_real_checkable_username`.
3. **`noul_confidence` 1-ULP docs note.** `docs/evaluation.md` (around line 104) documents that hand-written mirror-probability literals such as `0.42`/`0.58` differ from `1 - p` by 1 ULP in floating point, so `noul_confidence` can yield two adjacent threshold candidates instead of one; the code fix is out of scope here (tracked separately as #172). No test — this is a documentation-only deliverable.
4. **Ranking: `mean_recall_at_budget` and `top_k_query_accuracy`, with the divergence test.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1202` and `:1255`. `mean_recall_at_budget` is the thin mean of `recall_at_budget` over queries; `top_k_query_accuracy` is top-k ranking accuracy (is a relevant item among the top k) — the two diverge whenever a query has more than one relevant item, which is exactly the mistake recipe 17's local `top1_accuracy` made (it was `mean_recall_at_budget` under `top_k_query_accuracy`'s name). Tested by `test_mean_recall_at_budget_is_the_thin_mean`, `test_mean_recall_at_budget_skips_undefined_queries`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_credits_a_clear_winner`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_averages_over_queries`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_gives_fractional_credit_on_a_tie_at_the_top`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_diverges_from_mean_recall_at_budget_with_two_relevant_items` (the divergence test), `test_top_k_query_accuracy_agrees_with_mean_recall_at_budget_for_single_relevant_item`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_is_one_when_every_item_is_relevant`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_undefined_when_no_query_has_a_relevant_item`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_errors`.
5. **`outcome_curve(confidences, accepted, correct)`.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1528`, the `evaluate_outcomes` companion to `selective_curve`, returning the same `SelectiveCurve` row shape so recipes whose rule has a non-confidence review branch (04, 08, 11, 13, 14, 16, 21) can plot a risk-coverage curve that matches their own `evaluate_outcomes` numbers. Tested by `test_outcome_curve_equals_selective_curve_when_accepted_is_all_true`, `test_outcome_curve_uses_accepted_and_confidence_together`, `test_outcome_curve_is_nan_where_the_accepted_mask_selects_nothing`, `test_outcome_curve_rejects_out_of_range_confidence`, `test_outcome_curve_errors`.
6. **`set_agreement(gold_sets, choices)` and `fallback_metrics(gold_sets, choices, fallback)`.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:875` and `:899`. `set_agreement` is the share of choices inside an acceptable gold set (recipes 12 and 13's hand-rolled `choice in gold`); `fallback_metrics` is precision/recall/F1 of the fallback option via the two-class relabelling fallback recipes repeat. Tested by `test_set_agreement`, `test_fallback_metrics`, `test_fallback_metrics_accepts_choice_answers`, `test_fallback_metrics_degenerate_cases`.
7. **Docs: "Outcomes versus the confidence-only view".** `docs/evaluation.md` section "Outcomes versus the confidence-only view" (around line 297) states when `evaluate_selective`/`selective_curve` and `evaluate_outcomes`/`outcome_curve` coincide (a confidence-only review branch) and when they diverge (any additional non-confidence branch), and how to report the counterfactual for an exempted permissive option — recipe 16's lesson. This is a documentation-only deliverable; the behavior it describes is already covered by the pre-existing `test_evaluate_outcomes_matches_evaluate_selective_for_a_confidence_only_rule` and `test_evaluate_outcomes_diverges_from_evaluate_selective_with_a_second_review_branch` (not introduced by this PR).

Also from the issue body (items 2 and 4, folded into deliverables above): the "Noul three-path pattern" section states that a confidence-only review branch makes `evaluate_selective` and an outcome tally agree, and the "distance from 0.5, not margin at the threshold" warning (`docs/evaluation.md` line ~372) carries the per-label-threshold caveat for multi-label recipes.

**Explicitly out of scope** (per the scope-consolidation comment): the stable seeded-permutation helper was split out to #181 and has already landed on `main` via #184 (now in this branch through the merge, untouched by this PR); recipe-side migrations to use these helpers go to #163; the `noul_confidence` code fix (as opposed to the docs note) is #172.

## Decisions

- Function names and signatures follow the scope-consolidation comment verbatim (`outcome_curve(confidences, accepted, correct)`, `set_agreement(gold_sets, choices)`, `fallback_metrics(gold_sets, choices, fallback)`) rather than any alternative phrasing floated in earlier review comments on the issue.
- `pool_label_decisions` keeps per-label attribution by returning `(example_id, label)` keys alongside the pooled arrays, per acceptance criterion 1, rather than only the flat arrays.
- `outcome_curve` returns the same `SelectiveCurve` shape as `selective_curve` so existing plotting code that consumes one can consume the other unchanged.
- The wave-2 consistency-review follow-ups noted on the issue (S2 outcome-sweep caveats, S3 settling one `(accepted, correct)` parameter-order convention, S4 merging `false_merge_rate`/`false_link_rate`) are not addressed here — they were not part of the scope-consolidation comment's seven-item list and are left for a later pass.
- Local notebook execution was **not** run by this builder: two previous agents working this repository hung inside long-running shells executing `tools/execute_notebook.py` against scratch copies of other recipes. This PR touches no notebooks (`docs/evaluation.md`, `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tools/check_hygiene.py`, and their tests only), so notebook execution is delegated entirely to CI's per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` jobs, which run every notebook on the PR head and diff it against the committed file.

## How it was verified

All commands run from this branch after merging `origin/main` (base `89bdd1a`), in a clean `uv`-managed venv, from the worktree root:

- `ruff check .` — all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .` — 213 files already formatted.
