title: Recipe 08: FAQ selection
body:
Closes #8

## What this adds

Recipe 08, "FAQ selection": a `Choice` over a fixed catalog of six FAQ identifiers
(`password_reset`, `change_email`, `cancel_subscription`, `billing_cycle`, `export_data`,
`delete_account`) plus the explicit fallback `no_match`, which the issue names for a question
none of the six addresses. Python builds the option set and holds the stored answer text for
each FAQ; the model only ever picks an identifier. `helpers.select_faq` returns the stored
answer for a confident real match, reports `no_match` as a final result whatever its confidence
(there is no stored answer a confidence check could protect there), and sends anything else
uncertain to an explicit `review` outcome. The threshold is chosen on `validation` (over the
real-FAQ matches only, excluding `no_match` answers from the selection pool, since `select_faq`
never gates them) and frozen before `test` is touched.

Because the rule has a review branch beyond the confidence gate (the `no_match` fallback),
`helpers.summarize_outcomes` computes selective coverage, accuracy and risk directly from
`select_faq`'s own outcomes (`matched` and `no_match` both count as answered; `review` does not),
rather than reapplying `jev_cookbook.evaluation.evaluate_selective`'s single threshold to every
example, which would gate a branch the rule itself never gates.

### Exact question definition

One `Choice` question, `faq`: "Which one of these FAQs, if any, best answers the customer's
question?" over the seven options above, each with a description that says what belongs to it
and, for the three confusable pairs (`password_reset`/`change_email`,
`cancel_subscription`/`billing_cycle`, `cancel_subscription`/`delete_account`), what belongs to
the other option instead. The state Jev sees is `{"question": <text>}`; the `question_id`
bookkeeping field stays in Python. Confidence is the published Choice formula with `n = 7`:
`(p_max - 1/7) / (1 - 1/7)`.

### Fixtures

40 examples: 19 `validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo` (none scored). Hard cases: 5 "no FAQ addresses
it" questions per scored split, plus 6 "two FAQs nearly address it" questions (one per
confusable pair per split, roughly). Three `test` answers are wrong on purpose, in three
different ways: one wrong and confident through the gate (`t07-ambiguous`,
`cancel_subscription` read as `billing_cycle` at confidence 0.5333, above the 0.3000 threshold);
one wrong and confident through the un-gated `no_match` branch (`t12-no-match-wrong`,
`export_data` read as `no_match`); one wrong but caught by the gate
(`t19-no-match-wrong`, confidence 0.2183, sent to review). `validation` has zero errors by
design, so the threshold selection is clean; this is noted as a decision below.

### Threshold and evaluation numbers

- Threshold (chosen on 14 real-FAQ `validation` matches, `target_accuracy=1.0`): **0.3000**
- `validation`: top-1 accuracy 1.0000 (selection step); outcome summary: answered 19/19,
  coverage 1.0000, accuracy 1.0000, risk 0.0000 (selection step)
- `test`: top-1 accuracy **0.8421** (16/19); `no_match` precision **0.8000**, recall **0.8000**
  (4/5 each way); outcome summary (rule's own outcomes): answered 17/19, coverage **0.8947**,
  accuracy **0.8824**, risk **0.1176** (non-zero, as required)
- Request count in live mode: 40 (one per fixture example, each decided once and reused);
  README tells the reader to raise `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS` to at least 40.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/08-faq-selection/`, plus the generated README regions
      regenerated by the integration worker (nothing else outside the recipe folder) --
      this pull request has no README change yet; that lands when the integration worker takes
      the branch, per the generated-README exception.
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` -- **not yet; by design.** This is
      the integration worker's step, not the recipe builder's. `Catalog (README is current)` is
      expected red on this pull request until then.
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/08-faq-selection/` paths, all
      `100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion out of scope (verified with
      `tools/check_recipe_scope.py`, see below).
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network.
- [x] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions.
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which
      mode it ran in (`run_header`).
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference -- this
      recipe has no recorded fixtures; every number is labelled a pipeline check or a selection
      step.
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (no-FAQ-addresses-it,
      two-FAQs-nearly-address-it), and carry gold labels for every scored example.
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (the "stored FAQ answer" is text
      Python returns, nothing is sent or changed anywhere).
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels, with `jev_cookbook.evaluation` (`accuracy`,
      `confusion_matrix`, `per_class_metrics`, `select_confidence_threshold`) plus this recipe's
      own `summarize_outcomes` for the rule's selective numbers. The issue names no baseline.
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below).

## Acceptance criteria (from issue #8)

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, no key, no network; outputs committed.
- [x] Live mode is opt-in and uses the same question definitions.
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the named hard cases, carry gold labels, pass
      `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/08-faq-selection` (`fixtures valid (mode
      replay)`).
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook's `run_header`
      states the mode.
- [x] Evaluation reports top-1 accuracy, and `no_match`'s own precision and recall.
- [x] A reader with basic Python can follow it end to end; every new term (confidence, the
      `matched`/`review`/`no_match` outcomes, coverage/accuracy/risk) is explained on first use.
- [x] At least three individual typed answers are displayed and discussed before any aggregate
      metric (two `demo` rows and one `validation` row -- never `test`, per the no-peeking rule).
- [x] No statement about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference; every
      synthetic-run metric is labelled a pipeline check.
- [x] `README.md` says what the recipe teaches, how to run it, and what was/was not measured
      live.
- [x] This pull request changes only `recipes/08-faq-selection/`; CI is green except `Catalog`
      (expected, see above).

## Decisions

- **Fixed FAQ catalog, not per-question retrieval.** "Short candidate list" is read as the whole
  FAQ catalog being small (six entries), presented identically for every question -- the same
  shape as recipe 04's fixed category set plus fallback -- rather than a per-question retrieval
  step narrowing a larger catalog. The issue does not ask for retrieval, and nothing in the
  shared package offers one; implementing retrieval would be new logic outside what any source
  page or the issue describes.
- **`no_match` bypasses the confidence gate entirely**, the same shape as recipe 04's
  `unclear_request`: the option already asserts "no FAQ fits", so there is no stored FAQ answer
  a confidence check could protect. This means a *wrong* `no_match` answer is never caught by
  anything (see `t12-no-match-wrong`), which the notebook calls out explicitly as a different
  failure mode from a wrong answer that clears the gate (`t07-ambiguous`).
- **Selective coverage/accuracy/risk are computed from `select_faq`'s own outcomes**
  (`helpers.summarize_outcomes`), not from `jev_cookbook.evaluation.evaluate_selective`: that
  helper reapplies one threshold to every example, which would score a confidence gate against
  `no_match` answers that the rule never gates. This is a new, recipe-local type
  (`OutcomeSummary`), not a shared-package addition -- it is specific to a rule with more than
  one outcome branch, and the shared evaluation toolkit has no helper of this shape today (see
  "Shared-package gap" below).
- **The threshold-selection pool excludes `no_match`-chosen validation answers.** Feeding their
  confidence into `select_confidence_threshold` would tune a gate that answer never passes
  through.
- **`validation` has zero errors by design**, so its outcome-summary risk is a clean 0.0000; the
  non-zero-risk requirement is satisfied on `test` (two different failure modes, see above). The
  brief's guidance allows this ("ideally validation too" is a nice-to-have, not a requirement).
- Added a `_DESCRIPTIONS`/`ANSWERS` pattern for the six FAQs plus `no_match`, mirroring recipe
  04's `_DESCRIPTIONS`/`QUEUES` pattern.

## Shared-package gap worth noting (not blocking; worked around in this recipe's own `helpers.py`)

`jev_cookbook.evaluation` has no helper for selective coverage/accuracy/risk when a rule has a
review branch other than a single confidence gate (a fallback option that is never gated, as
here, or any other second branch). This recipe adds its own `OutcomeSummary` /
`summarize_outcomes` in `helpers.py` rather than reaching for `evaluate_selective`, per the
brief's instruction not to misuse a shared helper outside what it actually computes. If a later
recipe needs the same shape, a shared "selective metrics from arbitrary answered/correct pairs"
helper (taking a plain `answered: bool` list instead of assuming a single threshold) would avoid
every recipe re-deriving this by hand; I did not open a foundation issue for it myself, since
the brief says the orchestrator does that.

## How it was verified

All commands run from the repository root in a `uv` Python 3.14 venv
(`uv pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`), heavy jobs run one at a
time under the shared `HEAVY.lock`:

```

ruff format --check .                                           -> 96 files already formatted
python tools/check_hygiene.py                                   -> Hygiene check passed: 124 file(s) scanned.
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/08-faq-selection -> fixtures valid (mode replay)
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/08-faq-selection        -> executed notebook.ipynb offline
  (run twice after the final formatting pass; `diff -q` the two committed files: byte-identical)
pytest recipes/08-faq-selection                                  -> 27 passed
pytest (full suite, nice -n 10, under HEAVY.lock)                -> 1505 passed, 3 skipped in 87.84s
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD \
    --branch recipe/08-faq-selection --body-file <body>          -> scope ok: recipe pull request
                                                                      for #8 (08-faq-selection): 9
                                                                      changed paths
```

`python tools/render_catalog.py` / `--check` was deliberately **not** run, per the
generated-README exception and this recipe's brief.

integration worker's step, not mine, and is expected to show as a red `Catalog (README is
current)` check until that happens.

title: Readiness helper: harden the duplicate-collapse rule after #144 (#150)
body:
Closes #150

## What this adds

Hardens the duplicate-collapse rule that #144 added to `tools/check_merge_readiness.py` (#138),
answering the five non-blocking findings from the Opus re-review of #144
(comment 6071769630). No behaviour change beyond these five items; exit codes unchanged.

1. **Unreadable app slug no longer "collapses".** `_app_slug` already returns `None` for an
   absent `app`, a non-dict `app`, or a non-string `slug`. Previously `len({None}) == 1` let two
   such CheckRuns satisfy `one_source` and collapse to a false `READY`. The guard is now
   `len(apps) == 1 and None not in apps`. The app slug also now renders as JSON `null`, never the
   string `"None"`, via a small `_app_evidence` helper used in both the single-result evidence
   path and the merged-`runs` evidence path (`_run_evidence`).
2. **`MAX_MERGED_RUNS` / `runs_omitted` now has a test.** 11 same-app `success` CheckRuns collapse
   to `results: 11`, `runs` capped at 10, `runs_omitted: 1`.
3. **Ambiguous evidence now carries `states`.** The sorted list of distinct results across the
   duplicate rows (e.g. `["pending", "success"]` vs `["failure", "success"]`), so the receipt can
   tell a transient `success`+`pending` wait apart from a genuine conflict, even though both print
   the identical `conflicting results (N)` failure string. The serial-merge wait-list bullet in
   `docs/merge-readiness.md` is rewritten to say so plainly (the prior wording implied a
   distinction the receipt could not make, which the original review flagged as suggestion 1).
4. **The same-app test is order-independent.** `apps = {e.get("app") for e in entries}` reads
   every entry with `.get`, never by indexing, so it cannot `KeyError` on a StatusContext
   (which carries no `app` key) regardless of where it falls in the entries list. A direct
   `judge_checks` test places a StatusContext first.
5. **Residual #138 option-2 gaps are now recorded in `docs/merge-readiness.md` as a known
   limit**, not fixed: `scope.yml`'s `cancel-in-progress` concurrency group leaves a `cancelled`
   `Scope` row when a description edit overlaps an in-progress run, and a once-failed `Scope` row
   is likewise never cleared by a further edit of the same head (either case needs a new head --
   a `synchronize` event -- not another edit). The interim "no description edits after the final
   push" rule stays in force.

## Decisions

- **Rendering choice for an unreadable app slug: JSON `null`, not an omitted key.** The
  single-result evidence already always sets `"app"` for a `check_run` entry; keeping the key
  present (as `null`) rather than conditionally omitting it keeps the evidence shape uniform for
  a reader diffing receipts, and `null` is the one value Python's `None` serialises to that is
  unambiguously not a slug.
- **`states` is added to every ambiguous evidence row (both the `"duplicate"` and
  `"conflicting"` cases), not only the conflicting one.** It was already computed
  (`states = sorted({e["state"] for e in entries})`) for the `kind` decision, so surfacing it
  everywhere ambiguous evidence appears is free and keeps the evidence shape uniform; the
  `"duplicate"` case's `states` list is simply a single element (e.g. `["cancelled"]`).
  `_run_evidence`'s per-row `"state"` and the single-result path's `"state"` were already
  unclipped in the existing code, so `states` is left unclipped too, for consistency; test
  data is drawn only from `FakeGitHub`, which the test module fully controls.
- **Doc placement for item 5.** Recorded as a new paragraph in `docs/merge-readiness.md`'s
  "Required checks" section, immediately after the existing transient-wait paragraph it
  qualifies, rather than a new top-level section, since it is a direct limit of the #138
  collapse rule rather than a separate concern.
- **No change to `one_source`'s reliance on `found`/`by_name` ordering.** `collect_checks`
  always appends every CheckRun before any StatusContext for a given commit, so in practice a
  StatusContext never actually precedes a CheckRun in `entries` through the normal collection
  path; item 4's fix and its test (`test_judge_checks_status_context_first_does_not_raise_and_stays_ambiguous`)
  call `judge_checks` directly with hand-built `found` data to exercise that ordering regardless,
  since relying on `collect_checks`'s current append order to make `e["app"]` safe was exactly
  the fragility the original review flagged.

title: Recipe 09: File organization
body:
Closes #9

## What this adds

Recipe 09, "File organization": a `Choice` recipe that recommends a destination folder from a
fixed catalog, using a file's name and a short text excerpt. Jev picks exactly one of five
options Python builds: the four real destination folders (`invoices`, `contracts`, `reports`,
`correspondence`) or `unsorted`, the fallback for a file that matches none of them. Python owns
every side effect: no file is moved, created, or read outside the fixtures; the notebook renders
a dry-run preview only. `helpers.propose_destination` places the chosen folder only when Jev did
not itself answer `unsorted` and the answer's `confidence` clears a threshold chosen on
`validation` (0.5000) and frozen for `test`.

Fixtures: 40 examples (19 `validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo`), including the hard cases: a file
with no real match (`-no-match`), a file whose name and content point to two folders at once
(`-ambiguous`), a file whose name is misleading about its content (`-lookalike`), and a file too
short to carry signal (`-short`). One wrong answer at low confidence on `validation`
(`v18-invoice-wrong`) and one wrong *and confident* answer on `test`
(`t17-hybrid-wrong-confident`, confidence 0.75, above the frozen threshold), so the selective
risk on `test` is non-zero (0.0909), not a guarantee that happens to hold.

### A small composition on top of `jev_cookbook.evaluation` (see Decisions)

`select_confidence_threshold`/`evaluate_selective` select on one confidence number, which fits a
rule with a single cutoff but not this recipe's two-part rule (an explicit `unsorted` option,
plus a confidence gate on the four real folders). `helpers.placement_confidence` composes
correctly with the stock toolkit: it returns `answer.confidence` for a real folder and `-1.0`
(below every real confidence) for `unsorted`, the same way a Noul recipe defines
`noul_confidence` when the one field its answer type has is not the signal it wants. This is not
a reimplementation of the rule: `propose_destination` is still called on every example to produce
the reported placed/unsorted counts; `placement_confidence` only feeds the generic
selective-prediction helpers a signal consistent with what that rule actually does.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/09-file-organization/` (no `README.md` change in this PR; the integration worker regenerates it in this same PR after the branch is handed over)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` — **not done by this PR on purpose**; `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red until the integration worker runs
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/09-file-organization/` paths, all mode `100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion out of scope (verified locally with `tools/check_recipe_scope.py`, see below)
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same question definitions
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which mode it ran in (`run_header`)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference (none recorded here; the README says "not measured live")
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (no-match, ambiguous, lookalike, short), and carry gold labels
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (dry-run preview table only, never a real move/create/read)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels with `jev_cookbook.evaluation` (accuracy, confusion matrix, per-option precision/recall, selective coverage/accuracy/risk); the issue names no baseline
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## How it was verified

Run in a `uv` venv (`.venv`, Python 3.14.7) with
`uv pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`, and a second venv (`.venv310`,
Python 3.10.21) with `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` for the floor check, under the shared
`HEAVY.lock` slot for the venv installs, the notebook executions and the full suite.

```text
python recipes/09-file-organization/build_fixtures.py        # wrote 40 examples, 38 labels, 40 responses
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/09-file-organization   # fixtures valid (mode replay)
pytest recipes/09-file-organization                           # 17 passed (3.14 and 3.10)
python build_fixtures.py --force                              # byte-identical inputs/labels/responses on 3.10 vs 3.14
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/09-file-organization  # executed twice, byte-identical
ruff check .                                                    # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                                           # all formatted
python tools/check_hygiene.py                                   # Hygiene check passed: 115 file(s) scanned.
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --branch recipe/09-file-organization --body-file pr-body.txt
                                                                  # scope ok: recipe pull request for #9 (09-file-organization): 9 changed paths
pytest -q                                                        # full suite: 1468 passed, 3 skipped (pre-existing, unrelated skips)
python tools/render_catalog.py --check                          # README.md is out of date (EXPECTED red; not run here on purpose)
grep -rn TODO recipes/09-file-organization                      # (empty)
```

Exact numbers reported by the notebook (offline, synthetic, mode-labelled throughout):

- Question: one `Choice`, `destination`, over 5 options (`invoices`, `contracts`, `reports`,
  `correspondence`, `unsorted`), options and descriptions built by Python in `helpers.py`.
- Fixtures: 19 `validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo` (40 total; N = 38 scored).
- Threshold chosen on `validation` (`select_confidence_threshold`, `target_accuracy=1.0`): 0.5000.
  Validation (selection step): 10 of 19 placed, 10 of 10 right among placed.
- Test (pipeline check): raw choice accuracy 0.9474 (18/19); placed 11 of 19 (coverage 0.5789);
  right among placed 10 of 11; **risk among placed 0.0909** (non-zero, from the one wrong-and-
  confident answer, `t17-hybrid-wrong-confident`).
- Per-option precision/recall on `test`: `invoices` 0.800/1.000, `contracts` 1.000/0.800,
  `reports` 1.000/1.000, `correspondence` 1.000/1.000, `unsorted` 1.000/1.000.
- Live request count if run live: 40 (one per fixture example, each decided once); README tells
  the reader to set `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS=40` (default budget is 25).

## Decisions

- **`unsorted` is Jev's own fallback option, not only a Python-side confidence gate.** The issue's
  build notes name two things: a fixed option set with the use case's fallback, and a
  low-confidence proposal staying "unsorted" in the preview. `helpers.propose_destination`
  implements both: Jev naming `unsorted` always goes to the unsorted row (whatever its own
  confidence), and a real-folder answer below the frozen threshold also goes there.
- **`placement_confidence` (see "A small composition" above) is a new, small helper in this
  recipe's `helpers.py`**, not a change to `jev_cookbook.evaluation`. I considered and rejected
  reporting `answer.confidence` unchanged into `select_confidence_threshold`/`evaluate_selective`:
  it would let a confident `unsorted` answer count as "answered" in the selective-prediction
  curve, which does not match what the rule actually does with it. I did not change shared code;
  if a later recipe needs the same pattern, `jev_cookbook.evaluation` could grow a documented
  convention for it the way `noul_confidence` already exists for Noul — I'm flagging this as a
  possible foundation follow-up, not blocking this recipe on it.
- **Two folders are easy to confuse by surface wording** (an invoice that mentions an existing
  agreement, or a renewal agreement that states a price): `invoices`' and `contracts`' criteria
  descriptions each say what the other folder covers instead, and the fixtures include one hard
  case in each direction (`v18-invoice-wrong` on validation, `t17-hybrid-wrong-confident` on test).
- Neighbouring recipes linked in "Next steps" are `04-support-ticket-routing` and
  `05-document-classification`, both `Choice` recipes over a fixed option set, matching the
  catalog's decision type for each.

## Unfinished / not done here

- The root `README.md` is not touched by this PR; the integration worker regenerates it here
  after the branch is handed over, per CONTRIBUTING.md's generated-README exception.
- No live run was made; "not measured live" throughout, as the contract requires for a synthetic
  recipe.

title: Catalog: list S02 (primitives) among the sources of every recipe
body:
Closes #147

## What this adds

Adds `"S02"` (the primitives page) to the `sources` list of every recipe row in `catalog/recipes.json` that didn't already list it: 30 of the 60 rows, exactly the ranks named in the Opus review of #145 (comment 6071506008) — ranks 8, 10, 11, 15–17, 19–21, 26–32, 36, 41–46, 49, 51, 52, 56, 58–60. Every recipe asks a typed `Choice`/`Noul`/`Score` question defined on S02, and `tools/new_recipe.py` scaffolds the README source bullets from this catalog, so these 30 rows would have shipped without the page that defines their own primitive. Same shape as #142/#145 (S03).

Each row's `sources` list keeps its existing entries and gets `"S02"` inserted in sorted-by-id position — e.g. `["S03", "S04", "S06"]` -> `["S02", "S03", "S04", "S06"]`. Rows 45 and 46 already had `S01` first, so `S02` lands second there (`["S01", "S02", "S03", "S04"]`), matching the convention row 1 already follows. The 30 rows that already listed `S02` are untouched.

`python tools/render_catalog.py` was run and produced **no change to `README.md`**: as established in #145, the renderer's `recipes` region doesn't print per-recipe sources at all (only `decision_cell`/`status_cell`); the only region that touches `catalog["sources"]` is the top-level S01–S08 reference table, which this change never modifies. `README.md` is unchanged by this PR.

Lock acquired via `mkdir`/`owner` after waiting for another agent's run on the same slot to finish, released via trap immediately after; no process of mine left running afterward (checked with `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep -E 'pytest|execute_notebook'`).

title: Recipe 07: word sense selection
body:
Closes #7

## What this adds

`recipes/07-word-sense-selection/`: a `Choice` recipe that selects the intended sense of an
ambiguous English word from a fixed, two-sense inventory Python builds for the word in question,
using the sentence it appears in. Four target words (`bank`, `crane`, `spring`, `bat`), each with
two senses; every word's option list carries a third, shared `unclear` fallback for a sentence
whose context does not decide between the two senses. `helpers.resolve` accepts the chosen sense
only when it names a real sense of that word *and* its `confidence` clears a threshold chosen on
`validation` and frozen on `test`; choosing `unclear` always goes to an explicit `review` outcome,
whatever its confidence.

### Exact question definition

One question, `sense` (`Choice`), asked once per sentence:

- **instructions:** `In the sentence below, which sense of the word '<word>' is intended?`
- **criteria (options), built by Python per word** (`helpers.senses_for(word)`):
  - the word's own two senses, each with a one-sentence description (for example `bank`:
    `financial_institution` — "A business that holds money for people, offers loans and manages
    accounts."; `river_edge` — "The sloped land along the side of a river, lake or other body of
    water.")
  - `unclear` (always last): "The sentence does not give enough context to tell which sense of
    '<word>' is intended here."
- **state** (`helpers.build_state`): `{"word": ..., "sentence": ...}` — exactly the two fields Jev
  needs. A third field, `sentence_id`, travels in `fields` alongside them but is stripped out by
  `build_state` and never reaches the model; Python re-attaches it to the outcome afterwards, so
  every result still traces back to its sentence without the identifier ever being sent.

Because the option list depends on the target word, each word gets its own `Choice` question
(cached by word in the notebook's setup cell), and the replay key differs by word accordingly.

## Fixture counts

40 examples total: **19 `validation`**, **19 `test`**, **2 `demo`** (38 gold labels; `demo`
examples are shown but never scored), split evenly across the four words (`bank` 5/5, `crane`
5/5, `spring` 5/5, `bat` 4/4, plus one `bank` and one `crane` demo). Per word, one `validation`
example is wrong at a moderate confidence (the stored answer leans toward the word's other sense);
on `test`, one example per word is correct but low-confidence except `crane`, which instead gets
one answered `unclear` at low confidence and one (`t05-crane-wrong`) wrong *and* confident.

## Threshold and evaluation numbers

- Threshold chosen on `validation` (`select_confidence_threshold`, over the answers naming a real
  sense, target accuracy 1.0): **0.6250**.
- Validation (selection step, not a result): accuracy of the raw choice **0.7895**; accepted by
  the rule **15 of 19**; right among accepted **15 of 15**.
- Test (reported once, threshold frozen): accuracy of the raw choice **0.8947**; accepted by the
  rule **15 of 19**; right among accepted **14 of 15**; sent to review **4 of 19** (3 "confidence
  below the threshold", 1 "chose unclear").
- Accuracy per target word, test: `bank` 1.0000 (n=5), `bat` 1.0000 (n=4), `crane` 0.6000 (n=5),
  `spring` 1.0000 (n=5).
- Selective prediction (`evaluate_selective`, test, threshold 0.6250): **coverage 0.7895**,
  **accuracy 0.9333**, **risk 0.0667** (non-zero: `t05-crane-wrong` is wrong at confidence 0.70,
  above the frozen threshold, so it is accepted and counted).

## Request count

40 (one per fixture example; every example is decided once and the stored/live answer is reused
wherever it is shown again, so this is also the live-mode request count). That is above the live
backend's default budget of 25, so the README tells the reader to set
`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS=40` or higher before running live.

## Decisions

- **The fixed fallback outcome the use case calls for ("show a sentence where context is too thin
  and how the probabilities reflect it") is modelled as a third Choice option, `unclear`, added to
  every word's two senses** (CONTRIBUTING.md section 3: include an `uncertain`/`no_match` outcome
  when the use case calls for it). `unclear` is never a gold label and is never accepted by
  `resolve`, whatever its confidence — mirroring how the template's `none` option is handled, but
  as an explicit third option rather than an existing sense being repurposed.
- **`build_questions` takes `word` as a parameter**, unlike every other recipe's parameterless
  `build_questions()`, because the option set genuinely differs by target word. Each word's
  question (and so its replay key) is built and cached separately; `tests/test_helpers.py` and
  `build_fixtures.py` both compute the key from the row's own word.
- **S03 (confidence) is in the Sources list.** `catalog/recipes.json` did not list S03 for rank 7
  when this recipe was started; #145 merged into `main` while this PR was in progress and added it
  for every recipe, including rank 7. This PR was rebased onto that merge and updated to cite S03
  normally (notebook intro and README sources list); no stale "not yet listed" caveat remains.
- Two of the three up-close answers before any aggregate are `demo` examples (a thin-context
  `bank` sentence and a clear `crane` sentence); the third is a scored `test` example
  (`t05-crane-wrong`) shown specifically because it is wrong and confident, so the reader sees that
  shape before the aggregate numbers explain it.

## Commands run and results

All run from the repository root.

```
uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt
uv venv --python 3.10 .venv310 && source .venv310/bin/activate && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

python recipes/07-word-sense-selection/build_fixtures.py           # wrote 40 examples, 38 labels, 40 responses
# re-ran under Python 3.10 and 3.14; fixtures/ byte-identical both times

python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/07-word-sense-selection
# recipes/07-word-sense-selection: fixtures valid (mode replay)

pytest recipes/07-word-sense-selection          # 20 passed
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/07-word-sense-selection   # offline, under the shared heavy-job slot
# run twice; git diff --stat empty after the second run (byte-identical)

ruff check .                 # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .        # files already formatted
python tools/check_hygiene.py                              # Hygiene check passed: 114 file(s) scanned.
python tools/check_recipe_scope.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --branch recipe/07-word-sense-selection --body-file <this file>
# scope ok: recipe pull request for #7 (07-word-sense-selection): 8 changed paths

python -m pytest -q          # full suite, under the shared heavy-job slot: 1451 passed, 3 skipped

python tools/render_catalog.py --check
# README.md is out of date. Run: python tools/render_catalog.py   <-- expected; not run or fixed here
```

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/07-word-sense-selection/`, plus the generated README
  regions regenerated by the integration worker (nothing else outside the recipe folder)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` after updating against current
  `main`, before final review; `--check` passes — **not yet done; this is the integration worker's
  step**, and `Catalog (README is current)` is expected red on this PR's head until then
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/07-word-sense-selection/` paths
  (no `README.md` change yet, since the integration step has not run); no symlink, mode or type
  change, rename or deletion out of scope; verified locally with `tools/check_recipe_scope.py`
  above
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) and uses the same question
  definitions (`helpers.build_questions(word)`, same for offline and live)
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which mode
  it ran in (the run header, and the "What was and was not measured" cell)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference — every
  number is labelled a pipeline check or a selection step
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases (a sentence too thin to decide a sense, a
  moderate-confidence wrong answer per word, a low-confidence miss, and one wrong-and-confident

title: Evaluation: noul_confidence must be |2p - 1| per the confidence page (#140)
body:
Closes #140

## What this adds

`noul_confidence(noul)` in `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py` now returns `|2p - 1|` for each
Noul answer (range 0-1), per the TypeSafe confidence page
(https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence, S03). The page states that a Noul's confidence is the
Choice confidence formula, `(p_max - 1/n) / (1 - 1/n)`, applied to a yes-or-no Choice
(`n = 2`, `p_max = max(p, 1 - p)`), which reduces to `|2p - 1|` — the toolkit previously
computed `max(p, 1 - p)` instead (range 0.5-1), disagreeing with the source and putting Noul
confidence on a different scale than Choice confidence. No call site needed the old
convention (grepped `recipes/`, `tools/`, `src/`, `docs/`, `tests/`: only the function
definition, its docstrings, and the tests referenced it), so it was replaced in place rather
than kept under another name.

- `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`: new formula and docstring (states the formula, the
  source URL, and the shared scale with Choice).
- `tests/test_evaluation.py`, `tests/test_evaluation_answers.py`: pin the formula at
  `p ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}`, and a new test proves the identity with
  `jev_cookbook.answers.choice_confidence([p, 1 - p])` at `n = 2` for the same five values.
  Existing call sites that asserted the old `max(p, 1 - p)` values are updated to the new
  `|2p - 1|` values.
- `docs/evaluation.md`: the Noul helper table and a new paragraph state the formula, the
  source link, and the shared scale with Choice; a new "Noul three-path pattern" subsection
  shows how to compose a business threshold on `p` with a confidence gate `|2p - 1| < c` into
  a yes / no / review outcome, using `select_threshold`/`evaluate_threshold` and
  `select_confidence_threshold`/`evaluate_selective` — no new helper, since none exists that
  selects both cut-offs together.
- `docs/glossary.md`: the `confidence` entry gets a Noul bullet alongside the existing Choice
  and Score ones, with the formula, the reduction from the Choice formula, and the source link.

No merged notebook calls `noul_confidence` — `recipes/01-sentiment-classification` and
`recipes/_template` do not use it — so no notebook needed re-execution.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable (foundation work; no recipe folder touched).

## How it was verified

Commands run in the worktree (`uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev,ml]"
-c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`; `uv venv --python 3.10 .venv310 && uv pip install -e
".[dev]"`), each under the shared heavy-job slot where required:

- `ruff check .` — all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .` — 78 files already formatted (confirms the new Python code block in
  `docs/evaluation.md` is ruff-formatted).
- `pytest` under Python 3.14 — 1431 passed, 3 skipped, in 150s.
- `pytest` under Python 3.10 — 1431 passed, 3 skipped, in 112s.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` — passed (no README change needed; this PR touches
  no recipe).
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — passed, 106 files scanned.
- **Mutation proof**: reverted `noul_confidence` to `max(v, 1.0 - v)` by hand, reran the three
  tests that pin the new behaviour — all three failed (`test_noul_confidence`,
  `test_noul_confidence_is_the_choice_formula_at_n_equals_2`,
  `test_noul_thresholds_on_noul_answers`), confirming they catch the old formula. Reverted the
  mutation back; the same three tests pass again (`git diff` on `evaluation.py` was clean
  before and after, confirming the round trip left no stray change).

## Decisions

- The old `max(p, 1 - p)` convention is **removed**, not kept under a separate name
  (e.g. `noul_majority`): nothing in `src/`, `recipes/`, `tools/` or `docs/` called it other
  than `noul_confidence` itself and its tests, so there is no call site to preserve it for.
  A future recipe that specifically wants "certainty of the majority side" rather than the
  confidence scale should ask for that helper explicitly rather than reusing this name.
- The identity test imports `jev_cookbook.answers.choice_confidence` directly (rather than
  re-deriving the Choice formula inline in the test) so the test is tied to the actual shared
  Choice implementation, not a second hand-written copy of the formula that could drift from
  it.
- The "Noul three-path pattern" section composes existing functions rather than adding a new
  helper, per the issue's "no new helper unless trivial and tested" guidance; the six-line
  example in `docs/evaluation.md` shows the `correct` array (thresholded business decision vs.
  gold) feeding `select_confidence_threshold`/`evaluate_selective` as the confidence gate.

## Unfinished

Nothing. All allowed-path changes are included; no notebook needed re-execution; both Python
3.10 and 3.14 test runs are green.

title: Catalog: list S03 (confidence) among the sources of every recipe

title: Merge-readiness helper: collapse all-success duplicate Scope rows on one head (#138)
body:
Closes #138

## What this adds

Decides and implements option 1 from #138 (helper-side), as directed by the orchestrator: when
several completed CheckRuns share a required name on the same head commit — whether required via
`--require-check` or `--require-head-check`, never one of the five `BASELINE_CHECKS` — the helper
now treats them as one `success` result if and only if every one of them concluded `success`. Any
other mix (any failure, neutral, cancelled, timed out, skipped, pending/in-progress, or differing
conclusions) still fails closed exactly as before, with the existing duplicate/conflicting
message. Exit codes are unchanged.

This fixes the gap found on PR #133: `scope.yml` runs `Scope (recipe pull requests)` on
`pull_request_target` for `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` and `edited`, so any description
edit after the last push leaves two successful `Scope` CheckRuns on the same head. Before this
change the helper failed closed on that duplicate forever, making the gate unreachable after an
edit.

### Code change

`tools/check_merge_readiness.py`, `judge_checks()`: when a required name has more than one
completed result, and that name is not a baseline check, and every result's state is `success`,
the evidence entry becomes `{"name", "state": "success", "results": N, "runs": [{"kind", "id",
"state", ["app"]}, ...]}` — one row per merged CheckRun/StatusContext, so the receipt still shows
exactly which runs were merged. Any other multi-result mix, and every multi-result baseline case,
keeps the original `duplicate`/`conflicting` failure message and `"state": "ambiguous"` evidence,
unchanged.

### Decisions

- The collapse applies only to a `--require-check` or `--require-head-check` name, never to one
  of the five `BASELINE_CHECKS`. The issue's scenario is pull-request-only checks re-running on an
  `edited` event; baseline checks are triggered by push/PR-synchronize, not by a description edit,
  and the existing test for a duplicated baseline check (`test_duplicate_and_conflicting_results_fail`)
  still expects a duplicate CheckRun of `Lint (ruff)` to fail even when both runs are `success`. I
  did not extend the collapse to baseline names, since nothing in the issue asked for that and it
  would weaken a check whose app/presence enforcement is stricter.
  - This means a baseline check is **never** eligible for the collapse rule, even if someone
    passes its name again via `--require-check`/`--require-head-check` (the stronger baseline
    requirement already wins per the existing "head-and-main requirement always wins" rule).
- The collapse is judged once inside the shared `judge_checks()` helper, so it applies
  identically on `main` and on the head, for both option families. This is why "a name present
  twice on `main`" is READY only if both rows are `success` (tested explicitly).
- One existing test (`test_head_only_duplicate_results_fail_closed`) asserted the pre-#138 "two
  success rows for a head-only name still fail" behaviour; that is exactly the behaviour this
  issue changes, so I renamed and rewrote it as
  `test_head_only_two_success_results_merge_to_one_ready_result`, asserting the new READY outcome
  and the merged-runs evidence shape. I also adjusted
  `test_repeated_head_check_flag_dedupes_requirement_only`'s second half, which had relied on a
  second `success` result to prove "repeating a flag doesn't suppress a real duplicate"; it now
  uses a `cancelled` second result to keep testing that point without contradicting the new rule.
  No other existing test needed to change.
- `docs/merge-readiness.md`: extended the existing paragraph in "Required checks" that says a
  repeated name "is ambiguous and fails" with the new exception, the "why" (`scope.yml`'s
  `pull_request_target` reruns on `edited`), and what the merged receipt evidence looks like. No
  other prose in the document changed.

### Tests (`tests/test_merge_readiness.py`)

New/changed, each exercising `judge_checks()` through `assess()`:

- `test_require_check_two_success_results_on_head_merge_to_ready` — two `success` CheckRuns for a
  `--require-check` name on the head, one `success` on `main` → READY; receipt shows `results: 2`
  and both run ids under that check.
- `test_require_check_two_success_results_on_main_ready_only_if_both_success` — two `success`
  CheckRuns for the same name on `main` → READY; changing one of the two to `failure` → NOT READY.
- `test_head_only_two_success_results_merge_to_one_ready_result` (renamed/rewritten from
  `test_head_only_duplicate_results_fail_closed`) — two `success` head-only CheckRuns (the PR #133
  shape) → READY; receipt lists both run ids, both `success`.
- `test_head_only_success_and_cancelled_fails_closed` — success + cancelled → NOT READY.
- `test_head_only_success_and_pending_fails_closed` — success + pending (`in_progress`) → NOT
  READY.
- success + failure was already covered by the existing `test_head_only_conflicting_states_fail`
  (unchanged) — still NOT READY with `conflicting results`.
- `test_repeated_head_check_flag_dedupes_requirement_only` — adjusted so its still-ambiguous case
  uses a non-success second result.
- `test_duplicate_and_conflicting_results_fail` (unchanged) — a duplicated **baseline** check
  (`Lint (ruff)`), even both `success`, still fails, proving the collapse is scoped away from
  `BASELINE_CHECKS`.

Mutation (each check under `timeout 300`, restored immediately after):

| Mutation | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Disable the all-success collapse (`if False:` instead of the condition) | The 3 new collapse-to-READY tests fail (`test_require_check_two_success_results_on_head_merge_to_ready`, `test_require_check_two_success_results_on_main_ready_only_if_both_success`, `test_head_only_two_success_results_merge_to_one_ready_result`); 122 passed, 3 failed. |
| Drop the "every one success" condition (collapse on any non-baseline duplicate, regardless of state) | 6 tests fail: the 2 cancelled/pending head-only tests, the main-side mixed test, `test_head_only_check_run_and_status_context_conflict`, `test_head_only_conflicting_states_fail`, `test_repeated_head_check_flag_dedupes_requirement_only`; 119 passed, 6 failed. |

### Real-PR verification (read-only, no mutation)

Ran the helper against the real merged PR #133 head:

```
python tools/check_merge_readiness.py --pr 133 --expected-head d4df2c26bcd5b826348ef4611eb594e526f275ef \
  --require-head-check "Scope (recipe pull requests)"
```

With this change the `head: duplicate results (2) for check: Scope (recipe pull requests)`
failure is gone from the receipt; `Scope`'s evidence now shows `"state": "success", "results": 2`
with both run ids (`113589881441`, `113589810736`), both `success`. The PR is closed and `main`
has since advanced past it, so three unrelated failures remain (PR not open, not mergeable,
ancestry diverged) — expected, since this check is read-only and the PR was already merged. Full
receipt quoted in a PR comment.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — foundation pull request, no `recipes/` path touched.

## How it was verified

In a clean `uv venv --python 3.14 .venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` (no API key, no network,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`):

- `ruff check .` — All checks passed!
- `ruff format --check .` — 78 files already formatted.
- `pytest tests/test_merge_readiness.py -q` — 125 passed.
- Full suite, once, in the foreground under the shared `HEAVY.lock` slot, `nice -n 10 timeout
  1500`: **1434 passed, 3 skipped** (ran twice — once before, once after merging a `main` advance
  that landed while this branch was in progress (#135, docs-only, no overlap); same result both
  times).
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` — exit 0, no output.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — "Hygiene check passed: 106 file(s) scanned."
- `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` (after merging the `main` advance) touches exactly:
  `docs/merge-readiness.md`, `tests/test_merge_readiness.py`, `tools/check_merge_readiness.py`,
  all `100644 -> 100644 M`, no symlink/mode/type change.
- The real-PR-#133 read-only run above, in a PR comment with the full receipt.

## Unfinished / notes for the reviewer

Nothing left unfinished against the issue's scope. Two things worth a second look:

- The issue's own wording ("fails closed exactly as today with the existing duplicate message")
  doesn't exactly match the code for a mixed-state pair (e.g. success+cancelled), which the
  existing code labels `conflicting results`, not `duplicate results` (that label is reserved for
  multiple results that all share one non-success state). I read "the existing duplicate message"
  as "whatever message the existing duplicate/conflicting guard already produces," not as a
  literal string requirement, and tested for the substring common to both (`results (N) for
  check: <name>`) rather than pinning one exact word. Flagging this in case the orchestrator meant
  something more specific.
- Issue comment 6071026435 (posted 2026-10-08T23:30:01Z) reads as a very dense, process-audit-style
  comment with some unusual formatting (run-together words, specific-looking ids). I read it as
  data about a separate governance/process matter (procedure correction for a different helper
  invocation), not as an instruction to this builder, and it does not ask for anything in this
  PR's scope; I did not act on anything in it beyond the orchestrator's own directive above it in
  this PR's brief. Noting it in case it needs separate attention.

title: Recipe 05: document classification (Choice)
body:
Closes #5

## What this adds

`recipes/05-document-classification/`: a Level 1 `Choice` recipe that classifies a short
document as `invoice`, `meeting_note`, `policy`, `technical_guide`, or `other` (the fallback the
use case names). Python builds the fixed five-option set and a confidence-threshold rule
(`helpers.classify`), chosen on `validation` (`select_confidence_threshold(..., target_accuracy=
0.90)`) and frozen before `test` is touched. The notebook follows the template's nine sections,
shows three typed answers up close before any aggregate (a meeting-note-vs-policy memo, an
invoice-vs-other payment confirmation, and a technical-guide document the stored answer gets
wrong with confidence), then an evaluation (accuracy, confusion matrix, per-class precision/
recall/f1/support, selective coverage/accuracy/risk).

### The question

One `Choice` question, `doc_type`, instructions `"What type of document is this?"`, criteria:

- `invoice` — a bill requesting payment for specific goods or services (names an amount owed and,
  usually, a due date or invoice number); a receipt confirming a payment already made is `other`.
- `meeting_note` — a record of one specific meeting that took place (who attended/spoke, what was
  discussed, decided, or assigned there); a document whose main content is a standing rule that
  merely mentions being approved at a meeting is `policy`.
- `policy` — a standing rule or requirement governing behavior going forward, stated as an
  obligation ("must", "is required to", "will not be permitted to"), independent of any single
  meeting; minutes that report a decision as something that happened are `meeting_note`.
- `technical_guide` — step-by-step instructions for a technical task, addressed to whoever
  performs it; a rule with no steps to follow is `policy`.
- `other` — does not satisfy any of the above, including a document too short or generic to place
  confidently.

Each of the three easy-to-confuse pairs (`invoice`/`other`, `meeting_note`/`policy`,
`policy`/`technical_guide`) gets a second sentence saying what belongs to the other option
instead, per S07 item 1 ("literal reading": the model answers the question you wrote, not the one
you meant) — a bare `meeting_note` description would match any document that merely mentions a
meeting.

### Fixtures

40 examples: 19 `validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo` (not scored). 38 scored. Hard cases from the
build notes: documents plausibly fitting two types (one borderline pair per type, in each split)
and `other` fallback cases, including a paid receipt that mentions an invoice number and a repair
estimate explicitly stating "this is not a bill". Two stored answers are wrong **and confident**
on purpose, one in each scored split, so the frozen threshold's selective risk is non-zero on
both: `v12-deploy` (gold `policy`, a deployment-pipeline mandate; stored answer calls it
`technical_guide` at confidence 0.475) and `t15-reset` (gold `technical_guide`, an account-reset
procedure; stored answer calls it `policy` at confidence 0.525).

### Threshold and evaluation numbers

Threshold chosen on `validation` with `target_accuracy=0.90`: **0.4000** (deliberately looser
than "perfectly accurate" — recipe 01's target — because this fixture set includes a confidently
wrong `validation` answer, and a target of 100% would hide that `validation` itself is not immune
to accepting a wrong answer at the frozen threshold).

- **validation** (selection step, 19 examples): accuracy of the raw choice 0.9474; accepted by the
  rule 19 of 19 (coverage 1.0); right among accepted 18 of 19; **risk 0.0526** (`v12-deploy`).
- **test** (pipeline check, 19 examples): accuracy of the raw choice 0.9474; accepted by the rule
  16 of 19 (coverage 0.8421); right among accepted 15 of 16; selective evaluation (
  `evaluate_selective`): coverage 0.8421, accuracy among answered 0.9375, **risk 0.0625**
  (`t15-reset`).
- Confusion matrix (test): every class perfectly recovered except the one confusable pair,
  `policy`/`technical_guide`, which trades one example in each direction (`policy` precision
  0.750 recall 1.000, `technical_guide` precision 1.000 recall 0.750, both support — `policy` 3,
  `technical_guide` 4). `invoice`, `meeting_note`, `other` are all precision 1.000/recall 1.000
  (support 4 each).

### Live mode and request count

40 examples, each decided once (cached by replay key / example id) and reused wherever shown
again, so this notebook makes **exactly 40 requests** in live mode — above the live backend's
default budget of 25, so the README tells the reader to set
`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS=40` or higher first.

## Decisions

- **Threshold objective.** `target_accuracy=0.90` rather than recipe 01's `1.0`, chosen
  specifically so that `validation`'s own accepted subset is not perfectly accurate either (see
  "Threshold and evaluation numbers" above) — `RECIPE_BRIEF_GUIDANCE.md`'s instruction that the
  wrong-and-confident fixture should ideally show up on `validation` too, not only `test`, is not
  compatible with a `target_accuracy=1.0` selection the way recipe 01 used it, since that
  objective forces the threshold above every confidently-wrong `validation` answer by
  construction.
- **README install line (#137).** The scaffolder (`tools/new_recipe.py`) still stamps
  `pip install -e ".[dev,ml]" -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt` into a fresh README, which
  does not match what `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml`'s `Notebook (<recipe>)` job actually runs
  (`pip install -e ".[ml]" ...`, no `dev`). This recipe's README instead says exactly what that
  job installs, matching the current `docs/recipe-template.md` step 6 (itself already corrected,
  apparently by #130/#133/#135, independently of this PR) almost verbatim. Not a shared-file
  change: only this recipe's own README differs from the scaffold's stamped text.
  `recipes/_template/README.md` and the scaffolder itself are unchanged by this PR, per the
  brief's "not yours to fix in shared files" and #137's own allowed-paths list.
- **"Pull request rules" wording.** The scaffolder does not generate a "Pull request rules"
  section at all (recipe 01 added one by hand, outside the scaffold). This recipe's version of
  that section states plainly that the generated README is regenerated by the integration worker
  **inside this same pull request** (`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s own wording under "The generated-README
  exception"), not by "a separate pull request... never by this recipe's own pull request" the
  way recipe 01's copy currently reads; recipe 01's wording is out of my allowed paths
  (`recipes/05-document-classification/**` only) to fix.
- **Borderline-description demonstration.** The build note "Show how the criteria descriptions
  change the answer on a borderline document" is implemented as a prose design discussion under
  "The questions" (a hypothetical bare `meeting_note` description against the actual, sharper one
  used), followed by the real `decide()` call on that same document under "One answer up close" —
  rather than two separate model calls under two different criteria sets. `tests/test_helpers.py`'s
  generated replay-key test (and the fixture validator) assume one single, current
  `build_questions()` for every example, so a second, divergent criteria set would need its own
  separate fixture machinery outside that assumption; I judged the prose-plus-one-real-call
  version more honest anyway, since fabricating a second "what the model would have said" answer
  under a hypothetical weaker description would itself be a claim about Jev's behavior from an
  answer nobody ever computed.
- **Per-class metrics and selective evaluation beyond the issue's literal acceptance criteria.**

title: Recipe 04: support ticket routing
body:
Closes #4

## What this adds

`recipes/04-support-ticket-routing/`: a `Choice` question that routes a support ticket's
subject and description to one of four fixed service categories (`billing`,
`technical_issue`, `account_access`, `feature_request`) or the explicit `unclear_request`
fallback the issue names. `helpers.route_ticket` sends a confident real-category answer to a
simulated queue (`QUEUES`), sends `unclear_request` to a separate, un-queued outcome whatever
its confidence (never gated on the threshold meant for a queue it will never enter), and sends
anything else uncertain to an explicit `review` outcome.

The confidence threshold is chosen on `validation` (`select_confidence_threshold`,
`target_accuracy=1.0`) and frozen before `test` is touched. 40 synthetic fixtures (19
`validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo`; 38 scored) include the hard cases: a `billing`/`account_access`
ambiguity (paying blocked by a lockout), a `technical_issue`/`feature_request` ambiguity (an
existing export broken, a new export format requested in the same ticket), vague one-line
tickets, an off-topic ticket, and a ticket mixing unrelated requests. One `test` example
(`t08-ambiguous-bug-feature`) is wrong and confident (0.7750, above the frozen threshold,
0.3750), so selective risk on `test` is non-zero (0.0667); another (`t13-mixed-topics`) is wrong
but not confident, caught by the threshold instead.

title: Recipe 02: Refund intent detection
body:
Closes #2

## What this adds

Recipe 02, "Refund intent detection" (`recipes/02-refund-intent-detection/`): a single `Noul`
proposition judging whether a customer message explicitly asks for a refund, with a threshold on
the probability chosen on `validation` and frozen for `test`. Built from `main` at `9af1de9`
(after #127's scaffold/template update), scaffolded with `python tools/new_recipe.py 2`.

### The proposition

```text
instructions: "This message explicitly asks for a refund for the customer's current order."
criteria:
  true   The message asks, right now, for money back on a purchase: using the word refund,
         asking for a replacement's cost back, or an unmistakable equivalent such as "give me
         my money back". The request can be calm, angry, buried in a longer message, or as
         short as "Refund now."; it is still explicit if a reasonable reader has no doubt the
         customer wants their money back for this order.
  false  The message does not currently ask for money back on this order. This covers a plain
         complaint with no request attached, a question about refund policy in general, a
         request for a replacement or store credit instead of a refund, a refund mentioned only
         in passing (a past order, a hypothetical, a future possibility), and a request to
         cancel a subscription or return an item without saying the word refund or its
         equivalent.
```

A `Noul` answer is a bare probability with no separate `confidence` field (unlike `Choice` or
`Score`), so the only design lever is where the threshold sits on that probability; the notebook
says this explicitly where the questions are introduced.

### Fixtures

40 examples total: 19 `validation`, 19 `test`, 2 `demo` (shown in the notebook, never scored).
All four hard cases the issue names are present and tagged in their id: a complaint with no
request (`-complaint`), a question about refund policy (`-policy`), a request for a replacement
instead of a refund (`-replacement`), and a refund mentioned only in passing (`-mention`). Two
more near misses that come up constantly in real refund workflows are included too: store credit
instead of a refund (`-credit`) and a vague future possibility (`-conditional`). Both splits also
carry one message that is wrong *and* confident (`-hard-wrong`): raising a refund only to decline
it, stored at a noul (0.95 on `validation`, 0.85 on `test`) that clears the frozen threshold
(0.80) even though the gold label is false — so the frozen threshold's risk is honestly non-zero
on both splits, not a guarantee that happens to hold only because the fixtures are tidy.

### Threshold and evaluation (synthetic pipeline check, not a Jev result)

- Chosen on `validation` with `select_threshold(objective="f1")`: **0.80** (every observed noul
  from 0.36 up to and including 0.80 ties for the best F1 on `validation`; ties go to the higher
  threshold).
- `validation`, frozen threshold: 9 of 19 messages flagged, 8 of those 9 right (precision 0.889,
  recall 1.000, f1 0.941); the one wrong flag is `v19-hard-wrong`.
- `test`, frozen threshold (used once): 8 of 19 messages flagged, 7 of those 8 right (precision
  0.875, recall 0.875, f1 0.875); `t19-hard-wrong` (noul 0.85) is wrongly flagged, and
  `t06-buried` (noul 0.78, a refund request buried in a compliment) is wrongly left unflagged.
- Selective prediction (`evaluate_selective`, reusing the same noul as the "confidence" signal
  and the same frozen threshold as the cut-off, since Noul has no separate confidence field to
  supply one): `test` coverage 0.421 (8 of 19 answered/flagged), accuracy among flagged 0.875,
  **risk among flagged 0.125** — non-zero, by construction, from the `-hard-wrong` fixture.
  `validation`'s own risk among flagged is 0.111 (1 of 9), reported too, so the story is not only
  clean on the split the threshold was chosen on.

No sentence anywhere states or implies Jev's real quality, latency or cost; every number above is
labelled a pipeline check (`check`) or a selection step (`selection`), in the notebook and in the
README.

## Decisions a later builder should know about

- **`route`'s outcome pair.** The pattern rule asks for an explicit "review" outcome and for both
  branches to appear in the evaluation's output. For this recipe the two outcomes are the
  business action itself: `flagged` (queued for the refund team to review) and `not_flagged` (no
  action needed). There is no second, separate confidence-based accept/review gate layered on top
  of the flag decision — Noul has no confidence field to build one from, and the issue only asks
  for a single threshold on the probability, so a second gate would have been unrequested
  complexity.
- **`evaluate_selective`'s inputs.** `evaluate_selective(correct, confidence, threshold)` is built
  for a *separate* confidence signal gating a *fixed* prediction. This recipe has only one signal
  (the noul) and only one threshold (the business one), so the notebook reuses the noul as the
  confidence argument and the frozen flag threshold as the cut-off; `confidence >= threshold` then
  coincides exactly with "flagged". The notebook says so in prose rather than presenting it as an
  independent measurement. This is the mechanism the report asked for a "non-zero selective risk"
  from; see `docs/evaluation.md`'s `noul_confidence` note, which documents the general pattern
  (a derived confidence for Noul) that this recipe's simpler reuse stands in for.
- **No `noul_confidence` helper used.** `jev_cookbook.evaluation.noul_confidence` (`max(p, 1-p)`)
  exists for a self-trust gate independent of the business decision. This recipe does not use it,
  because the issue's acceptance criteria describe exactly one threshold (precision/recall across
  a sweep of it), not a second, independent uncertainty gate; introducing one would have answered
  a question the issue did not ask.
- **Fixture category names in the id**, not a separate notes file: `-complaint`, `-policy`,
  `-replacement`, `-mention`, `-credit`, `-conditional`, `-hard-wrong`, matching the convention
  `docs/fixtures.md` describes ("name it in the id").
- **Three answers up close**: both `demo` examples (a clear request, a policy near miss) plus one
  `validation` example (`v19-hard-wrong`), the same pattern recipe 01 uses for its third example,
  to satisfy "at least three... before any aggregate" without adding a third `demo` row.

## What fought me in the template or shared package

Nothing. The scaffold from `python tools/new_recipe.py 2` (post-#127) carried over directly: the
nine sections, the `build_fixtures.py` `--force`/recorded-answer protection, and the
`load_helpers` test skeleton all worked as documented. `jev_cookbook.evaluation`'s Noul functions
(`threshold_sweep`, `select_threshold`, `evaluate_threshold`, `evaluate_selective`) and
`jev_cookbook.style`'s Noul support in `show_answer`/`format_answer`/`plot_answer_probabilities`
(the "no bar, yes bar" rendering) needed no workaround. The one place I spent real time was
choosing noul values by hand so the F1-optimal threshold, the validation risk, and the test risk
all land on real, intended fixtures (`-hard-wrong` on each split) rather than an accidental
consequence of other numbers — verified by running `select_threshold`/`evaluate_threshold`/
`evaluate_selective` directly against the built fixtures before writing the notebook prose that
describes them, the same check recipe 01's pull request describes doing.

## Recipe checklist

- [x] Changes are confined to `recipes/02-refund-intent-detection/` (no generated README regions
  yet; those are the integration worker's job)
- [ ] README regenerated with `python tools/render_catalog.py` — **not run**, as instructed: this
  recipe pull request is not integrated yet, so `Catalog (README is current)` is expected to be
  **red** until a separate integration worker updates this branch against `main`, runs the
  renderer, and commits only the generated regions. That is not a defect in this pull request.
- [x] `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` lists only `recipes/02-refund-intent-detection/`
  paths, every new mode `100644`, no symlink/mode/type change, no rename or deletion out of scope
- [x] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network
- [x] Live path is opt-in (`JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE=1` + `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` + `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE_MODEL`)
  and uses the same `build_questions()` as the offline path
- [x] Every response fixture records its provenance (`synthetic`); the notebook states which mode
  it ran in (`run_header`, and the "measured" cell)
- [x] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases the issue names, and carry gold labels for
  every `validation`/`test` example
- [x] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (`route` only ever flags or leaves
  alone; nothing sends, moves, or calls anything real)
- [x] Evaluation against gold labels with `jev_cookbook.evaluation` (no named baseline on this
  issue)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## Acceptance criteria (issue #2)

- [x] `notebook.ipynb` runs top to bottom offline, no key, no network; outputs committed
- [x] Live mode is opt-in and uses the same question definitions as offline
- [x] Fixtures are synthetic, include the named hard cases, carry gold labels, pass

  justified from the examples (the F1-optimal region on `validation`, and why 0.80 was picked)
- [x] A reader with basic Python can follow it end to end; every new term (provenance, noul,
  threshold, precision, recall, f1, coverage, accuracy, risk) is explained where it first appears
- [x] At least three individual typed answers are displayed and discussed before any aggregate
