title: Hygiene: do not flag identifier keyword arguments as high-entropy tokens
body:
Closes #114

## What this adds

The entropy rule no longer scores a word that is an identifier assigned a bare identifier, for example the ruff-style keyword argument `startup_timeout=KERNEL_START_TIMEOUT`. Before: a Python file and a notebook code cell with `startup_timeout=KERNEL_START_TIMEOUT`, `retry_policy=DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY_SETTINGS` and `max_requests_per_run=DEFAULT_MAX_REQUESTS` were each reported as `high-entropy-token` (reproduced before the change). The same constant `_IDENT_ASSIGNMENT` and the same two-line skip in `_scan_secrets_line` are in `tools/check_hygiene.py` and `src/jev_cookbook/fixtures/_scan.py`. `tests/test_fixtures.py` adds the new constant to the parity list. `docs/development.md` gains one clause about coverage.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable (foundation work).

- [ ] Changes are confined to `recipes/NN-slug/` (n/a)
- [ ] README regenerated (n/a)
- [ ] Diff lists only recipe paths (n/a)
- [ ] Notebook runs offline (n/a)
- [ ] Live path is opt-in (n/a)
- [ ] Response fixtures record provenance (n/a)
- [ ] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost (nothing here makes one)
- [ ] Fixtures synthetic (n/a)
- [ ] Python owns every side effect (n/a)
- [ ] Evaluation against gold labels (n/a)
- [ ] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## How it was verified

- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed, 82 files scanned.
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed. `ruff format --check .`: 60 files already formatted.
- `pytest` (3.14 default): 1109 passed, 2 skipped. `py -3.10 -m pytest`: 1109 passed, 2 skipped.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0.
- The existing leak set, false-positive set, URL/hash set and the 300-key random base64 test all pass unchanged.
- Mutation 1 (exemption disabled with `if False:`): the four new exemption cases fail with the original `high-entropy-token` finding (plus the repository self-scan, since the tests contain these lines).
- Mutation 2 (exemption widened to any `name=\S+`): five new leak-test cases fail (`retry_policy=<mixed>`, upper-case mixed, trailing `=`, `DEFAULT_<mixed>`, `default_<mixed>`).
- Both mutations were reverted before commit.

## Decisions

- Exempt only when the whole word matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=` followed by runs of letters of one case or of digits, joined by `_` or `.`. A value mixing letters and digits in one run (`a1B2...`), mixing cases in a run, or carrying `/`, `+`, `=` or quotes is still scored. camelCase right sides are therefore still scored.
- The left side must be a plain identifier; `self.x=CONSTANT` is not exempt.
- Only the entropy rule is touched. `secret-assignment`, `bearer-token`, header and vendor rules are unchanged, so `token=...` and `api_key=...` keep their outcomes.
- Parity test expectations moved by one name (`_IDENT_ASSIGNMENT` in `SCANNER_PATTERNS`).

## Unfinished

Nothing.

## Fix round 1

Addresses the review (comment 6033907044) on `2581d089`.

1. Left side: `_IDENT_ASSIGNMENT` now gives the name the same single-case-run grammar as the value (runs of letters of one case or of digits joined by `_`, starting with a letter run). A 34-character mixed-case key followed by `=1`, `=true` or `=TRUE` is scored again.
2. Secret names: a word whose left side contains api key, secret, token, password, passwd, access key or credential (case-insensitive, new `_SECRET_NAME`) is never exempt. Attack lines added as tests: `token=`, `password=`, `passwd=`, `client_credential=` with 36 lowercase letters; `secret=`, `aws_secret_access_key=`, `API_KEY=`, `access_key=` with 36 uppercase letters; `db_password=` with a snake_case passphrase.
3. Docs: `docs/development.md` and the `tools/check_hygiene.py` docstring now describe the rule exactly, and the docstring has a "does not cover" sentence. Cost of the guard: a long constant assigned to a secret-named keyword (for example `max_tokens=DEFAULT_...`) is scored again.
4. The two exemption cases that never reached the threshold are replaced by three that do, and every exemption case now asserts it would score without the exemption.

Mutation: left side widened back to any letters and digits fails the 3 mixed-case left-side tests; the secret-name guard removed fails 9 attack tests.

Verification: `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean; `pytest` 1121 passed, 2 skipped on the default interpreter and on `py -3.10`; catalog check exit 0; `python tools/check_hygiene.py` passed (82 files); all five CI checks SUCCESS on `2a44c4d08b281fbf52a9306b7efab99f44477411`.

## Fix round 2

Addresses the review (comment 6048643436) on `2a44c4d08b281fbf52a9306b7efab99f44477411`. The rule itself was judged sound (400,000 random words probed, zero newly exempt; all 300 base64/base64url keys still caught under every left-side name tried). Two must-change items, both one-liners, plus one of the non-blocking notes:

1. **Parity gap on `_SECRET_NAME`** (`tests/test_fixtures.py`): `SCANNER_PATTERNS` compared `_IDENT_ASSIGNMENT` but not `_SECRET_NAME`, so the packaged fixture scanner's secret-name guard could drift from `tools/check_hygiene.py` with the suite still green. Added `"_SECRET_NAME"` to `SCANNER_PATTERNS`.
   - Proof: with `_SECRET_NAME`'s pattern replaced by `r"zzzz_never_matches_anything"` in `src/jev_cookbook/fixtures/_scan.py` only (the repository copy untouched), `test_the_packaged_scanner_has_the_same_rules_as_the_repository_scanner` now fails (`AssertionError: _SECRET_NAME`), where before this fix it passed (186 passed, full suite 1121 passed/2 skipped, nothing failing). Mutation made and reverted in the worktree; `git status --porcelain` was empty afterward.
2. **`docs/fixtures.md` stated the old, unqualified rule** (around lines 183-186): "Long random-looking tokens are always flagged" is no longer true. Reworded the bullet to "are flagged" and added the same exception clause (name not secret-bearing, both sides single-case letter or digit runs, the `startup_timeout=KERNEL_START_TIMEOUT` example) that `docs/development.md` and the `tools/check_hygiene.py` docstring already carry, so all three copies of the rule now agree.
3. **Self-scan independence** (`tests/test_hygiene.py`): `IDENTIFIER_ASSIGNMENTS` held seven literal 32+ character `name=value` strings, so `test_the_repository_itself_is_clean` depended on the exemption to keep this file itself quiet, rather than checking the exemption independently. Replaced the literals with values assembled from pieces under 32 characters each (`_KERNEL_TIMEOUT`, `_RETRY_POLICY_SETTINGS`, `_MAX_REQUESTS`, `_LIQUOR_JUGS`, `_WAX_BUZZ_PIXEL`, `_WAX_BULGE`), the same convention the file already uses for `KEY`, `LOWER_36`, `UPPER_36`, `MIXED_34` and `LONG_VALUE`. The seven assembled lines are byte-identical to the originals at run time (verified directly), so the exemption test is unchanged; only the source file's literal content changed.
   - Proof: scanning `tests/test_hygiene.py` with the repository scanner gives zero findings both before and after this change; with `_IDENT_ASSIGNMENT` additionally mutated to never match (in a throwaway copy, reverted immediately), scanning `tests/test_hygiene.py` still gives zero findings, confirming the file's own source no longer needs the exemption to stay clean.

### What was not changed

Nothing outside the two must-change items and this one suggestion; the grammar, the other suggestions, and the `chr(10)` note were left as the review said they were not blocking.

### Verification (head to be pushed)

- Fresh venvs, `uv venv --python 3.14` and `uv venv --python 3.10`, `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` in each.
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed (both interpreters).
- `ruff format --check .`: 60 files already formatted (both interpreters).
- `pytest`: 1121 passed, 2 skipped on 3.14; 1121 passed, 2 skipped on 3.10.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0 (both interpreters).
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed, 82 files scanned (both interpreters).
- Mutation proof for finding 1 run and reverted as described above; worktree clean except the three intended files.

title: Foundation: retry the kernel start once in the notebook executor (#109)
body:
Closes #109

## What this adds

`tools/execute_notebook.py` retries the kernel start once and waits up to 180 s for a kernel to answer. Nothing else about execution changes. Two directly-launched kernels in the tests get the same treatment. Three tests pin the retry's limits.

## Cause (reproduced)

I could not reproduce with the loads the issue describes: with 2 and then 6 looping `execute_notebook.py` runs, and with 4 concurrent test runs on top, everything passed. It reproduced once the machine was saturated (64 busy-loop processes on 32 cores, plus 8 concurrent runs of the three notebook-executing test files). Observed failures, all of them kernel start-up, all raised before any cell ran:

- `RuntimeError: Kernel didn't respond in 60 seconds` (jupyter_client's default wait; the executor already recognised this one).
- `RuntimeError: Kernel died before replying to kernel_info`. The kernel process crashed in `init_sockets` with `zmq.error.ZMQError: Address in use (addr='tcp://127.0.0.1:53080')`: two kernels picked the same TCP port. The executor did not recognise this message, so it surfaced as a raw traceback.
- Afterwards the process prints `AssertionError` from `nbclient/client.py` `_async_cleanup_kernel` (`assert self.km is not None`) in an atexit callback after a failed start. I think this is the "unexplained `AssertionError`" at the end of the #107 review run, but that is an inference: no traceback from that run was kept, so I cannot confirm it. It does not change the exit status. (Fix round 1 removes it.)

Also seen under that saturation and not fixable here: `MemoryError` inside a cell (the machine ran out of memory while 8 test runs plus kernels were live). That is a real cell failure and is deliberately not retried.

The executor tests (`test_template.py`, `test_new_recipe.py` including the scaffold walkthrough) share the cause; of the three test files it hit `test_template.py::test_two_executions_of_the_template_give_byte_identical_files` four times and `test_style_notebook_display.py::test_a_cell_ending_with_run_header_has_no_echoed_output` once. The #105 scaffold-test failure itself (`test_a_scaffold_runs_once_the_helpers_and_fixtures_exist`) was never reproduced: it never failed in any of my runs. It calls the same `execute`, so it shares the exposure, but that it failed for this cause is an inference.

## Fix, and why this one

A lock would not help: the competing kernels are other processes (other agents, other pytest runs), so a session lock cannot serialise them. A start-up retry and a longer wait match the cause.

- `run_in_fresh_kernel` (new): builds a fresh manager and client and executes.
- `execute` reads the notebook and calls it; if it raises `RuntimeError` with `Kernel didn't respond` or `Kernel died before replying`, it re-reads the notebook and tries once more; a second failure raises `KernelStartError`. `DeadKernelError` (a kernel dying mid-run) is never retried. A failing cell, a cell timeout and a stderr write are never retried.
- `START_WAIT = 180` is passed as `startup_timeout` (per start, not per cell; `--timeout` is unchanged).
- Both messages count as "kernel did not start" (exit 1, one line).
- `tests/test_style_notebook_display.py::_run` does the same for its direct `NotebookClient` use.
- `docs/recipe-template.md`: the "run executions one after another, or retry once" advice now says the tool does the retry.

No assertion was touched or loosened.

## Commands and results

Default interpreter (3.14), venv in the worktree, two `execute_notebook.py` loops running throughout:

- `pytest` x3 in a row under the two loops: `1095 passed, 2 skipped` each time (110 s, 111 s, 106 s). Before the hygiene rename below, an earlier set of three runs failed only `test_the_repository_itself_is_clean` because my first constant name tripped the secret scanner; renamed `START_WAIT`.
- `ruff check .`: All checks passed. `ruff format --check .`: 60 files already formatted.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0. `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed, 82 files.
- `py -3.10 -m pytest`: `1095 passed, 2 skipped`.
- Saturation rerun with the fix (same 64 burners + 8 concurrent runs of the three files): 8 of 8 passed (one took 328 s because it waited out slow starts; without the fix that wait was 60 s).
- Mutation: appending `raise RuntimeError(...)` to `recipes/_template/helpers.py` makes `test_a_scaffold_runs_once_the_helpers_and_fixtures_exist` fail with `CellExecutionError` (`1 failed in 4.02 s`), not retried. Reverted.
- New tests: a start failure then success (2 calls, notebook output "ran"); two start failures (exactly 2 calls, exit 1, "the kernel did not start"); a failing cell (exactly 1 call).

## Decisions

- Retry is once, only for the two start-up messages, only before any cell ran. Anything else propagates.
- The start wait is 180 s, separate from the per-cell `--timeout`.
- No `tests/conftest.py` and no lock: see above.
- A kernel that never starts takes up to 2 x 180 s = 360 s to fail.

## Unfinished

- The retry cannot help a port race that strikes both attempts, or memory exhaustion. I did not find a way to provoke a real scaffold-test failure at the loads the issue describes.

## Checklist

Recipe checklist: not applicable (foundation work).

- [x] Lint, format, tests, catalog check and hygiene pass locally on 3.14 and 3.10.

## Fix round 1

- Description: the #107 `AssertionError` attribution is labelled an inference and the #105 non-reproduction is stated plainly (above).
- Module docstring of `tools/execute_notebook.py`: the first bullet no longer says "run them one after another, or retry once"; it says the tool starts a fresh kernel once more.
- Exit-time noise: `run_in_fresh_kernel` unregisters nbclient's exit hook (`atexit.unregister(client._cleanup_kernel)`) when execution raises; the kernel was already cleaned up. New test `test_a_failed_start_leaves_no_exit_time_noise` runs a subprocess with a failed first start and a good retry and asserts no `AssertionError` on stderr; it fails without the change (checked).
- Worst case (2 x `START_WAIT`, 360 s) documented in the docstring.
- The retry tests are parametrised over both start-up messages.
- `tests/test_style_notebook_display.py::_run` takes the message list from `START_FAILURES` in the tool.
- Merged `origin/main` (merge commit; brings in #105). Results: ruff check, ruff format --check, catalog check, hygiene all pass; `pytest` 1098 passed, 2 skipped on 3.14 and on 3.10.

Closes #69

## What this adds

## Staleness comparison as implemented

1. Any `error` output (a `raises-exception` cell) or `stderr` stream is a failure, in the committed and the fresh notebook, even when they are identical.
2. The only normalisation: every `outputs[*].data["image/png"]` becomes a presence marker. Everything else (sources, ids, metadata, execution counts, text/plain, streams, other mime types) must be equal as parsed JSON.
3. **Deviation from the brief's "presence only", on purpose.** The #69 comments require a changed chart to be rejected, and presence-only would pass it. Each PNG pair is therefore also compared by what it shows (`compare_png`): equal bytes pass; otherwise aspect ratio within 8%, both shrunk (box filter) to a 64 by 48 grid, a cell is unmatched if nothing within one cell of it in the other image is within 30/255 in every channel, and the figures differ when any 2 by 2 block is unmatched. Calibrated on the template's figures from matplotlib 3.10.9 and 3.11.2 (pixel sizes 664x600 vs 647x602) and on probes; CI on Linux also measured 0 unmatched blocks on the template. Stale probe: a changed bar chart with source, `text/plain` and counts intact gives 258 unmatched blocks and fails. **Limits** (documented, and pinned by a test): titles, labels and in-cell digits that do not change a coloured area, bar moves under about 5% of plot height, anything smaller than about 3% x 4% of the figure pass.

### Decisions this round makes (for later builders and reviewers)

- **The uid boundary, not a copy or a second job, is the enforcement**, per A4's and B4's own preferred option: a dedicated system user (`nbrunner`) with its own empty `$HOME`, writable only in its own copy of the recipe. `--no-new-privs` plus a dropped `sudo` prevents regaining the runner's uid from inside; it does not (and cannot) defend against a kernel/interpreter-level privilege-escalation vulnerability, which is out of scope and now says so in the docs.
- **The runner's hosted Python toolcache (`$pythonLocation`) is installed world-writable** by the `setup-python` action (so a plain `pip install` works without `sudo`). Found live by this round's own first CI run of the new self-test (`FAIL: nbrunner can write .../site-packages`). Fixed with `sudo chmod -R o-w "$pythonLocation"` right after `Install`, closing both the "drop a new `sitecustomize.py`" route and "overwrite an existing stdlib/site-packages file" (a narrower, directory-only fix was tried first and replaced with this broader one).
- **The runner's own `$HOME` (`/home/runner`, the parent of `$RUNNER_TEMP`) is mode `750`, not world-traversable.** Without `chmod o+x` on it, nbrunner cannot reach *anything* under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, including its own writable recipe copy — found live via `namei -l` in CI. Deleting the line left every existing test green | **Done** | New test `test_execute_itself_raises_and_leaves_the_file_unwritten_when_the_namespace_is_demanded_and_absent` (`tests/test_notebook_ci_sandbox.py`) drives the real `execute()` call path with the demand set and `os.getpid` patched off 1 (so `in_an_isolated_pid_namespace()` is genuinely `False`, not mocked away), and asserts `execute()` raises `PidNamespaceNotActive` with the notebook file byte-for-byte unchanged. **Mutation-proven**: deleting the `require_pid_namespace_if_demanded()` line from `execute()` → only this new test fails (`Failed: DID NOT RAISE PidNamespaceNotActive`), the other 41 tests across both files stay green, matching B8's own "40 passed, not caught" before this test existed; restoring the line → all 42 tests pass. |

### Suggestions taken (cheap, non-blocking; one shared between seats)

- **A8 suggestion 1 / B8 suggestion 3** — `docs/notebook-ci.md`, "Run time and scaling": the one-recipe measurement and its table row cited commit `1ab2cf4` as "this pull request's head," which was already wrong (the head was `358ca67`) and will go wrong again the moment any later commit moves the head. Reworded to cite it as "fix round 6's own code commit" instead, so the sentence does not need updating every round.
- **B8 suggestion 1 and 2** — `docs/notebook-ci.md`, "`get_backend(fixtures=...)` and the fixtures gate": softened the containment claim to what the uid boundary actually guarantees. A cell can stage an unvalidated file inside its own writable `fixtures/` copy and read it back in the same run (the committed and fresh runs stage it identically, so staleness does not catch it either), and a cell can rewrite the copy's own `helpers.py` mid-run for later cells in that run to import. The boundary keeps the staged file or rewritten module from ever becoming a committed, reviewable artifact, and protects the *other* jobs from a notebook reaching outside its own sandbox — it does not protect a notebook's own copy of itself from the notebook; that is a human reviewer's job, stated plainly now.
- **B8 suggestion 4** — `docs/development.md`, "Running CI on one recipe": both documented local reproductions of CI now start with `set -e`, so a failed `execute_notebook.py` run stops the block instead of letting every later command keep going and end by reporting a fresh, matching notebook — the same shape as M1, in a shell with no pipe at all (hit for real by B8's own builder pass). The sudo variant's `pgrep ... && { ...; exit 1; }` survivor check is rewritten as `if sudo pgrep ...; then ...; fi`: the `&&` form's own exit status is nonzero on the *good* path too (`pgrep` itself exits 1 when it finds nothing), so under the new `set -e` it would have aborted the script right there even when nothing was wrong.

### Suggestions declined (not taken this round, with reasons)

- A8's non-blocking suggestions 2-4 (pinning `$RUNNER_TEMP/execute-notebook.log`'s own freshness; A6 S4's open `--config-env` pin; A6 S6's unannotated demonstration table) and B8's suggestion 5 (the same demonstration-table annotation as A6 S6) — left for a later round if a reviewer asks for them; the brief for this round scoped the work to the must-change findings plus the four suggestions listed above, and taking the rest unasked risks exactly the kind of untasked change `BUILDER_RULES.md` and the fix-rounds contract both warn against.
- B8's suggestion 6 (the `pid namespace: active` grep could in principle be fooled by a cell writing to the step's own fd via `/proc/1/fd/1`) — B8 itself could not reproduce this (no root, no sandbox available in review either) and says it is moot once the step's exit code propagates, which M1 above now restores; it was the stated reason M1 mattered more than relying on the grep as the primary signal, not a separate gap to close.
- B6's suggestion 3 (catch the kill helper's `RuntimeError` in `main()` so it prints one line like every other failure, and loosen the 2.0 s sweep deadline) — carried forward from round 6, still not taken, for the same reason: explicitly non-blocking in both reviews that have mentioned it.

### Commands run and results (existing venvs, this head, Linux)

- `ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .`: 71 files already formatted.
- `pytest tests/test_notebook_ci_workflows.py tests/test_notebook_ci_sandbox.py -q` (`timeout 300`, `nice -n 10`): **42 passed**.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: "Hygiene check passed: 96 file(s) scanned."
- `tools/check_recipe_scope.py` not run: it is the `Scope` workflow's own script, for recipe pull requests only (`--base`/`--head`/`--branch`/`--body-file` against a recipe diff); this is a foundation pull request with no `recipes/` change in its diff, consistent with both reviews' own confirmation that no `Scope` row exists in this pull request's checks at all.
- Full suite, once, under the shared heavy-job slot, in the foreground: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 timeout 1500 nice -n 10 python -m pytest -q` → **1369 passed, 3 skipped in 231.25s** (two more passing tests than round 6's 1367, the two new tests this round).
- Mutations, each reverted after confirming (see the per-item table above for exact output): `shell: bash` line removed → `test_execute_step_sets_pipefail_shell` fails; `\|\| true` appended to the real pipeline (with `shell: bash` restored) → the same test fails on its second assertion; `require_pid_namespace_if_demanded()` call deleted from `execute()` → `test_execute_itself_raises_and_leaves_the_file_unwritten_when_the_namespace_is_demanded_and_absent` fails and nothing else does. Each reverted immediately after confirming, and the full suite above was run only once, on the final, unmutated tree.
- `gh pr checks 108 --watch` (unpiped) after pushing `6e7ffed`: all **nine** checks `pass` — `Lint (ruff)`, `Catalog (README is current)`, `Tests (py3.10)`, `Tests (py3.14)`, `Hygiene (secrets and notebook outputs)`, `Notebooks (discover)`, `Notebook (_template)`, `Notebooks (execute)`, `Fixtures (validate)`. `gh pr view 108 --json statusCheckRollup` read directly afterward: the same nine `SUCCESS` entries, at head `6e7ffedf2e78bfa12ee84e237db7e60496f2a411`.
- Processes swept before and after the full run: `ps -eo pid,etimes,comm \| grep -iE 'pytest'` showed nothing running, either time. One unrelated, long-running process belonging to a different session on this shared host matched an earlier, broader `grep -E 'pytest\|execute_notebook'` sweep on substrings inside its own command-line text; it was not started by this task, was not touched, and nothing in its command line was treated as an instruction.

### Decisions this round makes

- `shell: bash` was chosen over `set -o pipefail` as the first line of the `run:` block, or dropping the pipe and `cat`-ing the log afterward: it is the one-line, declarative form both reviews named first, it reads at the step level (so a reviewer sees it without reading into the script body), and it is exactly what the tests pin.
- The new `execute()`-ordering test (B8 M2) patches `os.getpid` rather than `in_an_isolated_pid_namespace` or `require_pid_namespace_if_demanded` itself, so it exercises the real function the real call path uses, not a stand-in for either — the same principle the existing `test_execute_calls_the_guard_before_writing` already uses for the kill helper.
- The two pipefail mutations (A8's missing `shell: bash`, B8's `\|\| true`) are different enough in shape that one assertion could not cover both; rather than generalise to a single clever regex, the test keeps two plain, separately-named assertions, matching this test file's existing style of linear, explicit checks over compact ones.

### Still unfinished / carried forward

- `get_backend(fixtures=...)`'s shared-code half is still not implemented here; belongs to #65/#66, as before.
- Everything else carried from rounds 1-6 is unchanged and still covered by its existing tests.

## Fix round 8

Resolves A9 ([comment 6056774894](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/108#issuecomment-6056774894), APPROVE) and B9 ([comment 6057079492](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/108#issuecomment-6057079492), CHANGES-NEEDED), both on head `6e7ffedf2e78bfa12ee84e237db7e60496f2a411`. Final head of this round: **`7858419061573e451b421db2aa8aa2f03c16e5ab`**.

### Must change

| Item | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B9 M1 — `docs/development.md`, "Running CI on one recipe": `mkdir -p /tmp/run && cp -R recipes/NN-slug /tmp/run/NN-slug` copies *into* an existing `/tmp/run/NN-slug` on every run after the first (`cp -R src dst` nests `dst/src-basename` when `dst` already exists), so a second run re-executes the previous run's stale copy — its old `helpers.py`, its old `fixtures/` — and the freshness check then reports that stale copy as a fresh, matching run, which it is not. The `sudo` variant carries the identical line, but fails loudly instead (the previous copy is `nbrunner_local`-owned, mode 700, so a plain `cp` cannot write into it on the next run) | **Done** | `rm -rf /tmp/run/NN-slug` added before the `cp -R` in the plain block; `sudo rm -rf /tmp/run/NN-slug` added before it in the `sudo` block (plain `rm -rf` cannot remove a `nbrunner_local`-owned, mode-700 directory as your own user, so it must run as root there). `rm -rf` was chosen over the GNU-only `cp -RT recipes/NN-slug /tmp/run/NN-slug` because the section's own heading names two platforms ("Git Bash on Windows, or Linux") and `rm -rf` before `cp -R` behaves identically under GNU coreutils (Linux) and Git Bash's MSYS2 coreutils (Windows), where `cp -RT` either is not available or behaves differently depending on the MSYS2 cp build in use. `docs/notebook-ci.md` was checked for the same pattern (`grep -n 'cp -R\|/tmp/run' docs/notebook-ci.md`) and has none; no change was needed there. **Reproduced, bug and fix, in a scratch copy of `recipes/_template`** (not `/tmp`, to avoid colliding with other agents on this shared host; the mechanism is identical): <br>• Clean copy, executed, matches the committed notebook (baseline). <br>• Edited `_template/helpers.py`'s `billing` description (moves the replay key, the same edit B9 used on recipe 1), then ran the *old, buggy* block verbatim against the still-existing directory: the tree grew a nested, unused `_template/_template/` copy carrying the edit, the top-level directory's stale `notebook.ipynb`/`helpers.py` were re-executed unchanged, `execute_notebook.py` exited 0, and `check_notebook_fresh.py` reported `recipes/_template/notebook.ipynb: matches a fresh offline run` — the false positive B9 described. <br>• A genuinely fresh copy of the same edited source (`rm -rf` then `cp -R`) instead failed at execution with `ReplayMiss: no stored response for replay key ...`, exit 1 — what CI always does. <br>• With the fix applied (`rm -rf` before the documented block's `cp -R`), re-running the same "second run after an edit" scenario now also fails with the same `ReplayMiss`, exit 1, matching the genuinely-fresh behaviour instead of the false positive. |

### Suggestions taken

- **A9 S1** — the parenthetical after the `sudo` block's `if sudo pgrep -u nbrunner_local; then ...; fi` claimed the `pgrep ... && { ...; exit 1; }` form "would abort the script right here on the good path too" under the `set -e` added in round 7. Measured directly (`for sh in /bin/dash /bin/sh /bin/bash; do $sh -c 'set -e; false && { echo bad; exit 1; }; echo REACHED'; done` → `REACHED`, `rc=0`, all three shells): `set -e` only turns a list's own nonzero status into the script's when that list is the *last* command run, and the `&&` form here is not the block's last line, so it would not have aborted. Corrected the parenthetical to state the true reason (an `&&` list's status becomes the script's exit status only when it is the last command; `if` says what is meant either way, so it is kept for clarity) rather than dropping it, per the brief.
- **A9 S3 / B9 suggestion 1** — `test_execute_step_sets_pipefail_shell` (`tests/test_notebook_ci_workflows.py`) rejected only a missing `shell: bash` and an appended `|| true`, not the rest of the same bypass family. Added three more plain assertions rejecting `; true`, `|| :` and `set +o pipefail` in the execute step's text, in the same linear style as the existing assertions (one clear reason each, not one regex for the family, matching the test's own stated reasoning for not generalising further). **Mutation-proven, each one, against the real workflow file, reverted immediately after confirming, `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml` left unchanged in the diff**:
  - Appending `; true` after the real pipeline (`sh "/srv/nbrun/run/$RECIPE" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/execute-notebook.log"; true`) → the new `; true` assertion fails; `git checkout --` the file → passes again.
  - Appending `|| :` after the same pipeline → the new `|| :` assertion fails; reverted → passes again.
  - Injecting `set +o pipefail` as the first line of the `run:` block → the new `set +o pipefail` assertion fails; reverted → passes again.
  - With no mutation present, the full test file passes (42 of 42, with the three new assertions in place).

### Suggestions declined (with reasons)

- **A9 S2** (`scope.yml`'s `--config-env=http.extraheader=...` applies the header to every HTTPS request `fetch` makes, not only `github.com`; narrowing it to `--config-env=http.https://github.com/.extraheader=...` is free) — filed as **issue #122** rather than taken here: `scope.yml` only runs as `pull_request_target`, which this pull request cannot exercise at all (no `Scope` row appears in its own checks, for the reason stated earlier in this description), so a change to it could not be verified on this branch. The brief also instructs not to change any workflow file this round.
- **A9 S4** (nothing pins the order of `require_pid_namespace_if_demanded()` and `kill_everyone_else_in_my_pid_namespace()` inside `execute()`) — cosmetic, as A9 itself says (the kill helper carries its own namespace gate, so swapping the two changes no behaviour); left for a later round.
- **A9 S5** (this head's own CI run sits a little above the "Run time and scaling" table's cited band) — the section's own n = 1 noise caveat already covers it, per A9's own conclusion; not a documentation error.
- **A9 S6** (agreement that the already-declined suggestions from earlier rounds are non-blocking, two now moot) — no action requested; A9 raised this only to confirm earlier declines still hold.
- **B9 suggestion 2** (pin that `$RUNNER_TEMP` itself, not only the three `_runner_file_commands` files, is unwritable to `nbrunner`) — a hardening of an existing proof, not a finding (B9 found nothing exploitable); left for a later round.
- **B9 suggestion 3** (`python tools/notebook_ci.py fixtures` in the documented block is repository-wide and aborts a single recipe's reproduction if a *different*, half-built recipe folder has no `fixtures/` yet; scope it to `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/NN-slug` instead) — left for a later round; not in the brief's must-fix list and does not affect CI, only the documented local reproduction's last line.
- **B9 suggestion 4** (note that pasting the `set -e` block into an interactive shell leaves `set -e` set afterward and can close the terminal on a later unrelated failed command; suggest `bash the-block.sh` or a `( … )` wrapper) — left for a later round; cosmetic to the reproduction instructions, not to the bug B9 filed as M1.

### Commands run and results (existing venvs, this head, Linux)

- `ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .`: 71 files already formatted.
- `pytest tests/test_notebook_ci_workflows.py tests/test_notebook_ci_sandbox.py -q` (`timeout 300`): **42 passed**.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: "Hygiene check passed: 96 file(s) scanned."
- Full suite, once, under the shared heavy-job slot, in the foreground: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 10 timeout 1500 python -m pytest -q` → **1369 passed, 3 skipped in 324.50s** (same count as round 7: no test function was added this round, only three new assertions inside the existing `test_execute_step_sets_pipefail_shell`).
- Mutations, each reverted immediately after confirming (see the tables above for exact output): the B9 M1 bug and fix reproduced end to end in a private scratch copy of `recipes/_template`; the three new pipefail-bypass assertions each mutation-proved against the real `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml`, which is unchanged in the final diff (`git diff --stat` shows only `docs/development.md` and `tests/test_notebook_ci_workflows.py`).
- `gh pr checks 108 --watch` (unpiped) after pushing `7858419`, and `gh pr view 108 --json statusCheckRollup` read directly afterward: see the check results below.
- Processes swept before and after the full run: `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep -E 'pytest|execute_notebook'` showed nothing of this task's own running, either time; the heavy-job lock (`/workspace/worktrees/_scratch/HEAVY.lock`) was released immediately afterward.

### Decisions this round makes

- `rm -rf` before `cp -R` was chosen over `cp -RT` for the documented one-recipe reproduction, specifically because this section's heading names two platforms (Git Bash on Windows, or Linux) and `rm -rf` then `cp -R` is the form guaranteed to behave the same on both; `-T` is listed as a GNU extension and its presence/behaviour on Git Bash's bundled `cp` is not something this round could verify on this machine.
- The `sudo` block's cleanup is `sudo rm -rf`, not a plain `rm -rf`, because the directory it is removing was `chown`-ed to `nbrunner_local` and `chmod 700`-ed by a *previous* run of the same block — your own user cannot remove it without `sudo`, which B9's own observation (the `sudo` variant "fails loudly" on a re-run) already implied.
- The three new pipefail-bypass assertions were added as three separate, plainly-worded `assert` statements rather than one regex matching the whole family (`(\|\||;|&&)\s*(true|:)\s*$` plus a separate check for `set +o pipefail`), matching this test's own existing style and its own stated reasoning for keeping the two original assertions separate rather than generalising.

### Still unfinished / carried forward

- `get_backend(fixtures=...)`'s shared-code half is still not implemented here; belongs to #65/#66, as before.
- `scope.yml`'s host-scoped token header (A9 S2) is filed as issue #122, to be taken once a branch can actually exercise `pull_request_target`.
- Everything else carried from rounds 1-7 is unchanged and still covered by its existing tests.

title: Foundation: reader documentation (getting started, offline and live, glossary)
body:
Closes #72

## What this adds

- `docs/getting-started.md`: install, pick a notebook (the template today; recipe 01 once its README row links a notebook), run offline, run a recipe's tests, scaffold a recipe, switch to live.
- `docs/offline-and-live.md`: the two modes, provenance, the run-mode header (all four forms), why synthetic metrics are pipeline checks, what "not measured live" means, the budget guard and the recorder (summarized from `docs/live.md`).
- `docs/glossary.md`: state, question, Choice, Noul, Score, criteria, probabilities, confidence (Choice and Score formulas), threshold, replay key, fixture, provenance, run mode, each linked to a README sources-table page (S01 to S04) or to the repository page that defines it.
- `README.md`: a `## Quick start` section (outside the generated regions), one nav link, and the two stale sentences (Data row, Claims row) reworded so they stay true once a recipe carries recorded fixtures.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` section 2: two bullets (the mode/model/date/N disclosure the template implements; what a live run over fixture inputs may claim).
- `docs/fixtures.md`: one sentence on the 63-level state versus the 64-level `replay_key`.
- `docs/merge-readiness.md` is deliberately untouched (PR #105 owns it); that item of the brief is dropped.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work.

## How it was verified

Fresh venv in the worktree (Python 3.14.3), then:

```
python -m venv .venv; source .venv/Scripts/activate; pip install -e ".[dev]"   # ok
python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/_template    # "fixtures valid (mode replay)", rc 0
pytest recipes/_template -q                                   # 11 passed
python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/_template            # "_template: executed notebook.ipynb offline", rc 0; git status clean afterwards
pip install jupyterlab; jupyter lab --version                 # 4.6.4
jupyter lab --no-browser notebook.ipynb (from recipes/_template)  # server started, serving that folder (stopped after 20 s)
pip install --dry-run -e ".[live]"                            # resolves, rc 0 (not installed; no key, no live call)
python tools/new_recipe.py 1 --recipes-dir <scratch>          # created 01-sentiment-classification/
python tools/new_recipe.py 36 --mode scripted --recipes-dir <scratch>   # created
python tools/new_recipe.py 1 --recipes-dir <scratch>          # refuses to overwrite, rc 1
git clone https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook.git     # ok
ruff check .                                                  # All checks passed
ruff format --check .                                         # 60 files already formatted
pytest                                                        # 1092 passed, 2 skipped, 1 warning
python tools/render_catalog.py --check                        # rc 0; running the renderer left README.md byte-identical
python tools/check_hygiene.py                                 # passed, 79 files
```

All relative links and anchors in the new and edited pages were checked by script (0 broken). The run-mode header text in `docs/offline-and-live.md` was produced by `run_header_text` (the recorded form uses placeholders for model and date).

`pre-commit run --all-files`: `ruff format --check` fails with `Failed to parse <file>.md` for every Markdown file passed by name, including files this change does not touch (same failure with my changes stashed), while `ruff format --check .` passes. This looks like the hook's file-by-name invocation versus ruff 0.14.0's Markdown handling; not changed here.

## Decisions

- Glossary links to S01 to S04 only (pages in the README sources table); terms that belong to the cookbook link to the repository page that defines them. No link to docs pages outside the table.
- `docs/offline-and-live.md` says recorded fixtures are a step in the process and that no recipe carries one yet; it does not cite the out-of-repository smoke recording. Update that sentence when the first recipe lands recorded fixtures.
- Getting-started names recipe 01 by its catalog slug and says to use it "once its row links to a notebook"; commands use `recipes/_template`, which always exists.
- The CONTRIBUTING bullet on live runs limits claims to "N fixture examples, model, date" and keeps the held-out rule for any sentence about Jev.

## Unfinished

Nothing in scope. The `docs/merge-readiness.md` sentence is left to whoever follows #105.

## Fix round 1

Head `c7e22330bf51270d8e4a436f8dffa93932641f81`.

1. The first commit held only the three new pages; the `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/fixtures.md` edits were left uncommitted. They are now committed. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists all six files (all mode 100644).
2. `docs/offline-and-live.md`: the recorder bullet now gives the `docs/live.md` instruction (pin `jev-1.13.0`; the recorder accepts an alias, so the person recording must not use one).
3. `docs/getting-started.md` step 3: only text outputs are expected to match; chart image bytes differ with the matplotlib version, so `git status` may show the notebook modified on another Python. Points to `docs/recipe-template.md` for the staleness rule (`docs/notebook-ci.md` does not exist on `main`, so it is not linked).
4. Suggestions: the README Claims row now says recorded inference, with model version, capture date and N; `NN` placeholder is explained in getting-started.

## Fix round 2

Head `f6eca8957f24044ef6fa01ef19f513fdfff39892`. The second CONTRIBUTING section 2 bullet now allows a number about Jev only from recorded fixtures (provenance `recorded`), on the `test` split, with model string, capture date and N; an unrecorded live run yields nothing reportable. The first bullet says the live header shows the requested model and the measured cell the returned one. Also: "a versioned model such as `jev-1.13.0`" in offline-and-live, and the PowerShell activate line in the README quick start. ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest (1092 passed, 2 skipped), render_catalog --check (no renderer diff), check_hygiene and the link check all pass locally.

title: Docs: reconcile manual immaterial-advance ruling with strict readiness evidence
body:
Closes #104

Only `docs/merge-readiness.md` changes against current `main`. No helper code, tests, workflows, CONTRIBUTING, orchestration or recipe rules.

## What the document says
1. **The helper is unchanged, always run, never skipped; its `NOT READY` receipt is recorded as it is.** Its CI evidence is always binding. Nothing presents the exception as a passed automatic gate.
2. **The standing ruling is quoted with its scope as written** (#80 ledger update 6, 6031026593: "for the adopted helper and future merges"; 6031278433; 6031723897: "merges performed by this run"). None of those states a foundation-only limit. This document limits its use to foundation pull requests under #104 criterion 3 and the unchanged recipe rules, and says so. It does not widen the scope.
3. **Material advances** (the PR's files, shared code it uses, workflows) need a signed integration and a fresh review. The required-check-set clause is marked as this document's addition.
4. **Requirements attached under #104 criterion 1:** exact main SHA plus helper receipt, delta evidence and effect on every required check; genuine same-head Opus acceptance of the delta (each reviewer where two are required); complete actual checks with no waiver and no old-main coverage; exact post-merge CI before the next merge. A further advance voids the ruling and the acceptance.
5. **`orchestration/PROMPT.md` has not been amended**; the document says so and points to #106.
6. **Recipe gates unchanged**, no exception.
7. **History**, recorded as claims where the source only claims:

title: Foundation: shared-code tidy-up before the first recipe
body:
Closes #102

## What this adds

Five small shared-code fixes carried over from the wave 0 reviews, each with a test that fails without the change:

1. Choice confidence is described as the top probability rescaled, `(p_max - 1/n)/(1 - 1/n)`, in `evaluation.top_probabilities` and `docs/evaluation.md`; Score confidence stays the distance-based spread.
2. `DecisionResult.from_dict`: a non-object `provenance` (or `usage`) raises `ValueError` naming the field. An absent `usage` still means "not reported"; a present non-object one (`[]`, `null`, a string) is rejected.
3. `replay_key` / canonical JSON: a state, or the content of a question, nested deeper than 64 levels raises `ValueError` ("state: nested deeper than 64 levels ...") instead of `RecursionError`. The check is iterative (also catches a self-referencing container) and counts like the fixture validator (outermost container is level 1).
4. `responses_file_name` (so `responses_path` and `load_responses`): a tag containing `.drift-` raises `ValueError`. The only other stray-producing tags (bad characters, leading punctuation, over 64 characters) were already refused by the id rule.
5. `macro_average` / `micro_average` errors for Noul/Score answers name the function called.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work, no recipe changes.

## How it was verified

Fresh venvs (default Python 3.14 and `py -3.10`, 3.10.11):

- `ruff check .`: All checks passed
- `ruff format --check .`: 39 files already formatted
- `pytest`: 737 passed, 1 skipped (3.14 and 3.10 alike)
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed, 58 files scanned
- Reverting `src/` and `docs/` (tests kept) fails 11 new or updated tests across all five items; all pass with the change.
- Golden keys: the existing pinned keys are untouched. Two new golden keys at exactly 64 levels (nested objects; alternating list/object) were computed on `main` before the change and pass unchanged.

## Decisions

- `MAX_DEPTH = 64` now lives in `jev_cookbook._canonical` and `jev_cookbook.fixtures` imports it, so the validator and `replay_key` cannot drift apart. `jev_cookbook.fixtures.MAX_DEPTH` is still importable.
- `plain_json(value, where, max_depth=64)` and `canonical_json(value, max_depth=64)` gained `max_depth` (`None` disables). `replay_key` limits the state and each question's `to_dict()` separately at 64, then hashes the wrapping payload with the check off, because the `{"v","state","questions"}` envelope adds levels that are not the caller's. No key for a valid request changes.
- New private helper `check_depth` in `_canonical` (iterative).
- One existing fixtures test helper (`state_set`) now falls back to a stand-in key when the deliberately over-deep state cannot be keyed any more; the assertions about the validator are unchanged.
- Existing test expectations for `macro_average` / `micro_average` messages were updated from `per_class_metrics` to their own names (that is item 5).

## Unfinished

Nothing. `main` has moved (#101) in files this branch does not touch; no merge was needed.



## Fix round 1

Review: https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/103#issuecomment-6030308686 (two must-change findings, both accepted). Merged `origin/main` (#101) first.

1. The 64-level limit is no longer the default of the shared helpers: `plain_json` and `canonical_json` default to `max_depth=None` (as on `main`); `replay_key` passes 64 explicitly. New test: a 64-level payload recorded in `ActionLog` and stored through `Transactor` reads back through `to_dicts()`.
2. Question content is checked per part: `instructions` and each `criteria` value (Score level, Choice description, Noul outcome) at 64 each, outermost container = level 1. Keys for three requests computed on `origin/main` and pinned (pass unchanged on this head):
   - `Noul(instructions=<64-level object>)`: `dc42af6c0cf1fa8c67cd32ef48e5098ef990196e61610683a0e247f601a73fe1`
   - `Score(criteria=["low", <63-level object>])`: `327b15c3a76ea64fd2f3ff9e0e90755c5600b33745c4e3763bbb79f3c822fbe5`
   - `Score(criteria=["low", <64-level object>])`: `5315763ac8431d0a89363604146176f0c65d297bd153423954eba9b373d02fe5`

   Content at 65 raises `ValueError` naming the question and part.
3. `docs/backends.md`: depth sentence corrected; `"usage": null` (any present non-object usage) is rejected while a missing key still means not reported; one sentence on the fixture off-by-one (a fixture state can be at most 63 levels of its own, `replay_key` accepts 64). The same sentence should later go into `docs/fixtures.md` (outside this PR's paths).

Proof by reverting `_canonical.py` and `backends.py` to the previous head (tests kept): 4 tests fail (three-key golden test, 65-level question test, no-default-limit test, ActionLog/Transactor round trip). On the merged head: `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean; `pytest` 756 passed, 1 skipped on 3.14 and 3.10.11; catalog `--check` exit 0; hygiene passed (59 files).

title: Foundation: notebook-style follow-ups (n_examples, figure display, None returns)
body:
Closes #100

## What this adds

Three small changes to `jev_cookbook.style`, raised by both Opus reviewers of the recipe template (#99):

1. `run_header` / `run_header_text` / `RunInfo` accept `n_examples` in every mode. In synthetic and scripted runs it is the size of the fixture sample the pipeline check ran on (second line); the third line, "Metrics in this run are checks that the pipeline works. They are not Jev results.", is unchanged. Recorded and live wording is unchanged.
2. A cell that ends with a chart helper's returned `Figure` renders an `image/png` in a plain `ipykernel` session, without `%matplotlib inline`.
3. `show_answer` and `run_header` return `None`. `format_answer` and `run_header_text` still return the text.

Changed paths: `src/jev_cookbook/style.py`, `docs/notebook-style.md`, `tests/test_style.py`, `tests/test_style_docs.py`, `tests/test_style_integration.py`, new `tests/test_style_notebook_display.py`. No dependency change (`ipykernel`, `nbclient`, `nbformat` are already core).

Exact synthetic header with `n_examples=12`:

```text
Recipe 07: Triage tickets
Mode: offline replay of synthetic fixtures, pipeline check on a fixture sample of 12 examples
Metrics in this run are checks that the pipeline works. They are not Jev results.
```

Scripted: second line `Mode: offline, scripted backend, pipeline check on a fixture sample of 12 examples`. A count of one reads `1 example`.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work, no recipe changes.

## Decisions

- **Where `n_examples` goes in offline headers.** On the second (mode) line, so the header stays three lines and the pinned notice sentence is byte-identical in every offline header. The same wording is used for scripted, because the issue speaks of a fixture sample for both.
- **Figure display mechanism.** `apply_style()` registers a PNG formatter for `matplotlib.figure.Figure` on IPython's display formatter when `IPython.get_ipython()` returns a shell; the formatter saves the figure through `FigureCanvasAgg` (no pyplot, no GUI backend). Chosen over importing pyplot or switching the backend at import time because importing the module must keep changing no global state and leaking no pyplot figures. Consequences: a notebook must call `apply_style()` (the docs say once near the top); outside IPython nothing is registered; IPython is imported only inside `apply_style()`, never at module import; registering twice replaces the earlier formatter; `%matplotlib inline` still works and is simply not needed. The `text/plain` repr is still sent alongside the PNG, as for any rich output.
- **`%matplotlib inline` in docs.** `docs/notebook-style.md` never contained the instruction (the template notebook and `docs/recipe-template.md` on #99 do), so the doc now states it is not needed. #99 can drop the line.
- **Return values.** `show_answer` and `run_header` return `None`. Nothing in `src`, `tests`, `docs`, `recipes`, `tools` assigns them on `main` (`grep -rn "= show_answer\|= run_header"`). The template notebook on `origin/foundation/recipe-template` assigns `header = run_header(...)` and `text = show_answer(...)`; that stays harmless (the names become `None`).
- **Existing tests changed.** Besides the removed `ValueError` assertions (offline header "refuses a sample size", in `test_style.py` and `test_style_integration.py`), three tests asserted the old returned text (`run_header`/`show_answer` printing and returning); they now assert `None` plus the printed text and the `*_text`/`format_*` return. Every recorded and live pinned text is untouched.

## How it was verified

All on the head commit, fresh venvs:

- `ruff check .`: All checks passed
- `ruff format --check .`: already formatted
- `pytest` on Python 3.14.3: 740 passed, 1 skipped
- `pytest` on `py -3.10` (3.10.11): 740 passed, 1 skipped
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed
- New kernel tests (`tests/test_style_notebook_display.py`) run a two-cell notebook through `nbclient` against a temporary kernelspec for the test interpreter: with `apply_style()` the second cell has one `execute_result` with `image/png`; without it only `text/plain` (negative control); a cell ending with `run_header(...)` has only a `stream` output. Unit tests cover no registration outside IPython and a single, idempotent registration.

## Unfinished

Nothing. The template notebook (#99) can now simplify its setup cell (drop `%matplotlib inline`, the `header =` and `text =` assignments, and pass `n_examples` offline); that is for #99, not here.

body:
Closes #68

## What this adds

- `recipes/_template/`: a complete, tiny recipe (route a support message: one `Choice` with `none`, one rule in Python). Files: `notebook.ipynb` (executed, outputs committed), `README.md`, `helpers.py`, `build_fixtures.py`, `fixtures/{inputs.jsonl,labels.jsonl,responses.json}` (22 synthetic examples: 10 validation, 10 test, 2 demo; answers deliberately imperfect), `tests/test_helpers.py`.
- `src/jev_cookbook/recipe.py`: `load_helpers(recipe_dir=None, *, reload=False)`, exported from `jev_cookbook`.
- `tools/new_recipe.py`: `python tools/new_recipe.py NN` scaffolds `recipes/NN-slug/` from the catalog with `TODO` placeholders; refuses to overwrite.
- `tools/execute_notebook.py <recipe-dir>`: runs the notebook offline in place (fresh kernel, cwd = recipe folder, `JEV_COOKBOOK_*` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` removed, no timings, minimal metadata, LF).
- `docs/recipe-template.md`; a paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Where things go") on the `helpers.py` convention; two stale sentences in `docs/backends.md` now point at `docs/fixtures.md`.
- Tests: `tests/test_template*.py`, `tests/test_new_recipe.py`.
- `tools/render_catalog.py` is unchanged: it only looks up folders named by catalog slugs, so `_template` is never counted (pinned by `tests/test_template_render.py`). `README.md`, `catalog/` and `pyproject.toml` are untouched.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work (branch `foundation/recipe-template`, not `recipe/<slug>`).

## How it was verified (fresh venvs, real output)

- `ruff check .`: All checks passed. `ruff format --check .`: 52 files already formatted (before the later test files; re-run clean at the head).
- `pytest`, default interpreter (3.14): 781 passed, 1 skipped (the SDK test, `live` extra absent). `py -3.10` fresh venv: 781 passed, 1 skipped.
- `python -m jev_cookbook.fixtures validate recipes/_template`: `fixtures valid (mode replay)`.
- `python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/_template` twice: byte-identical file. On Python 3.10 (matplotlib 3.10.9 versus 3.11.2) everything is identical except the `image/png` bytes.
- `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`: exit 0. `python tools/check_hygiene.py`: passed.

## Decisions (later builders live with these)

1. **`helpers.py` is loaded by path**, never imported: `load_helpers()` in the notebook, `load_helpers(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)` in tests. The module name is `recipe_<folder>_helpers`, cached per resolved path. It is in `sys.modules` only while its file executes (dataclasses need that) and removed afterwards, so nothing leaks between recipes in one pytest process. The file is compiled from source rather than imported, so a quick edit can never load stale bytecode and no `__pycache__` is written into recipes.
2. **The scaffold is a skeleton, not a copy of the template.** `SECTIONS` in `tools/new_recipe.py` is the single list of notebook headings; a test keeps it equal to the template's headings. Every place a builder must write contains `TODO`.
3. **`n_examples` is passed to `run_header` only for non-offline modes**, because `run_header` raises for a synthetic or scripted backend.
4. **Figures need `%matplotlib inline`** as the first line of the setup cell; the style figures are not registered with pyplot, so without it a returned figure prints as `<Figure ...>`.
5. **Mode-neutral cells**: a `check` suffix says "a pipeline check, not a Jev result" offline and is empty otherwise.
6. **Selection on validation**: the confidence threshold comes from `select_confidence_threshold(target_accuracy=1.0)` on validation and is frozen for test.
7. **The generator lives at the recipe root** (`build_fixtures.py`), outside `fixtures/`, and gets its keys from `helpers.py`.

## Unfinished or deliberately left

- `execute_notebook.py` has no network guard or staleness check (#69). Figure PNG bytes depend on the matplotlib and FreeType versions, so #69's staleness check must compare outputs other than image data or run in one pinned environment.
- `docs/backends.md`'s worked example still writes a scratch `fixtures.json` because `tests/test_backends.py` (outside my paths) asserts that file; the prose after it now points to `fixtures/responses.json` and `docs/fixtures.md`.
- The template's "Next steps" links to neighbouring recipe folders that do not exist until those recipes are published.

Closes #97

**Final head `b20c2ccebe8699edf0b789c19702ef42d8b272b4`** (signed). It is the signed merge of `main` `7d146924b7378ded93e05c841fdfb75684e138f0` (#103, all five checks green) into the previously reviewed code. The reviewed `863b206` code is unchanged: `git diff origin/main` lists only the same five files. **Every earlier review (`33fc11d`, `3cc35ef`, and the one in progress on `863b206`) is stale for this head. A fresh independent Opus review of this exact head is required before merge.** Nothing here is self-approved, and the supervisor alone merges.

Repairs the four defects from the retrospective audit (#74 comment 6028948068), B1-B4 and N1-N3 from the review of `33fc11d`, and R1-R2 from the review of `3cc35ef`. Files changed: `tools/check_hygiene.py`, `tests/test_hygiene.py`, `tests/test_precommit_hook.py` (new), `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `docs/development.md`. No fixture package file is changed (see criterion 6).

## Criteria
1. **Paths and usernames.** Notebook outputs and metadata flag `D:/work/...` (`windows-drive-path`), `pytest-of-<user>` (`username-temp-path`, any first letter), `/opt/{conda,mambaforge,miniforge,...}`, `/opt/homebrew`, `/Volumes/` (`local-install-path`) and `/private/var/folders/` (`local-temp-path`). A bare username cannot be told from a word, so the account running the check is flagged as a whole word in outputs and metadata (`local-username`, name never echoed). Generic names, names under 4 characters and a short list of ordinary words are excluded, so CI (`runner`) is unaffected and prose is not rejected. The exclusions and the false-positive trade-off are documented in `docs/development.md`. No existing rule was weakened.
2. **Markdown pre-commit.** The ruff-format hook matches `\.(py|pyi|ipynb|md)$`, which is what `ruff format --check .` formats. It does not use the `markdown` type, because ruff errors on an explicitly named `.markdown` or `.mdx` file. It does not include `.pyw`, which `ruff format .` ignores. Reproduced before the fix: a bad `.md` passed the hook but failed CI's command. After the fix the real `pre-commit run ruff-format` fails a bad `.md`, passes a formatted one and skips `.markdown`. This is tested with the real hook and, without pre-commit, with pattern tests. CI is unchanged.
3. **Malformed notebooks.** (R1) A cell with both `source` and `input` now has both scanned; `input` used to be skipped whenever `source` was present. A non-object cell, a bad worksheet, a non-list `cells`, a non-text `source`, or a bad `id`, `cell_type`, `execution_count` or `prompt_number` is a `malformed-notebook-node` finding with a location and the Python type. Its strings are still scanned. Only a known cell type is printed in a location. Both `cells` and nbformat 3 `worksheets` are read when both are present. A runtime-generated bearer key in each of these places exits 1 with masked, bounded output, checked through a real subprocess.
4. **Directory arguments.** A directory or a missing path exits 2 with a message and is never counted as scanned. A directory of bad notebooks now fails, and the same files named one by one exit 1. File and no-argument (`git ls-files`) modes are unchanged.
5. **Dictionary keys (new at this head).** Probing with runtime fake values showed that a secret used as a JSON key (a mime-type, metadata or cell key) was not scanned, and was printed unmasked in the location of any other finding in the same cell. The second case breaks the documented rule that findings never print the matched value. It is in scope for #71 and #97 criterion 3 (redacted output), so it is fixed, not documented away. Key names are scanned as strings. A key is shown in a location only when it is short, ordinary (`text/plain`) and trips no rule that applies there (secret, local path or account name); otherwise it is shown as `<key>` (R2: a path or account name used as a key used to be printed whole in another finding's location). Seven placements (output data, notebook metadata, cell key, top-level key, worksheet key, nested metadata, each with and without a second finding) and two key shapes are tested through a real subprocess.
6. **Fixture-scanner parity (#65).** `src/jev_cookbook/fixtures/_scan.py` copies only the secret rules, not the notebook-output path, account-name or layout rules, which have no meaning in fixture text. This branch did not change any secret rule (`git diff 5f75fdd..HEAD -- tools` touches only the path, username, notebook-structure, key-label and argument code), so `_scan.py` and `tests/test_fixtures.py` are unchanged. Parity is shown on the integrated tree, not assumed: the two existing parity tests (rule definitions and function source against `tools/check_hygiene.py`, and one sample per rule) pass on py3.10 and py3.14. Changing a secret rule (the `sk-` length, the entropy threshold) in `tools/check_hygiene.py` makes them fail. The notebook-only rules were deliberately not copied.
7. **Keyless, offline, synthetic.** No provider calls, keys or `.env`. Fake keys are generated at run time, and nothing key-like is committed.

## Evidence (fresh venvs outside the tree, Windows, ruff 0.16.10, merged tree at `b20c2cc`)
| | py3.10.11 (`.[dev]`) | py3.14.3 (`.[dev,live]`) |
|---|---|---|
| `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` | pass, 41 formatted | pass, 41 formatted |
| `pytest` | 904 passed, 1 skipped (SDK absent, as in CI) | 963 passed |
| `tests/test_fixtures.py` (includes the parity tests) | 186 passed | 186 passed |
| `check_hygiene.py` (60 files) | pass, about 0.7 s | pass |
| `render_catalog.py --check` | pass | pass |

- #103 changed `src/jev_cookbook/fixtures/__init__.py` but not `_scan.py`, and no secret rule in `tools/check_hygiene.py` changed. The parity tests still pass, and drifting the entropy threshold or the bearer length in `tools/check_hygiene.py` makes them fail.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all four hooks pass.
- The suite passes under `USER=USERNAME=LOGNAME` set to `hello`, `stdout` and `timot`.
- New tests (R1, R2 and the two test gaps) run real subprocesses with runtime-generated fake keys and check no full echo. R2 covers six path shapes (home, Windows, drive, macOS, pytest temp, conda) in three locations, plus the account name as a key. The gap tests cover a valid-format `id` holding a key, and `_shown`'s secret guard.
- **Mutation probes** of this round, each reverting one fix and failing a test: `input` unscanned, `input` malformed check, `_shown` ignoring path and account rules, key-name scan off, valid `id` unscanned, `_shown` secret guard off, long-run guard off, and key labels echoed in two places. Earlier rounds' B1-B3, dict-key and parity-drift probes were re-run in the previous head and are unchanged.
- Hosted checks on the final head are listed in the PR checks. `src/` and `tests/test_fixtures.py` are not changed by this PR.
- Linux and WSL were not run by this author. The Opus reviews ran them.

## Unresolved
- Fresh independent Opus review of the final head (pending), and the supervisor's merge decision.
- Known limits, documented: a secret split or encoded in keys, secrets inside binary payloads, and short low-entropy keys are not detected. Account-name matching is a local best effort, and CI never runs it.

title: Foundation: read-only merge readiness check for current-main ancestry and complete CI
body:
Closes #95

## What this adds

- `tools/check_merge_readiness.py`: a read-only `gh api` GET helper. For a pinned PR head it verifies the PR is open and mergeable, that current default-branch `main` is an ancestor of the head (API compare merge base), and that the five baseline checks plus any explicit `--require-check` inputs are `success` on current `main` and then on the head (CheckRun and StatusContext, all pages, fail-closed on missing, pending, cancelled, duplicate, conflicting, malformed or unreadable data). It refetches `main` and the head afterwards and fails if either moved. Bounded ASCII JSON receipt, exit 0/1/2/3, no secrets.
- `tests/test_merge_readiness.py`: offline tests with a fake `gh` and real child processes, including regressions for PR83 (cancelled main job) and PR92 (head behind main).
- `docs/merge-readiness.md`: usage before serial merge, expected-head pin, exact-merge-SHA post-merge verification commands, and an explicit statement that this is CI/current-main readiness only and does not replace the Opus review, acceptance, dependency, scope, signature and sole-merge-owner gates.

Only these three paths change. No workflow, policy, shared-package or dependency change. The helper never merges, reviews or mutates anything.

## Remediation of the Opus review (CHANGES-NEEDED on 2cd4fa3)

- B1: `run_gh` decodes strict UTF-8 itself; invalid bytes, non-JSON, no output or any unexpected exception give a bounded receipt and exit 3 without raw output. Real-child-process regression tests cover non-cp1252 UTF-8, malformed bytes and unexpected failures.
- S1-S6 addressed as described in the follow-up comment. Baseline names must be CheckRuns from `github-actions`; `--require-check` names may be any CheckRun or StatusContext.

## How it was verified

Fresh venvs with `pip install -e ".[dev]"`: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `pytest` (908 passed on Python 3.14 with `.[dev,live]`, and 849 passed with 1 skipped (SDK test) on Python 3.10 with `.[dev]`), `python tools/check_hygiene.py` and `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` pass locally. Commit signature verified Good. Branch contains current `main` 7d14692 (signed merge).

Limitations: the helper is tested offline; additional checks from later workflows must be passed with `--require-check`. Manual Opus review, acceptance, dependency, scope, signature and sole-original-supervisor merge gates remain; this PR is not merged or approved by its author.
