title: Foundation: evaluation toolkit
body:
Closes #66

## What this adds

`jev_cookbook.evaluation`, a single module (`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, one file because it is one flat namespace notebooks import from and has no internal layering), its tests (`tests/test_evaluation.py`, 110 tests) and a reference page (`docs/evaluation.md`). Plain numpy only. All metric groups in the issue scope are done: Choice, Noul, multi-label, Score and ranking, selective prediction, calibration, paired bootstrap, usage accounting. Nothing is unfinished except the real-class tests (see below).

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable: foundation work (recipe-only items skipped).

## Decisions (later builders live with these)

- **Empty input raises `ValueError`** in every public function (tested per function, plus a test that fails if a new public function lacks one). Unequal lengths, out-of-range probabilities and bad settings raise too.
- **Undefined quantities return NaN**, never 0.0, and each docstring says when (table in `docs/evaluation.md`). Class precision is NaN if never predicted, recall NaN if no support, F1 NaN only if the class is in neither gold nor predictions; kappa NaN if chance agreement is 1; nDCG NaN if no positive gain; recall at budget NaN if nothing relevant; selective accuracy NaN if nothing answered.
- **Macro averages cover present classes only** (at least one gold or predicted example); inside a present class, undefined precision or recall counts as 0.0. Unused labels never drag the mean.
- **Ties in rankings are resolved in expectation** (average gain over the tied positions; fractional credit in top-k), so results do not depend on input order. nDCG uses linear gain by default, `gain="exponential"` for `2^r - 1`.
- **Answers are duck typed** by attribute (`choice`, `score`, `noul`, `confidence`, `probabilities`); `ChoiceLike`/`ScoreLike`/`NoulLike` runtime Protocols document the shape. Nothing is imported from #63.
- **What the answer values hold** (from the TypeSafe docs): `noul` is the probability of yes, 0 to 1, and a Noul has no `confidence`. Choice `confidence` is `(p_max - 1/n) / (1 - 1/n)`, so it is not the top probability. Calibration therefore takes a probability argument; `top_probabilities(answers)` supplies the top probability from Choice/Score answers. Score `probabilities` are keyed by `int` level in the SDK type (string keys only on the wire JSON); level matching accepts both. Score `confidence` is a distance-based spread measure, `max(0, 1 - sum p_i |i - m| / MAD_unif)`, not the Choice rescaling. Score `score` is an expected level, so MAE uses it while exact agreement uses the modal level (`score_level`, ties to the lowest level).
- **Noul has no confidence, so `noul_confidence(p) = max(p, 1 - p)`** is a toolkit convention offered for selective prediction; it is not an API value.
- **Select on validation, report on test.** Selectors (`select_threshold`, `select_confidence_threshold`) return a plain float; evaluators (`evaluate_threshold`, `evaluate_selective`) take it. Candidate thresholds are distinct observed values; threshold ties go to the higher threshold in `select_threshold`, and to the lower (more coverage) in `select_confidence_threshold`. Infeasible constraints raise.
- **Bootstrap**: `seed` is a required keyword-only argument; `numpy.random.default_rng(seed)`; percentile interval; resampling done in fixed-size chunks (the chunk rule is part of the deterministic result).
- **Usage**: `sum_usage` accepts mappings (or attribute objects, or `None` blocks); missing counts are tallied in `requests_missing_*` rather than treated as 0.
- Reliability bins are equal-width `(lower, upper]` with 0 in the first bin; edges are rounded to 9 decimals first to avoid float noise (0.7 * 10).

## How it was verified

Local, in a fresh venv (Python 3.14 default; no CI on `main` yet):

```
$ ruff check .
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check .
11 files already formatted
$ pytest -q
115 passed (default Python 3.14 and Python 3.10.11)
$ python tools/render_catalog.py --check
(exit 0)
```

Every metric test compares to a value computed by hand with the arithmetic in a comment. Fix round 1 added tests for the two threshold tie-breaks, the bootstrap percentiles and count-weighted ECE; each was shown to fail under the reviewer's mutation (`>=` to `>`, `[-1]` to `[0]`, fixed `[0.25, 0.75]` quantiles, unweighted bin mean) and passes on the real code. Noul answers passed to selective-prediction functions now raise a `ValueError` naming `noul_confidence`.

## Unfinished / follow-ups

- Tests use stand-in classes; real-class tests to be added after #63 merges.
- Not run under CI yet.

## Fix round 2

Head `cace2a9d6dc6661f388b0e42073ca44614fbadc8`. Review findings and what changed:

1. **Score modal level unpinned.** Added `test_score_level_is_the_most_likely_level_not_the_rounded_expected_score` in `tests/test_evaluation_answers.py`: a real `ScoreAnswer.from_probabilities([0.5, 0.1, 0.4], ...)` (expected score 0.9, modal level 0) asserts `score_level == 0`, `exact_agreement([0], [a]) == 1.0`, `exact_agreement([1], [a]) == 0.0`, `mean_absolute_error([0], [a]) == 0.9`. Mutation `score_level` returns `int(round(answer.score))`: 5 failures, including the new test.
2. **Choice calibration could not fail.** `test_calibration_on_real_answers` now pins the reliability bins (counts `[0, 0, 4, 2, 0]`, bin means and observed rates) and ECE = 4/6 * 0.05 + 2/6 * 0.25 = 0.7/6, with the arithmetic in a comment. Mutations: `top_probabilities` returning `.confidence` fails it (plus three others); ECE as an unweighted bin mean fails it (and `test_ece_weights_bins_by_count`).
3. **Choice metrics silently scored Noul/Score answers as 0.0.** `_choice_value` now takes the calling function's name and raises `ValueError` ("`accuracy` compares Choice options; a Noul answer is a probability, so use evaluate_threshold or threshold_sweep ...", with the Score variant pointing at `score_level`/`exact_agreement`/`mean_absolute_error`). Applies to `accuracy`, `confusion_matrix`, `per_class_metrics`, `cohens_kappa`, and so to the macro and micro averages (their errors name `per_class_metrics`). New test `test_choice_metrics_reject_noul_and_score_answers_naming_the_function` covers Noul and Score on `accuracy` and `per_class_metrics`, plus kappa, confusion matrix and both averages.
4. **Docs tidy-ups.** Accounting now says `Usage` objects or mappings (docstring of `sum_usage` too); the Result types table lists all eight types (added `ClassificationCounts`, `ReliabilityBin`, `BootstrapResult`); added a pointer that metrics on synthetic fixtures are pipeline checks, labelled next to the number as `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires.

Commands (all pass): `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `pytest` (308 passed on 3.14 and on Python 3.10), `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`, `python tools/check_hygiene.py`. All five CI checks SUCCESS at this head.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Integration

- **Merged:** `origin/main` into `foundation/evaluation` (merge commit, no conflicts). This brings CI (Lint, Catalog, Tests py3.10, Tests py3.14, Hygiene), the hygiene scanner, the catalog policy docs and the merged backends (#63/#84).
- **Tests added:** `tests/test_evaluation_answers.py`, 8 tests that run the toolkit on the real `ChoiceAnswer`, `ScoreAnswer`, `NoulAnswer`, `Usage` and `DecisionResult` (built with `from_probabilities` and `Provenance.synthetic()`): Choice metrics, Noul threshold functions, Score functions (int keys, read-only `MappingProxyType`), selective prediction on `top_probabilities`, calibration, `sum_usage` with `None` token counts and on `DecisionResult.usage`, and the NaN convention. The stand-in tests are unchanged. Total 306 tests.
- **Changes to `evaluation.py`:** none. No incompatibility found: it recognises answers by attribute, reads mappings only, and already converts Score keys with `_level_key`.
- **Docs:** added a "Result types" section to `docs/evaluation.md` listing the plain-attribute fields of `ConfusionMatrix`, `ThresholdPoint`, `SelectiveCurve`, `SelectiveResult`, `UsageTotals` (these were already plain dataclass fields).
- **Commands (all pass):** `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `pytest` (306 passed on 3.14 and on `py -3.10`), `python tools/render_catalog.py --check`, `python tools/check_hygiene.py`; all five CI checks SUCCESS at the new head.

title: Foundation: CI baseline for lint, tests, and the README catalog check
body:
Closes #62

## What this adds

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: workflow `CI` on pull requests and pushes to `main`, with `permissions: contents: read`, `concurrency` that cancels superseded runs, pip caching, and third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs (version in a comment). No secrets, no key, no live API calls (jobs install packages from PyPI). Checkout uses `persist-credentials: false`.
- `tests/test_render_catalog.py`: 16 tests for `tools/render_catalog.py` against temporary project trees (every test, including the region tests, uses the `project` fixture, which monkeypatches ROOT to `tmp_path`; the real `README.md`, `catalog/`, and `recipes/` are never touched). Covers region replacement, published detection from `recipes/<slug>/notebook.ipynb`, and `--check` exit codes and messages.
- `docs/development.md`: a "Continuous integration" section listing the check names.
- No change to `tools/render_catalog.py` was needed.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable (foundation work); none of the recipe items apply.

- [ ] Changes are confined to `recipes/NN-slug/` (n/a)
- [ ] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (n/a)
- [ ] Live path is opt-in and uses the same question definitions (n/a)
- [ ] Every response fixture records its provenance; the notebook states which mode it ran in (n/a)
- [ ] No claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost without recorded live inference (n/a; none made)
- [ ] Fixtures are synthetic, include the hard cases, and carry gold labels (n/a)
- [ ] Python owns every side effect; actions are simulated (n/a)
- [ ] Evaluation against gold labels, with the baseline the issue names (n/a)
- [x] Every acceptance criterion on the issue is met (see below)

## Check names (for required checks later)

| Check name | Command |
| --- | --- |
| `Lint (ruff)` | `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` |
| `Catalog (README is current)` | `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` |
| `Tests (py3.10)` | `pytest` |
| `Tests (py3.14)` | `pytest` |

## How it was verified

Local, in a fresh venv (Python 3.14.3), plus a separate Python 3.10 venv for pytest:

```
ruff check .                         -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                -> 9 files already formatted
pytest                               -> 18 passed (2 existing + 16 new)
py3.10: pytest -q                    -> 18 passed
python tools/render_catalog.py --check -> exit 0
```

Tests can fail: I temporarily broke `render_catalog.py` and restored it each time with `git checkout`. `is_published` always True: 5 failures. `--check` returning 0 when stale: 3 failures. Removing the README write: 3 failures. Writing CRLF: `test_write_mode_rewrites_readme_and_reports` fails (it checks raw bytes). `render_levels` returning an empty string: `test_render_fills_every_region_and_keeps_prose` fails (it asserts levels rows and the Categories/Levels badge counts).

### Deliberately stale README (local only, nothing pushed)

I changed a word inside a generated region (`Classify a short` to `Classify a SHORT` in the recipes table), ran the check, then restored the file:

```
$ python tools/render_catalog.py --check
README.md is out of date. Run: python tools/render_catalog.py
exit code: 1
$ git checkout README.md
$ python tools/render_catalog.py --check
after restore exit code: 0
```

Editing prose outside the generated regions (the title line) does not fail the check, by design.

## Decisions

- **Three jobs, not one.** Lint, catalog, and tests report separately, so a failure names its cause and later required checks can be chosen per job. Catalog needs only the standard library, so that job installs nothing. Notebook execution (#69) should be added as new jobs, not folded into these.
- **Check names are the contract.** Job `name:` values above are what branch protection will reference. The test job name is derived from the matrix (`Tests (py<version>)`); changing the matrix versions changes the check names.
- **Two Python versions for tests: 3.10 (the package floor) and 3.14.** The suite takes about a second and the dependency install is cached, so the second job costs roughly a minute of Linux runner time per run. It is worth it because contributors develop on 3.14 here and the floor alone would not catch breakage there; 3.10 alone could pass code that fails on the interpreter people actually use. Lint and catalog run once, on 3.10, since their results do not depend on the interpreter. Intermediate versions (3.11 to 3.13) are not covered; revisit if a bug slips between them. When #69 adds notebook execution, which is the expensive part, it should probably run on one version only.
- **Lint installs `.[dev]`** so the ruff version comes from the single exact pin in `pyproject.toml`, not a second copy in the workflow.
- **Concurrency group** is per pull request number (or ref on push) and cancels in-progress runs; a push to `main` is never cancelled by a pull request run.
- **`pytest` testpaths include `recipes/`, which does not exist yet.** pytest tolerates this (18 collected, no error); no change made.
- **Pinned actions:** `actions/checkout` v7.0.1 (`3d3c42e5...`), `actions/setup-python` v7.0.0 (`5fda3b95...`), resolved from the tag refs via the GitHub API.
- **Tests load the tool by file path** (`importlib`), since `tools/` is not a package, and patch `ROOT` instead of changing the tool.

## Unfinished

- Making these checks required (branch protection) is a repository setting, not done here.
- CI results are in the checks section of this pull request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Fix round 1

Review findings addressed in `39f86b2c613a0a0bc786618014c134857ff452af`: the CRLF assertion now reads bytes; the levels rows and badge counts are asserted; the five region tests use the `project` fixture so no test touches the real `recipes/`; every checkout step sets `persist-credentials: false`; two wording fixes in `docs/development.md` and the workflow header (no more "offline"). Not done, by instruction: concurrency on `main`, cache key, lint installing only ruff, categories sort test, and the `paths` note for #69.

title: Foundation: project scaffolding and Python package skeleton
body:
Closes #61

## What this adds

- `pyproject.toml`: package `jev_cookbook` under `src/`, Python >= 3.10. Core deps: `numpy`, `matplotlib`, `nbclient`, `nbformat`, `ipykernel`. Extras: `live` (`typesafe-sdk`), `ml` (`scikit-learn`), `dev` (`ruff`, `pytest`).
- Ruff (pinned `ruff==0.16.10` in the `dev` extra) for lint and format (line length 100, py310, notebooks included, rules `E4,E7,E9,F,W,I,B,UP`, no ignores). Pytest with `--import-mode=importlib`.
- `src/jev_cookbook/__init__.py` (version only, no side effects), `tests/test_import.py` (imports the package in a subprocess that blocks `typesafe`/`typesafe_sdk`, records environment reads of `TYPESAFE*`/`JEV_*` and `socket`/`urllib` audit events, and fails on any).
- `docs/development.md`: install, lint, test commands and the dependency policy.

**Change outside the issue's stated scope:** `tools/render_catalog.py` was changed in its own commit (539e54c). `ruff check .` flagged B008 on it and `ruff format --check .` wanted a reformat. I stopped and asked; the orchestrator approved editing that file for two things only: `ruff format`, and a behavior-preserving rewrite of the one flagged line (`lambda m, body=fn(catalog): ...` became `lambda m, fn=fn: m.group(1) + fn(catalog) + "\n" + m.group(2)`). The rule set is unchanged and there are no ignores. Nothing else in the file changed.

**Testpaths:** pytest `testpaths = ["tests", "recipes"]`, so plain `pytest` also runs recipe-level tests (a missing `recipes/` is accepted). How a recipe's tests import its `helpers.py` is left to #68.

## Recipe checklist

Foundation work, so recipe-only items are not applicable.

- [ ] Changes are confined to `recipes/NN-slug/` (n/a: foundation work)
- [ ] Notebook runs top to bottom offline, with no key and no network (n/a: no notebook)
